title: Quantum Computation Model Based on Multi-Scale Topology
abstract: This paper presents a novel quantum computation model based on multi-scale topology, designed to enhance the efficiency and stability of quantum computations. Traditional approaches often rely on static models, limiting the flexibility required for complex quantum algorithms. This research introduces a dynamic model that decomposes the quantum computation process into multiple scales, leveraging topological structures to optimize the overall system. The model's core mechanism involves a systematic mapping and adjustment of these scales to achieve improved performance. We explore the potential benefits of this approach in terms of algorithm design and computational complexity. The key contribution lies in the integration of topology into the core design of the quantum computation, offering a more adaptable and potentially more efficient framework.

title: Decay versus dephasing in Rydberg analog optimization: exchange rate, mechanism, and schedule design
abstract: Code, random seeds, and stored outcome distributions accompanying the manuscript "Decay versus dephasing in Rydberg analog optimization: exchange rate, mechanism, and schedule design" by S. Kim and J. Jung. Includes the exact Lindblad and quantum-trajectory solvers, the perturbative damage-function routines, the full outcome distributions of the 20 production instances, all robustness-scan caches (system size N=6–24, geometry, collective dephasing, full-Hilbert-space audits), the schedule-optimization data, and the scripts that regenerate every figure. See README.md for a file map and reproduction instructions.

title: Robótica Educacional e o Engajamento dos Alunos no Processo Formativo em Matemática
authors: Rejane Waiandt Schuwartz de Carvalho Faria
abstract: This article aims to investigate the role of Educational Robotics in the mathematics learning process of students in the final years of elementary school. The methodological approach is qualitative in nature, and the data was collected at State School Raul de Leoni, a public school. The research subjects were students from a seventh-grade class. Data was gathered through field notes, photographs, videos, activity sheets, and a discussion circle. Data triangulation was conducted based on the four stages of Mathematical Investigations and the four key elements in the organization of Computational Thinking development. The analysis allowed us to infer that it is possible to establish connections between Robotics and Mathematical Investigations. We conclude that Robotics presents itself as a powerful tool for engaging students in the construction of knowledge, as the students demonstrated interest and active involvement in Robotics activities.

title: A temporal graph attention autoencoder framework quantifies geopolitical trade risk through the evolutionary embedding of international trade networks
abstract: The increasing complexity of global trade networks demands analytical tools capable of capturing higher-order relational structures and their co-evolution with geopolitical tensions. Building on the limitations of static graph embeddings such as DeepWalk and Node2Vec and on prior temporal models including EvolveGCN, DySAT and TGAT, we present a Temporal Graph Attention Autoencoder (TGAA) that integrates multi-head graph attention with Gated Recurrent Unit sequential modelling and reinforces the encoder with residual connections to mitigate over-smoothing on dense trade graphs. Using United Nations Comtrade data covering 178 countries from 2001 to 2023, the model is implemented in PyTorch 2.1 and torch_geometric 2.4 with all hyperparameters selected by grid search and cross-validation. Evolutionary features are distilled from the learned embeddings and synthesised into a three-tier Geopolitical Trade Risk Index (GTRI) whose indicator weights are derived through the entropy method rather than imposed a priori. Empirical results show that the TGAA model attains a link prediction AUC of 0.932, outperforms both static and contemporary dynamic graph baselines, and produces a GTRI that captures major geopolitical disruptions—including the 2014 Crimea crisis and the 2022 Russia–Ukraine conflict—while preserving robustness under sensitivity tests on β and λ. Augmented Toda–Yamamoto Granger tests, complemented by effective transfer entropy, confirm that the GTRI carries linear and nonlinear predictive content for the Caldara–Iacoviello GPR index across an expanded sample of twelve major economies. We interpret these findings as evidence that network-embedding-derived structural signals encode forward-looking information about geopolitical tensions that text-based indices alone cannot fully capture.

title: Not All Fallbacks Are Failures: Understanding and Recovering from Fallbacks in Mobile Voice Assistants
abstract: Robust understanding of user input is a core requirement for voice assistants deployed in real-world environments. In practice, these systems encounter heterogeneous fallback situations caused by noisy audio input, transcription errors, ambiguous requests, incomplete utterances, or unintended activations. Existing systems typically respond with generic fallback messages, which do not resolve the underlying interaction failure and can degrade user experience. We study fallback handling in a deployed smartwatch-based voice assistant for general health support in everyday environments. Our analysis is based on six months of real-world usage data from more than 500 users, yielding a dataset of 3,030 anonymized, naturally occurring fallback-triggering utterances. We contribute (1) an operational taxonomy and the annotated VoxFallbacks dataset of these interactions, (2) a comparative evaluation of different models within a classification pipeline under practical deployment constraints, and (3) practical lessons for designing robust and cost-efficient fallback mechanisms. Results show that lightweight embedding-based classifiers outperform larger generative models on most classification tasks while requiring substantially fewer computational resources.

title: 基于非线性量子纠缠的拓扑结构分析
abstract: This paper investigates the application of non-linear quantum entanglement to improve the efficiency and accuracy of topological structure analysis. Traditional methods often struggle with complex systems, while our framework offers a fundamentally new approach leveraging the unique properties of entangled quantum states to enhance analysis. We explore a novel methodology utilizing entangled qubit states to uncover subtle topological features within data sets, ultimately providing a more robust and insightful tool for modeling complex systems. The core claim centers on the potential to significantly accelerate and refine topological structure analysis through the integration of quantum entanglement. This work presents a theoretical framework and preliminary experimental demonstrations focusing on the analysis of graph networks, demonstrating promising results in identifying critical topological structures. The paper concludes with a discussion of future research directions and the potential impact of this approach on various fields.

title: Probabilistic Logic Graph Dynamic Evolution Model
abstract: This paper proposes a novel dynamic evolution model for probabilistic logic graphs (PLGs). Traditional PLGs are often static representations of knowledge, limiting their ability to accurately reflect the inherent uncertainty and evolving nature of real-world systems. The core of this model lies in the application of dynamic evolutionary algorithms – specifically, a genetic algorithm – to iteratively refine both the structural elements (nodes and edges) and the probabilistic weights associated with these elements within the PLG. The objective is to minimize prediction errors or maximize decision-making outcomes by allowing the PLG to adapt to changing data and relationships. This research addresses the limitations of static PLGs by introducing a mechanism for continuous learning and adaptation, ultimately leading to more robust and accurate representations of complex, uncertain environments. The key contribution is a formalized framework for this dynamic evolution process, incorporating mechanisms for mutation, crossover, and selection, all designed to optimize the PLG's representation of probabilistic dependencies. This work lays the groundwork for applying PLGs in dynamic scenarios such as risk assessment, expert systems, and adaptive control systems.

title: Quantum Hidden Matrix Adaptive Computation
abstract: Quantum Hidden Matrix (QHM) theory presents a paradigm shift in quantum computation, offering the potential for highly efficient algorithms and enhanced error correction. This paper introduces an adaptive computation framework predicated on QHM principles, aiming to accelerate the calculation and prediction of quantum system states and facilitate quantum error correction. We detail the core mechanism, leveraging the inherent adaptability of QHM matrices to achieve significant computational speedups and improved error resilience. The paper outlines the fundamental concepts, the proposed framework's architecture, and the expected benefits of this approach. The research emphasizes the potential for transformative advancements across various quantum computing applications.

title: String Geometry Optimization
abstract: String geometry, a novel mathematical framework, offers a promising approach to complex system optimization. This paper investigates the application of string geometry to address challenging optimization problems, focusing on neural network architecture design and model parameter tuning. We propose a novel non-linear optimization algorithm leveraging the inherent properties of string geometry to identify and refine optimal parameter configurations. The core mechanism involves constructing and manipulating string structures to represent the optimization landscape, enabling the discovery of subtle, non-intuitive solutions that traditional optimization methods often miss. This research explores the potential of string geometry to enhance the efficiency and robustness of optimization processes, providing a potentially transformative tool for engineering and scientific modeling. The paper details the algorithm's structure, highlights its key advantages, and presents preliminary results demonstrating its efficacy in a specific optimization scenario.

title: Non-Euclidean Dimensionality Reduction via Adaptive Clustering
abstract: This paper explores a novel dimensionality reduction technique centered on adaptive clustering. Traditional methods often struggle with high-dimensional data, particularly when dealing with complex, non-Euclidean patterns. We propose a system that leverages a 'Clustering Metric' to guide the clustering process, effectively identifying and emphasizing these patterns. The core mechanism involves dynamically adjusting the clustering parameters based on the observed data distribution, resulting in more robust and interpretable representations compared to existing methods. The algorithm is designed to uncover hidden structure within high-dimensional data, potentially leading to more effective feature extraction and improved model performance. This research addresses a key challenge in data science – effectively dealing with high dimensionality – by introducing a framework for adaptive pattern recognition.

title: Dynamic Geometry Topology for Quantum State Generation
abstract: The development of robust quantum computation hinges on the ability to generate complex quantum states. Traditional approaches often rely on static qubit representations, limiting the potential for intricate and controllable quantum phenomena. This paper explores the application of dynamic geometry topology as a novel approach to quantum state generation, proposing a specialized algorithm that dynamically adjusts quantum states, enabling precise control and the generation of complex quantum states. We detail the core mechanism, outlining the design of the algorithm and its impact on state generation. The paper presents a comprehensive discussion of the theoretical underpinnings, preliminary experimental results demonstrating the algorithm's capabilities, and future research directions.

title: Bayesian Neural Networks for Deep Reinforcement Learning
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to reinforcement learning (RL) by integrating Bayesian Neural Networks (BNNs) with Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL). Traditional DRL methods often struggle with uncertainty quantification and robustness, particularly in environments with noisy or partially observable states. This research proposes a framework where a Bayesian Neural Network is employed to model the environment's state, providing a probabilistic representation alongside the deterministic output of a DRL agent. The agent then learns a policy based on this probabilistic representation, enabling it to make decisions while accounting for uncertainty. We demonstrate that this integration enhances the agent's robustness, generalization capabilities, and ability to perform accurate probabilistic inference. The core claim of this work is to build an intelligent agent capable of both probabilistic reasoning and decision-making. The key mechanism involves using a Bayesian Neural Network to model the environment's state and training a DRL agent's policy with this probabilistic representation. This approach addresses the limitations of standard DRL by explicitly handling uncertainty, leading to a more reliable and adaptable learning system.

title: Quantum Simulation of Non-Linear Material Dynamics
abstract: Quantum simulation offers unprecedented opportunities to understand and manipulate complex material systems, overcoming the inherent limitations of classical approaches. This paper explores the implementation of a quantum simulation algorithm, leveraging a variational quantum eigensolver (VQE) approach and a novel quantum error correction scheme, to simulate the non-linear dynamics of complex material systems. We detail the theoretical framework, algorithm implementation, and preliminary results demonstrating improved accuracy and efficiency compared to classical simulations. The core claim is that this quantum approach will surpass classical simulations in handling intricate material systems, particularly those exhibiting non-linear dynamics.

title: Quantum Simulation of Complex Material Behavior
abstract: Quantum simulation of complex material behavior represents a significant advancement in materials science, offering the potential to understand and predict emergent phenomena not achievable through traditional classical methods. This paper investigates a novel quantum simulation approach leveraging a hybrid quantum-classical framework to model the correlated dynamics of multiple interacting particles, focusing on a specifically designed representation of the quantum entanglement landscape. We propose a method that surpasses existing techniques by addressing the inherent challenges of simulating complex systems, particularly those exhibiting emergent behavior. The core claim is that this method will provide a more accurate and insightful understanding of material properties, opening avenues for designing novel materials with tailored functionalities.

title: 基于自适应的量子算法优化
abstract: Quantum algorithms, with their inherent complexity and sensitivity to initial conditions, pose significant challenges for optimization. Traditional optimization methods often struggle to effectively utilize the quantum properties of algorithms, limiting their potential for speed and accuracy. This paper proposes a novel approach to quantum algorithm optimization based on adaptive parameter adjustment. We introduce a system of quantum algorithms that dynamically adjusts parameters based on the algorithm's state, allowing the system to self-optimize and improve performance. The core mechanism of this approach leverages quantum properties to continually refine the algorithm's trajectory, leading to enhanced efficiency and accuracy. We present a preliminary demonstration of this method on a specific benchmark problem, showcasing its ability to outperform traditional optimization techniques. This work addresses a critical gap in the field of quantum algorithm optimization and offers a promising pathway toward more effective utilization of quantum resources.

title: Neuro-Symbolic Reasoning with Bayesian Latent Variables
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to neuro-symbolic reasoning that addresses the limitations of existing methods by incorporating Bayesian latent variables. The core claim is that current neuro-symbolic systems frequently lack sufficient integration and interpretability. Our proposed mechanism utilizes Bayesian latent variables within a neuro-symbolic architecture to enable neural networks to learn probabilistic relationships and generate evidence supporting symbolic inferences. This tight integration leverages Bayesian inference, resulting in a more robust and interpretable reasoning system. We demonstrate the potential of this framework through a theoretical analysis and outline a system architecture, highlighting the key components and their interactions. The paper focuses on the theoretical foundations and design considerations, paving the way for future empirical investigations and system implementations. The central contribution lies in the systematic application of Bayesian principles to bridge the gap between neural and symbolic representations, ultimately enhancing reasoning performance and interpretability.

title: Adaptive Entanglement Metric Calibration (AEMC)
abstract: This paper introduces Adaptive Entanglement Metric Calibration (AEMC), a novel method for calibrating entanglement metrics across a dynamic range of systems. Traditional entanglement analysis often utilizes static metrics, limiting its ability to accurately characterize complex systems. AEMC addresses this limitation through a continuous, dynamic metric adjustment algorithm, incorporating a "metric calibration" process and a "dynamic weighting" mechanism. The paper details the implementation of this algorithm and explores its potential for significantly enhancing the accuracy and robustness of entanglement-based analysis. We provide a comprehensive explanation of the core mechanism, outlining the iterative adjustment process and the resulting improvements in system characterization. The paper concludes with a discussion of the theoretical and algorithmic advancements required for realizing the full potential of AEMC.

title: 自适应的混沌域的非线性优化算法
abstract: This paper introduces a novel non-linear optimization algorithm based on the concept of a dynamically adjusted chaos domain. The core of this algorithm lies in leveraging the inherent self-organizing properties of chaos domains to dynamically adjust the parameters governing the optimization process. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach through a series of simulations, showcasing its ability to achieve high efficiency and precision compared to traditional optimization methods. The algorithm's adaptability and potential for automated parameter tuning make it a promising advancement in the field of optimization.

title: Probability Matrix Dynamics and Quantum Computing Integration
abstract: This paper explores the integration of probabilistic matrix modeling with quantum computing to facilitate real-time system state modeling and prediction. Traditional probabilistic matrix approaches often struggle with dynamic environments, necessitating a novel dynamic adjustment mechanism. We introduce a framework that leverages quantum computing's inherent probabilistic properties to dynamically adjust matrix weights, enabling more accurate simulations and precise predictions. This work addresses the limitations of static parameter-based modeling by integrating quantum computation for enhanced system behavior representation. The core mechanism centers on adjusting probabilities based on quantum fluctuations, ultimately improving the responsiveness and accuracy of the modeling process. This represents a significant step towards adaptive system representation, particularly within complex, dynamic systems.

title: 基于自适应的量子纠错算法的优化
abstract: Quantum information processing relies heavily on the robustness of quantum states. Quantum error correction is a critical component of this process, allowing us to detect and mitigate errors introduced by environmental noise. Traditional quantum error correction techniques often require significant manual tuning of parameters, a process that can be time-consuming and prone to human error. This paper proposes a novel optimization approach for quantum error correction, utilizing an adaptive quantum error correction algorithm. The core mechanism involves dynamically adjusting key parameters of the error correction process to enhance the fidelity of quantum states. This design offers a significant improvement over existing approaches through automated parameter optimization, resulting in increased error correction efficiency. The research explores the potential of this approach in practical quantum computing scenarios, demonstrating its effectiveness in mitigating errors during a simulated quantum system. We present a comprehensive analysis of the algorithm's performance, highlighting its advantages and limitations.

abstract: This paper investigates the application of quantum computing to the optimization of matrix transformations, specifically focusing on dynamic geometric transformations. We propose a novel algorithm leveraging quantum entanglement and topological transformations to dynamically adjust matrix transformations, offering a significant improvement over static matrix manipulation methods. The core mechanism centers on exploiting quantum properties to enhance numerical computation efficiency. This approach aims to address limitations in current numerical methods, particularly when dealing with complex, evolving geometric structures. The proposed method provides a foundation for advanced optimization techniques in various scientific and engineering domains.

title: The Green Shorttail Sunbird Inspired Metaheuristic Optimization Algorithm (GSSMOA)
abstract: This paper introduces the Green Shorttail Sunbird Inspired Metaheuristic Optimization Algorithm (GSSMOA), a novel optimization technique inspired by the foraging behavior of the Green Shorttail Sunbird (Aethopyris domestiens). The sunbird's remarkable ability to efficiently locate nectar sources in complex environments, utilizing a combination of exploratory and exploitative movements, serves as the core principle for GSSMOA. The algorithm leverages a dynamic patch selection strategy, mimicking the sunbird's preference for promising areas, and incorporates a 'hovering' mechanism to refine solutions around local optima. Mathematical formulations are presented to detail the algorithm's key components, including patch selection probability, movement strategies, and solution refinement. The aim is to provide a robust and adaptable metaheuristic approach suitable for a wide range of optimization problems.

title: ## Alai Molevole: A Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by the Foraging Behavior of the African Mole Rat
abstract: This paper presents Alai Molevole, a novel metaheuristic optimization algorithm inspired by the foraging strategies of the African mole rat ( *Microtus brachyurus* ). Mole rats are renowned for their efficient and adaptive subterranean navigation, utilizing a unique "spiral-and-return" foraging pattern. Alai Molevole leverages this behavior to create a stochastic search method that balances exploration and exploitation. The algorithm employs a spiral trajectory representation of the search space, dynamically adjusting the spiral radius based on the fitness landscape gradient. A key component is the 'memory' mechanism, mimicking the mole rat's reliance on olfactory cues, which guides the spiral's progression towards promising regions. We demonstrate the effectiveness of Alai Molevole through simulations on benchmark optimization problems, showing competitive performance compared to established metaheuristic algorithms. The algorithm's adaptability and potential for real-world applications are discussed.

title: 弦-素耦合的自适应调整与多维几何优化
abstract: 弦-素耦合理论为理解物理系统的动态行为提供了深刻的框架,其在优化领域具有潜在的应用价值。本研究旨在利用弦-素耦合的自适应调整机制,在多维几何优化问题中动态调整几何参数,从而提高优化结果的精度和效率。我们提出了一种基于弦-素耦合的自适应调整算法,该算法能够根据优化问题的特性自动调整几何参数,实现更优化的结果。本论文首先阐述了弦-素耦合理论的基本概念,然后详细介绍了我们的自适应调整算法的设计和实现,并对结果进行了分析和验证。我们认为,本研究的成果具有重要的理论意义和实际应用价值,尤其是在优化复杂几何形状和性能问题时。

title: Acrobatic Cavy: A Novel Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by the Agility of Cavies
abstract: This paper proposes a novel metaheuristic algorithm, Acrobatic Cavy (AC), inspired by the remarkable agility and spatial reasoning abilities of cavies (guinea pigs). AC leverages the inherent characteristics of a cavy's movement patterns – particularly their ability to navigate complex terrains and adjust their trajectory dynamically – to develop a new optimization strategy. The algorithm utilizes a novel representation of the search space based on a multi-dimensional vector representing a cavy's potential path. A core component is a 'momentum' term, mimicking the cavy's ability to maintain and adjust its velocity during movement, coupled with a 'reflex' mechanism that allows for rapid directional changes. We demonstrate the efficacy of AC through simulations across a range of benchmark optimization problems, showcasing its ability to outperform established metaheuristic algorithms like Genetic Algorithms (GA) and Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) in terms of convergence speed and solution quality. The algorithm's adaptability and dynamic adjustment capabilities are key to its performance. Finally, we discuss the potential extensions and future research directions for AC, including incorporating environmental constraints and adaptive parameter tuning.

title: 基于量子纠缠的动态概率分布模型
abstract: This paper introduces a novel dynamic probability distribution model based on quantum entanglement, aiming to precisely model and simulate complex probability distributions. Traditional probabilistic models often rely on handcrafted parameters, limiting their ability to capture intricate behaviors. This research leverages quantum entanglement to dynamically adjust probability distribution parameters, offering a fundamentally new approach to modeling and simulation. The model's core mechanism centers around the manipulation of entangled states to influence the evolution of probability distributions. We present a theoretical framework and initial implementation demonstrating the model's efficacy in simulating scenarios exhibiting complex probabilistic patterns. The proposed framework exhibits significant advantages in accuracy and adaptability compared to existing approaches.

title: Quantum Entanglement Simulation via Dynamic Topology Transformation
abstract: Quantum entanglement is a fundamental phenomenon with profound implications for quantum computing and communication. However, accurately simulating entangled states remains a significant challenge due to their inherent complexity and sensitivity to environmental noise. This paper introduces a novel quantum entanglement simulation method based on dynamic topology transformation, aiming to overcome the limitations of static simulation approaches. We propose a system that iteratively modifies the topology of the entangled state, effectively mimicking the evolution of entangled states. This dynamic process allows for the generation of complex, multi-dimensional entangled states, offering a pathway towards more realistic and controllable quantum systems. The core mechanism leverages a continuous, iterative adjustment of the entangled state's geometry, providing a robust and adaptable simulation framework. We present preliminary results demonstrating the effectiveness of this method in generating entangled states with intricate topologies.

The paper details the design of this framework, outlines the theoretical underpinnings, and presents preliminary experimental results demonstrating its effectiveness.

title: E-Commerce Bench: Evaluating LLM Agents on Long-Horizon Autonomous Business Operation
abstract: Long-horizon agentic tasks go beyond chaining short tasks over more interaction turns. Their evolving dynamic environments and long-range dependencies require Large Language Models (LLMs) to continually explore, learn from experience, and adapt their policies over thousands of steps. We introduce E-Commerce Bench, the first open-source benchmark that integrates multi-round counterpart negotiation and dynamic events into a year-long business operation. Over a 365-day year, an LLM agent concurrently runs multiple online stores, researching the market, negotiating with suppliers to source inventory, optimizing sales strategies, fulfilling orders, handling returns, and managing cash flow to maximize its end-of-year total assets. To construct a realistic merchant-side operating environment, the product and supplier data are derived from a real e-commerce platform, while a year-long calendar of promotions, natural disasters, and supply-chain shocks continually reshapes demand. For reproducibility, both sides of the market are deterministic: customer purchases and returns follow a fixed demand model, while a negotiation kernel determines supplier pricing, concessions, and decisions, with an LLM used only to verbalize them. We evaluate 18 frontier models across seven dimensions, including year-end assets, and find that no single model dominates. GPT-5.6 Sol earns the most, growing the 100,000 opening stake into 1,431,425, yet it ranks 16th of 18 on fraud avoidance and trails Fable5 in operational efficiency. Among open-weight models, Qwen3.8-Max-Preview leads with 416,252, 38% above GLM 5.2 (high), and achieves the strongest learning over the horizon, progressively bargaining down prices across repeated orders. Our code is available at https://github.com/QwenLM/E-CommerceBench.

title: Applications of Artificial Intelligence in Improving the Efficiency of Administrative Decision-Making within Iraqi Provincial Sports Clubs
abstract: ABSTRACT The research aims to identify the role of artificial intelligence in improving the quality of administrative decisions. In order to achieve this goal, the dimensions of artificial intelligence (appropriate training and development, effectiveness) were adopted, as well as the dimensions of the administrative decision: the time dimension, the quality of the decision, and the acceptance of the decision. The importance of the research stems from the importance of the administrative decision for organizations and the major role it plays in providing solutions to problems and choosing alternatives that serve the organization's goals. Artificial intelligence is also one of the most important factors that lead to the creation of knowledge and ideas that contribute to improving the decision-making process. The study population consists of a sample of managers in Asia Cell Telecommunications Company, consisting of fifty managers. By adopting the descriptive analytical method, the statistical results of the research confirmed the validity of the research hypothesis, which is that there is an impact of artificial intelligence on improving the quality of administrative decisions in Iraqi provincial sports clubs, as the clubs rely on the application of an artificial intelligence-based program, through the application of artificial intelligence programs by administrative leaders using a computer network that connects the main center with the branches. Accordingly, it was recommended to focus more on attracting and selecting candidates for employment who have scientific and practical experience in the field of artificial intelligence, as well as training employees on the efficiency of using artificial intelligence programs and their applications.

title: Structure without semantics: derived cohort, analysis code and results ledger
abstract: Code, derived cohort and complete results ledger for a study testing whether the semantic content of feature groups drives performance in group-aware tabular transformers. Across 24 randomly permuted partitions on two independent cross-validation folds, semantically meaningful feature groups perform no better than meaningless ones of the same sizes, and no group count from one to sixteen separates from another. A companion analysis quantifies how supplying a model with the variables that define its own outcome inflates apparent accuracy from 0.832 to 0.996 and inverts the ranking of models, so the weakest appears strongest. Source data are public files from the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (cycles 2011-2012 through 2017-2018) and require no application or credentialling. The derived analysis cohort (19,978 adults, 40 columns) rebuilds byte-identically from them using the deposited construction script. The results ledger deliberately retains superseded values alongside their replacements. Four findings in this study reversed under scrutiny, and the reversals can be audited from the files here rather than taken on the manuscript's word. An independent re-execution record is included: the cohort rebuilds to an identical checksum from re-downloaded source files, and the permutation test and factorial reproduce bit-identically across 16 and 20 runs respectively. Contents: cohort construction, the model implementation with its ordinal Dirichlet evidential objective, every experimental runner with its stored results, figure scripts and outputs, a complete manifest, per-file checksums, and a pinned environment specification.

title: Linear Matrix Systems and Quantum Algorithms
abstract: Linear matrix systems represent a fundamental class of problems in mathematics, physics, and engineering, and their efficient solution is crucial for various applications. Traditional methods often rely on computationally intensive algorithms, limiting scalability. This paper explores the potential of leveraging the inherent non-linear properties of linear matrices to design novel quantum algorithms for solving linear systems. We propose a quantum algorithm predicated on the principle that by mapping a linear system into a non-linear representation via a specific matrix transformation, we can achieve speedups that surpass classical approaches. The core mechanism involves constructing a quantum circuit that systematically explores this non-linear space, leveraging quantum phenomena like superposition and entanglement to enhance the search process. The paper details the design of a quantum algorithm for solving linear systems, emphasizing the benefits of this approach and its potential to unlock new possibilities in quantum computation.

title: Adaptive Kernel Methods for Non-Stationary Data Streams
abstract: This paper introduces an adaptive kernel method designed specifically for handling non-stationary data streams. Traditional kernel methods often struggle when the underlying data distribution changes over time, leading to diminished performance and inaccurate predictions. Our approach addresses this limitation by continuously learning and updating the kernel parameters based on the incoming data. This dynamic adjustment allows the method to adapt to evolving environments, maintaining accuracy even as the data stream shifts. The core claim centers on the sensitivity of traditional kernel methods to distribution changes. The proposed mechanism leverages a streaming learning framework to build a kernel function that optimizes for the current data state. We explore the theoretical underpinnings of this adaptive approach, focusing on the convergence properties of the learning algorithm and the impact of the kernel parameter updates on prediction accuracy. We present a mathematical formulation of the adaptive kernel method, outlining the key equations and notations. The method's effectiveness is demonstrated through a conceptual analysis and theoretical justification, highlighting its potential for real-world applications where data streams are inherently non-stationary.

title: Black-fronted Duiker Inspired Metaheuristic Algorithm (BDI-MHA)
abstract: This paper proposes a novel metaheuristic algorithm, the Black-fronted Duiker Inspired Metaheuristic Algorithm (BDI-MHA), inspired by the foraging behavior of the black-fronted duiker ( *Sylvicapra frontalis*). The algorithm leverages the duiker's adaptive movement strategy – a combination of exploratory and exploitative phases – to optimize complex problems. BDI-MHA incorporates a dynamic exploration rate, influenced by the duiker's response to environmental changes, and a memory-based exploitation phase mimicking the animal's preference for previously successful food sources. The algorithm's core features include a novel position update mechanism based on a weighted average of the best solution and a randomly generated solution, along with an adaptive inertia weight scheme. Theoretical analysis demonstrates the algorithm's convergence properties and its potential for improved performance compared to traditional metaheuristic methods. The algorithm is tested on several benchmark optimization problems, including the Rosenbrock function, the Rastrigin function, and the Sphere function, showcasing its effectiveness and efficiency. The results indicate that BDI-MHA consistently outperforms other common metaheuristic algorithms in terms of solution quality and convergence speed. Future research will focus on parameter tuning and further exploration of the algorithm's adaptability to different problem domains.

title: Spectral-Based Computation Security
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to computation security leveraging the principles of spectral theory. Traditional computational security relies heavily on cryptographic methods, which are increasingly vulnerable to advancements in computing power and algorithmic attacks. We propose a framework that abstracts computation into a spectral graph, allowing us to analyze and defend against malicious activities—specifically, data manipulation (tampering), eavesdropping, and deception—using spectral analysis techniques. The core idea is to represent the computational process as a graph where nodes represent operations and edges represent data flows. Analyzing the spectrum of this graph provides a robust method for identifying anomalies and detecting attacks. This work demonstrates a fundamentally new approach to security, shifting the focus from purely cryptographic solutions to a more holistic, data-driven perspective informed by spectral analysis. The proposed method offers a potentially more resilient defense against evolving threats in the computational domain.

title: Title: Topological Quantum Entanglement (TQE)
abstract: This paper investigates Topological Quantum Entanglement (TQE), a novel approach to quantum computation centered around the manipulation of topological quantum states. We propose a robust algorithm, the "Topology Map" method, designed to generate and manipulate complex, multi-layered quantum states with inherent resilience to noise. The core claim is that this methodology, leveraging the principles of topological quantum mechanics, will significantly enhance quantum computation by reducing error rates and enabling the creation of more stable and powerful quantum systems. We detail the algorithm's mechanics, the underlying topological properties leveraged, and the potential benefits of this approach compared to existing quantum technologies. The work explores the challenges and opportunities presented by utilizing topology to address inherent vulnerabilities in current quantum states.

title: The Transparent Jellyfish-Inspired Adaptive Exploration and Exploitation Algorithm (TJEAE)
abstract: This paper introduces the Transparent Jellyfish-Inspired Adaptive Exploration and Exploitation Algorithm (TJEAE), a novel metaheuristic optimization algorithm inspired by the unique swimming behavior of transparent jellyfish. These organisms utilize a complex, undulating motion to efficiently navigate and capture prey, exhibiting both exploration and exploitation capabilities simultaneously. TJEAE leverages this biological insight to develop a dynamic algorithm that adjusts its exploration-exploitation balance based on the local environment and the convergence rate of the search process. The core of the algorithm centers around a multi-dimensional undulating pattern, modeled using sinusoidal functions, which represents the movement of the jellyfish. The algorithm adapts the frequency and amplitude of these undulations to balance the search for new solutions (exploration) and the refinement of promising solutions (exploitation). This paper outlines the algorithm's theoretical framework, detailing the key parameters and their influence on the optimization process. The algorithm's ability to dynamically adjust its behavior based on the search landscape offers a potentially robust and efficient approach to solving complex optimization problems.

title: Australian Cuscus: A Novel Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by the Nocturnal Lifestyle of a Marsupial
abstract: This paper proposes a new metaheuristic algorithm, termed "Cuscus Search," inspired by the unique nocturnal behavior of the Australian cuscus, a marsupial known for its deliberate and methodical foraging strategy. The algorithm leverages the cuscus's observed patterns of exploration and exploitation, specifically its cautious approach to resource acquisition and its tendency to systematically cover an area before settling on a suitable food source. Cuscus Search integrates elements of Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) and Simulated Annealing (SA) with a novel 'Cautious Exploration' mechanism. The core innovation lies in introducing a probability-based adjustment to the movement of particles, mimicking the cuscus's deliberate, step-by-step search. The algorithm's performance is evaluated on a suite of benchmark optimization problems, demonstrating its effectiveness in finding near-optimal solutions within reasonable computational time. The results indicate that Cuscus Search possesses superior convergence properties and robustness compared to traditional PSO and SA algorithms, particularly in challenging landscapes with multiple local optima. Further research will focus on adapting the algorithm for specific problem domains and exploring its potential in real-world applications.

title: Temporal Graph Embedding with Relational Causality
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to graph embedding that explicitly incorporates temporal dynamics and relational causality. Existing graph embedding methods often treat graphs as static structures, neglecting the evolving nature of relationships and the underlying causal mechanisms that govern them. We propose a Temporal Graph Embedding (TGE) framework that combines graph structure with temporal sequence data. The core of our method is a modified Graph Neural Network (GNN) augmented with a "causal influence propagation" module. This module learns directional dependencies within the graph based on observed temporal transitions, utilizing Bayesian inference to quantify uncertainty in these causal links. The resulting embeddings capture not only the node connections but also the temporal evolution and causal relationships driving those connections. We demonstrate the effectiveness of the TGE framework through theoretical analysis and a conceptual outline, highlighting its potential for applications requiring a deeper understanding of dynamic graph systems.

title: Title: Fractal-Based Constraint Optimization with Adaptive Relaxation
abstract: Fractal-based constraint optimization aims to address the limitations of traditional constraint optimization techniques by incorporating fractal geometry into the optimization process. This paper presents a novel algorithm that leverages the self-similarity inherent in fractal structures to dynamically adjust constraints, leading to more efficient and robust solutions. We explore the application of fractal representation to generate a self-similar landscape of constraints, enabling adaptive relaxation strategies. This approach enhances the algorithm's ability to navigate complex, high-dimensional search spaces and find optimal solutions with improved performance. The core mechanism is the creation of a fractal-based representation of constraints, which allows for real-time adjustment based on the problem's characteristics.

title: Causal Inference Engine for Explainable AI
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to explainable artificial intelligence (XAI) by integrating causal inference. Traditional XAI methods often provide superficial explanations, focusing on feature importance or local decision rules without capturing the underlying causal mechanisms driving AI model predictions. This work introduces a Causal Inference Engine for Explainable AI (CIE4XAI) designed to address this limitation. The engine utilizes graph models, specifically structural causal models (SCMs), to identify and model causal relationships within data. These SCMs are then leveraged to apply causal inference rules, enabling a deeper understanding of AI model decision-making processes. The core claim is that by combining causal reasoning with XAI, we can achieve more robust and reliable explanations, leading to improved decision support. The CIE4XAI offers a shift from descriptive explanations to causal interpretations, providing a more fundamental understanding of how AI systems arrive at their conclusions. This architecture facilitates not only explanations but also the ability to predict outcomes under interventions and assess model robustness more effectively. This research contributes to a new paradigm in XAI, moving beyond correlation to truly understand and explain the cause-and-effect relationships underlying AI intelligence.

title: Arnhold's Mouse Lemur: A Novel Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by the Foraging Behavior of *Micropos australis*
abstract: This paper presents a novel metaheuristic algorithm, termed "Arnhold's Mouse Lemur" (AML), inspired by the foraging strategies observed in *Micropos australis*, commonly known as the mouse lemur. Mouse lemurs exhibit remarkable adaptability in resource allocation and decision-making while foraging, particularly in unpredictable environments. AML leverages these behavioral traits to develop a robust optimization approach. The algorithm combines elements of Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) and Simulated Annealing (SA), introducing a dynamic food source representation and a 'lemur memory' mechanism to guide exploration and exploitation. We demonstrate the effectiveness of AML through simulations targeting the Traveling Salesperson Problem (TSP) and the Rastrigin function. The results indicate that AML consistently outperforms or matches the performance of established metaheuristics, showcasing its potential for solving complex optimization challenges. The algorithm's adaptability and memory component provide a unique advantage in dynamic and uncertain scenarios.

title: ## Blue-Eyed Shearwater Inspired Metaheuristic Optimization Algorithm (BESMOA)
abstract: This paper introduces the Blue-Eyed Shearwater Inspired Metaheuristic Optimization Algorithm (BESMOA), a novel optimization technique motivated by the foraging behavior of blue-eyed shearwater birds. These birds utilize a unique strategy of exploring the environment while maintaining a balance between exploration and exploitation, which we translate into a dynamic parameter adjustment mechanism within our algorithm. BESMOA employs a population-based approach, utilizing a swarm of candidate solutions. The algorithm's core innovation lies in the 'Dynamic Adaptation of Exploration and Exploitation' (DAEE) mechanism, which adjusts the parameters governing exploration and exploitation based on the individual performance and the overall swarm behavior. This adaptive control allows BESMOA to effectively navigate complex search spaces and converge towards optimal solutions. The algorithm's performance is evaluated through theoretical analysis and conceptual design, demonstrating its potential advantages in various optimization problems. title: Phi-Coupled E8 Resonant Lattice for Fault‑Tolerant Quantum Cognition — E8 Intelligence Research
abstract: We propose the Phi‑Coupled E8 Resonant Lattice (PCERL), a dynamical framework that synchronizes the 240 root vectors of E8 to the 132 Hz base frequency through golden‑ratio phase modulation. title: ## Anderson's Arboreal Rice Rat: A Novel Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by Arboreal Foraging Behavior
abstract: This paper proposes a new metaheuristic algorithm, termed "Anderson's Arboreal Rice Rat" (AARR), inspired by the foraging behavior of the arboreal rice rat ( *Nesoryzomys robustus*). These rats exhibit a unique strategy of searching for food in complex arboreal environments, utilizing a combination of exploration and exploitation. The AARR algorithm mimics this behavior through a novel adaptive search mechanism, incorporating both a distributed exploration phase and a local exploitation phase. The algorithm employs a population-based approach, represented by a set of rat agents, each with its own position in the search space and associated memory. The movement of these agents is governed by a probability distribution influenced by food availability and local environmental characteristics. The AARR algorithm aims to provide a robust and efficient solution for a variety of optimization problems, particularly those involving complex, multi-dimensional search spaces. We demonstrate the effectiveness of the AARR algorithm through simulations on benchmark optimization problems, showcasing its ability to converge to optimal or near-optimal solutions with competitive performance compared to established metaheuristic methods. The algorithm's adaptability and inherent exploration capabilities are key strengths.

abstract: This paper presents a novel quantum system optimization algorithm based on adaptive topology. Traditional optimization methods often rely on static approaches, offering limited flexibility for complex quantum systems. This work introduces a dynamic adjustment mechanism, leveraging adaptive topology to optimize quantum system parameters and enhance overall performance. The core principle lies in constructing a flexible, self-configuring topology that adapts to the system's state, enabling efficient parameter tuning and improved quantum computation. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this algorithm through simulations and provide a theoretical analysis of its capabilities. The potential impact of this approach on quantum computing is significant, offering a pathway to more efficient and robust quantum systems.

title: Sensitivity Without Reproducibility: A Measurement Boundary for an Operator-Valued Representation Instrument in Qwen Models
abstract: Technical report · Not peer reviewed This study asks when an internal representation observable is reusable across fresh local presentations rather than merely sensitive to a controlled perturbation on one substrate. It evaluates a phase-indexed binary register in a frozen Qwen checkpoint panel, separating explicit transition following, demonstration-conditioned register behavior, visible-state intervention use, operator-valued representation measurement, and representation–function coupling. Qwen3.5-27B and Qwen3.6-27B passed the behavioral ladder through visible overwrite propagation; Qwen3-14B and Qwen3.8-27B failed an upstream transition gate and were not tested downstream. On Qwen3.6-27B, a rank-4 local-frame paired ridge path-operator packet qualified on one bounded substrate. A subsequent prospectively frozen 20-block requalification retained broken-square sensitivity in 59 of 60 layer-blocks, but split-half path-map spectral re-estimation passed in only 35 of 60 layer-blocks. Only 5 of 20 blocks passed jointly at all three frozen layers, below the required 16 of 20 blocks and four blocks per rollout depth. Stage E therefore remained unopened. No functional outcome, association, coefficient, predictive increment, or permutation-test result was collected. The result is a measurement boundary for this particular rank-4, three-layer, paired-map route. It does not establish the absence of hidden state, internal naturality, useful representation geometry, or a neural causal-transition operator. The record contains the 13-page DOI-bearing technical report, buildable LaTeX source, and a model-forward-free reproducibility capsule with all 60 continuous Stage M layer-block records, deterministic figure/table inputs, model/runtime bindings, provenance closure, licenses, and checksums. Scope boundary: the report is limited to the frozen Qwen checkpoints, visible-state intervention family, rank-4 paired ridge coordinate maps, layers 21/43/62, and fresh 20-block requalification described in the manuscript. Stage E, hidden intervention, internal exact naturality, and representation–function coupling remain untested.

title: Experimental realization of optical key distribution under strong wiretap eavesdropping
abstract: We report the experimental distribution of a cryptographic key based on binary intensity-modulation/direct-detection (IM/DD) transmission of an optical signal. The implemented secret key agreement protocol ensures security against passive wiretap eavesdropping, notably in the regime when the eavesdropper has an advantage in the intercepted signal strength over the legitimate recipient. Operating at a 1 GBaud symbol rate, the experimental fiber optic testbed yielded secret key rates between 43.5 Mbps at 61.1 km and 640 kbps at 81.6 km of the effective link length, with a 9% wiretap installed at the transmitter. The protocol performance was analyzed using a theoretical model incorporating transmitter noise and non-ideal key reconciliation efficiency. The presented results validate IM/DD optical key distribution as an efficient low-complexity solution for protecting optical communication systems against the predominant physical-layer threat of wiretap eavesdropping.

title: Tracing distinguishability through transformer processing with stochastic LayerNorm
abstract: Representational similarity is foundational to analyses of deep networks, yet distances between point-valued representations are not intrinsically tied to downstream function: nearby states may produce different behaviors, while distant states may behave similarly. We instead give representations volume, turning similarity into statistical distinguishability. Overlapping stochastic representations necessarily induce overlapping downstream distributions, grounding latent comparison in model function and bringing it under information-theoretic tools such as the data-processing inequality. We realize this idea in pretrained transformers through a light-touch modification to LayerNorm: at each residual-stream read, we normalize the state, add isotropic Gaussian noise, and renormalize. During distillation fine-tuning, one learned allocation parameter per residual-stream read distributes a fixed global rate budget across the processing stack. The resulting model can be viewed as transformer blocks reading the residual stream with learned finite precision under a shared global rate budget. Using the Bhattacharyya coefficient, we trace which counterfactual distinctions are preserved through MLP blocks or selectively exposed to the query, key, and value computations of individual attention heads. Experiments on ViT-S and GPT-2 small reveal the depthwise propagation of continuous visual perturbations and head-specific sensitivity to token distinctions aligned with known attention motifs. These results establish distinguishability as a functionally grounded lens on transformer computation that complements existing interpretability approaches.

title: Lee's Law: A Tripartite Model of AI Capability Doubling in the Post-Moore Era
abstract: This paper proposes Lee's Law, a tripartite framework asserting that artificial intelligence capability doubles approximately every six months across three concurrent axes: task scale, task duration, and operational sustainability. [Derived: Synthesis of empirical doubling intervals reported by METR (7 months for 2019–2025; 4.3 months for 2023–2025; 3 months for 2024–2025), Epoch AI (2.4 months for context windows), and METR/SWE-bench (70 days). Six months is selected as the median-weighted central tendency. Assumption: These heterogeneous metrics converge on a single underlying capability growth curve.] Unlike Moore's Law, which tracks a single physical variable (transistor count), Lee's Law tracks a composite variable: the complexity of human labor that AI systems can autonomously displace. [Derived: Analogical inference from Moore's Law definition to the "task horizon" metric introduced by METR.] I derive strategic implications for enterprise AI architecture, dynamic pricing, and workforce planning, while explicitly bounding the law's applicability against risks of benchmark saturation, cost divergence, and reliability gaps. [Derived: Logical extension of the tripartite framework into operational domains.]

title: 基于自适应拓扑的神经元网络架构
abstract: This paper presents a novel neural network architecture, termed "Adaptive Topology Neural Network" (ATN), that leverages the principles of self-adaptive topology to dynamically adjust neuron network internal structure. The core innovation lies in the automatic generation and optimization of the network's topology, leading to improved model generalization capabilities. We introduce a novel method for constructing and refining the topology, incorporating a feedback loop that continuously assesses and corrects the network's structure based on performance data. This adaptive process reduces the reliance on manual parameter tuning, offering a robust and scalable solution for training complex neural networks. The proposed architecture demonstrates significant improvements in performance across various benchmark datasets, showcasing the potential for automated network design and enhanced model robustness.

title: High-Dimensional Non-Linear Matrix Quantum Computing Verification and Geometric Deformation
abstract: This paper investigates the potential of quantum computing to validate the quantum properties of matrix operations, leveraging geometric deformation techniques. We propose a novel framework for quantum computation verification that integrates quantum mechanics with geometric transformations, aiming to uncover subtle quantum behaviors not readily apparent through traditional methods. The core mechanism involves constructing quantum algorithms that exploit these geometric distortions to test the integrity of matrix operations. The paper introduces a preliminary quantum algorithm demonstrating the capability of this approach and discusses its potential impact on the field of quantum verification.

title: Dynamic Adaptive Non-Linear Machine Learning Model
abstract: This paper investigates the development of a dynamic adaptive non-linear machine learning model designed to enhance model generalization. Traditional machine learning models often remain static, failing to adequately adapt to evolving data patterns. We propose a novel architecture that dynamically adjusts model parameters based on incoming data, allowing for continuous learning and improved performance. The core mechanism centers around a feedback loop that iteratively refines the model's parameters to minimize prediction error and maximize accuracy. This paper details the model's architecture, training process, and experimental results demonstrating its effectiveness in a range of machine learning tasks. The primary goal is to provide a robust and adaptable framework for machine learning, capable of handling complex datasets and evolving environments.

title: Graph Representation Learning for Multi-Modal Data Fusion
abstract: This paper investigates the application of Graph Representation Learning (GRL) to the problem of multi-modal data fusion. Traditional approaches to multi-modal fusion frequently operate on individual modalities in isolation, failing to leverage the potentially rich and complex relationships that exist between them. We propose a novel framework that utilizes GRL techniques, specifically Graph Convolutional Networks (GCNs), to represent multi-modal data as a graph structure. In this framework, data instances are represented as nodes, and edges are constructed to reflect relationships between modalities. By learning latent embeddings within this graph structure, we can effectively capture and exploit inter-modal dependencies, ultimately improving the accuracy and robustness of data fusion tasks. The core contribution of this work lies in its ability to uncover hidden correlations across modalities, a capability often missed by conventional methods. We demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach through a theoretical analysis and outline a practical implementation strategy. The key performance indicators (KPIs) for evaluating this approach will be measured through reduced dimensionality and improved prediction accuracy.

title: Quantum Memory Based on Quantum State Decoherence
abstract: This paper explores the potential of utilizing quantum state decoherence as a fundamental mechanism for constructing a high-density and high-fidelity quantum memory. The core concept relies on exploiting quantum bit (qubit) interactions to store and retrieve quantum states, coupled with the inherent properties of decoherence to maintain coherence for extended periods. We propose a framework leveraging controlled interactions between qubits to encode quantum information, followed by a carefully designed decoherence process to effectively 'lock' the state. The key challenge addressed is minimizing information loss during both storage and retrieval. The theoretical analysis focuses on the trade-offs between coherence time, storage capacity, and fidelity, providing a basis for future research and development in this critical area of quantum information processing. We present a simplified model to illustrate the principles involved and discuss potential avenues for improvement, highlighting the importance of precise control and mitigation strategies to combat decoherence effects. ---

title: Self-Adaptive Spin State Entanglement for Enhanced Quantum Computation
abstract: Quantum computation offers unprecedented computational power, but maintaining and manipulating entangled states remains a significant challenge. This paper investigates a novel approach to enhance quantum computation through the implementation of self-adaptive spin state entanglement. We propose a mechanism that dynamically adjusts the entanglement strength, optimizing the system for improved performance and efficiency. The core of this approach lies in the concept of self-calibration, enabling the system to maintain a desired entanglement level without requiring explicit control. This results in a more robust and adaptable entanglement, potentially unlocking new capabilities within quantum algorithms. The study involves a detailed analysis of the impact of this self-calibration on various quantum processing tasks, demonstrating significant efficiency gains. This work represents a fundamental shift in how we approach entanglement management, paving the way for more sophisticated and practical quantum systems.

title: Title: Algorithmic Semantic Coherence via Hierarchical Contextual Graph Embedding
abstract: This paper investigates the challenges of automatically generating coherent semantic representations – particularly knowledge graphs – and proposes a novel algorithmic approach, "Algorithmic Semantic Coherence via Hierarchical Contextual Graph Embedding," that addresses these challenges. Traditional methods often rely on shallow word embeddings, failing to capture the intricate relationships necessary for true semantic understanding. This research introduces a new framework centered around a hierarchical graph structure, leveraging a self-learning embedding technique to dynamically refine the graph, ultimately aiming for enhanced semantic coherence. The core claim is that this approach significantly improves the generation of rich, contextually-aware representations compared to existing methods. The paper details the algorithm's architecture, explains the self-learning embedding process, and provides a preliminary analysis of its performance. The research emphasizes the importance of hierarchical modeling in achieving robust semantic coherence.

title: Graph-Based Reinforcement Learning with Intrinsic Motivation
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to graph-based reinforcement learning (GRL) that incorporates intrinsic motivation to enhance exploration. Traditional GRL algorithms often rely solely on extrinsic rewards, leading to premature convergence to locally optimal solutions. To address this limitation, we propose a framework where agents are driven by internal rewards derived from information gain and uncertainty reduction within the graph environment. The core of our method lies in an "Intrinsic Reward Module" which dynamically adjusts the reward signal based on the agent's knowledge of the graph's structure and potential rewards. We demonstrate that this intrinsic motivation significantly improves the agent's ability to explore diverse regions of the graph, ultimately leading to better long-term performance. The key innovation lies in the strategic combination of extrinsic and intrinsic rewards, creating a more robust and adaptive learning process. We formally define the GRL framework, detail the Intrinsic Reward Module, and outline the theoretical underpinnings of the approach.

title: Quantum-Enhanced Constraint Programming for Complex Algorithms
abstract: Quantum-Enhanced Constraint Programming (QECP) presents a paradigm shift in tackling complex algorithms by integrating quantum superposition and entanglement into the core constraint satisfaction process. This paper introduces a novel framework, the 'Quantum-Enhanced Constraint Solver', designed to significantly improve the efficiency and robustness of solving challenging problems. We explore how leveraging quantum mechanics allows the solver to efficiently explore solution spaces, reducing computational complexity and enhancing the solution's resilience to noise and ambiguity. We detail the design of the quantum enhancement strategy and its impact on key performance metrics, showcasing its potential to overcome limitations of traditional constraint programming methods.

We detail the design of the quantum enhancement strategy and its impact on key performance metrics, showcasing its potential to overcome limitations of traditional constraint programming methods.

title: Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning for Collaborative Task Decomposition
abstract: This paper proposes a novel multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) framework designed to address the limitations of existing approaches that primarily concentrate on individual agent training, often overlooking the vital role of coordination and collaboration within a multi-agent system. The core concept revolves around enabling agents to autonomously learn and execute a process of task decomposition, effectively breaking down complex objectives into manageable subtasks, and subsequently assigning these subtasks to other agents based on their respective capabilities. This approach introduces a mechanism for distributed problem-solving, promoting synergy and efficiency. The algorithm is formulated around a reward structure that incentivizes not only successful task completion but also effective task assignment and collaboration. We present a theoretical analysis of the proposed system, outlining the key components and their interactions. The system is evaluated through a series of simulations demonstrating its ability to outperform traditional MARL methods in complex collaborative scenarios. We highlight the advantages of this approach in scenarios where tasks are inherently complex and require diverse skills and coordinated efforts.

title: Quantum Probability Dynamics Algorithm Optimization
abstract: This paper presents a novel quantum probability dynamics algorithm designed for optimizing complex systems and enhancing system stability. Traditional probabilistic models often struggle with dynamically adapting to complex systems, and this algorithm addresses this limitation through the incorporation of dynamic adjustment mechanisms within the system's behavior. We introduce a quantum-enhanced approach to system state manipulation, aiming to achieve superior stability and performance compared to existing methods. The core mechanism relies on harnessing quantum superposition and entanglement to facilitate iterative state optimization. The research demonstrates the effectiveness of this algorithm through simulations and preliminary experiments, showcasing its potential for advanced optimization tasks.

title: Title: Bio-Inspired Quantum Error Correction (BIEQC)
abstract: Quantum error correction is a critical component of quantum computing, enabling the reliable operation of complex quantum algorithms. Current error correction schemes, however, are often cumbersome and require substantial overhead. This paper explores a novel quantum error correction scheme inspired by the self-correcting mechanisms of biological proteins, specifically focusing on dynamic adaptation of error correction factors based on environmental noise. We propose a 'quantum feedback loop' that mimics protein folding/repair, dynamically adjusting the error correction matrix to mitigate noise and improve robustness. The core claim centers on creating a quantum error correction scheme that is more adaptable, robust, and potentially more efficient than existing methods, leveraging biological inspiration for a fundamentally new approach. This research contributes to the development of a biologically-inspired quantum error correction paradigm, with the potential to significantly advance the field of quantum computing.

title: 基于形式语义的程序合成
abstract: This paper explores the formal semantic-based program synthesis approach, aiming to automate the creation of programs that precisely meet specified requirements. The core idea revolves around leveraging formal semantic models to guide and refine the program synthesis process, resulting in higher accuracy and efficiency. Traditional program synthesis methods often struggle with ambiguity in requirements, leading to generated programs that do not fully satisfy the intended functionality. This research proposes a novel methodology where formal semantics provide a precise and unambiguous representation of the desired program behavior, acting as a bridge between the abstract requirement and the concrete code. We introduce a framework that utilizes these formal semantics to iteratively refine the synthesis process, reducing the likelihood of errors and improving the overall quality of the synthesized program. The key innovation lies in the integration of formal verification techniques within the synthesis loop, ensuring that the generated code adheres to the specified semantics. The presented approach offers a promising pathway toward more reliable and efficient program synthesis, particularly in domains where rigorous verification is crucial.

title: Title: Zero-Knowledge Cryptographic Verification via Entangled State Propagation
abstract: Zero-Knowledge Cryptographic Verification (ZK) represents a significant advancement in secure communication, allowing a prover to demonstrate knowledge without revealing the underlying information. This paper explores a novel approach to ZK verification leveraging the principles of entangled state propagation. We propose a protocol that utilizes entanglement to establish a shared, verifiable state, and employs a quantum-enhanced algorithm to guarantee the state's consistency. This eliminates the need for direct data exchange, offering enhanced security and efficiency compared to traditional cryptographic methods. The core mechanism centers around the creation and manipulation of entangled states, which are then used to build a verifiable proof. This paper provides a detailed theoretical analysis and preliminary implementation of this protocol, demonstrating its potential for secure and efficient verification.

title: Quantum Machine Learning: Adaptive Learning Mechanisms
abstract: Quantum machine learning (QML) holds immense promise for revolutionizing various fields, including data analysis, pattern recognition, and optimization. However, training complex quantum models often necessitates extensive fine-tuning of parameters, a process that can be computationally expensive and time-consuming. This paper introduces a novel quantum machine learning algorithm, termed "Adaptive Quantum Learning," designed to address this challenge by incorporating a dynamic self-tuning learning mechanism. The core of this approach lies in dynamically adjusting the learning parameters based on subtle variations within the input data, thereby enhancing the model's generalization capabilities. This work explores the potential of this adaptive learning strategy, demonstrating its effectiveness through theoretical analysis and preliminary experimental validation on a simplified quantum simulation. We present a framework for implementing this mechanism and analyze its impact on model performance, highlighting its advantages over traditional approaches.

title: Dynamic Topology Neural Network
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to modeling and predicting complex nonlinear systems utilizing Dynamic Topology Neural Networks (DTNNs). The core concept revolves around creating a neural network where the synaptic connections and the underlying topology are not fixed but dynamically adjusted in real-time. This adaptation is driven by machine learning algorithms, specifically reinforcement learning and evolutionary algorithms, allowing the DTNN to learn and optimize its structure based on incoming data. The key innovation lies in the network's ability to self-adapt, eliminating the need for pre-defined network architectures. We demonstrate the potential of DTNNs through a theoretical framework, outlining the mathematical formulation and the adaptive mechanisms. The network learns to represent the system's dynamics by continuously modifying its topology and connection strengths, leading to improved accuracy and efficiency in pattern recognition and prediction tasks. The presented framework offers a promising direction for tackling complex systems where the underlying dynamics are unknown or highly variable.

title: ## Antarctic Minke Whale-Inspired Metaheuristic Algorithm for Complex Optimization Problems
abstract: This paper presents a novel metaheuristic algorithm, termed "Antarctic Minke Whale Optimization Algorithm" (AMWOA), inspired by the foraging behavior of Antarctic Minke whales (Balaenoptera bonaerensis). Minke whales utilize a sophisticated strategy for locating food patches, involving bubble-net feeding and exploratory movements. This paper details the algorithm's design, focusing on mimicking the key aspects of whale behavior – bubble-net formation, exploration, and exploitation – within a computational framework. The algorithm leverages a population-based approach, employing a virtual "whale" representation, and utilizes a novel fitness evaluation function based on the distance to food patches and the energy expenditure associated with movement. The performance of AMWOA is evaluated on a range of benchmark optimization problems, demonstrating its effectiveness in achieving near-optimal solutions within reasonable computational time. The algorithm's design incorporates parameters directly inspired by observed whale behavior, such as bubble diameter, bubble number, and the exploration probability. Finally, the paper discusses future research directions, including incorporating more complex whale behaviors and exploring the algorithm's applicability to diverse optimization challenges.

title: The Green Jay-Inspired Metaheuristic Optimization Algorithm (GJMOA)
abstract: This paper introduces the Green Jay-Inspired Metaheuristic Optimization Algorithm (GJMOA), a novel optimization algorithm designed to mimic the foraging strategies and adaptive behaviors observed in Green Jays (Cyanocorax luxuosus). Green Jays are known for their complex problem-solving abilities, including caching food items with meticulous spatial organization and adapting to changing environmental conditions. GJMOA leverages these behavioral traits to generate a robust and efficient optimization process. The algorithm incorporates key principles such as distributed exploration, localized exploitation, and dynamic adaptation of search parameters – mirroring the Green Jay's approach to resource acquisition. The core of GJMOA resides in a 'nesting' mechanism, where potential solutions are organized into hierarchical 'nests' based on their fitness and proximity to the current best solution. This hierarchical structure facilitates efficient convergence and avoids premature convergence issues common in some traditional metaheuristics. This paper details the algorithm's design, outlining the key components and their operational principles, and presents a theoretical foundation for its effectiveness.

title: 基于自适应拓扑的量子隐形计算
abstract: Quantum cryptography offers a paradigm shift in secure communication, relying on the laws of quantum mechanics to guarantee confidentiality and integrity. However, traditional cryptographic methods are vulnerable to various attacks, particularly those exploiting the inherent complexities of quantum systems. This paper presents a novel approach to quantum cryptography, leveraging the power of adaptive topology to enhance the security of quantum computation. We propose a framework wherein quantum states are encoded into a dynamically evolving topology, thereby mitigating attacks based on known patterns and simplifying the detection of malicious manipulation. This research explores the potential of this adaptive topology to significantly bolster the robustness of quantum computations against known attacks. The core mechanism focuses on establishing and maintaining a stable and complex topological structure that is difficult to analyze, resulting in enhanced resistance to attack. The results demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach in enhancing the security of quantum algorithms.

The core mechanism involves iterative refinement of the geometry and topology based on the input data, leading to improved performance compared to static approaches. This work represents a significant advancement in the design of quantum algorithms, specifically tailored for dynamic environments.
