title: The Elastic Game: A Narrative Review of Dynamic Difficulty Adjustment and Player Modeling from Malone's Challenge to Adaptive Platform Games
abstract: Dynamic difficulty adjustment---the game's attempt to measure the player and reshape the challenge---moved from Malone's theory of intrinsically motivating challenge through the AI-for-DDA workshop's proposals and the AI difficulty scaling to the data-driven player models, the behavioral modelling surveys, and the adaptive platform games whose effects the eye trackers measured. This article presents a narrative review of that arc's canonical line: Malone's 1981 intrinsic motivation, Hunicke and Chapman's 2004 AI for DDA, Spronck and colleagues' 2004 difficulty scaling, Yannakakis and Hallam's 2007 entertainment optimization, Missura and Gartner's 2009 player modelling, Pedersen, Togelius, and Yannakakis's 2010 experience modeling, Lopes and Bidarra's 2011 adaptivity survey, Shaker and colleagues' 2010 personalized content, Zook and Riedl's 2012 temporal player model, Bakkes and colleagues' 2012 behavioural modelling, Isaksen and colleagues' 2015 survival analysis, and Denisova and Cairns's 2015 adaptation effects. The review is organized around three themes: the challenge's theory, in which the intrinsic motivation's theory and the AI workshop's proposals defined the adjustment's problem; player modeling, in which the preference models, the physiological entertainment measures, and the behavioural and temporal data-driven profiles made the player measurable; and adaptive systems and evaluation, in which the personalized generation, the survival analysis's game spaces, and the adaptation's measured effects built the evidence. It is concluded that the elastic game is the challenge's feedback loop---the player's model as the difficulty's input---and that its arc is the measurement's rise from the designer's intuition to the player's data.

title: Fenocosm reproduction snapshot: the fenocosm analysis package
abstract: The fenocosm analysis package — the software snapshot that regenerates every number and figure in the Fenocosm arm of the Feno program. Contents: the fenocosm/ package (the protocol module pinning every constant and seed; the exact 2k-state Kronecker forward pass and MSM-Cox counting channel; the sparse-event competitor roster — homogeneous Poisson, a Bayesian-blocks piecewise-constant Poisson, a free-transition Poisson HMM, a periodic-windowed Poisson, a Weibull renewal; the wavelet-scattering moment vector; the IAAFT and mask-aware point-process surrogate generators; the loaders and fetch/reduction modules; and one driver module per sealed record), the x*.py top-level drivers, verify.sh and the x0_verify.py apparatus gate, the tests/ suite (data-free by construction), tools/ (including the pandoc-free paper-PDF builder), and vendor/ with its CHECKSUMS.sha256 pinning the four vendored CC BY 4.0 modules byte-for-byte. LICENSE, CITATION.cff, PROVENANCE.md, README.md, CONSTITUTION.md and FINDINGS.md travel with it. Not included: data/ (all real light curves, flare event lists and burst tables are public archival products fetched at run time and never committed — the fetch and reduction code is included) and out/ (the sealed records are deposited separately, each with its own DOI). The apparatus gate runs from this snapshot with no network and no data files. Deposit note. All seven Feno-program repositories are private and remain private, so this deposit is standalone: it carries its own reproduction materials, its metadata contains no repository link, and sibling work is referenced by DOI rather than by repository path. Related Zenodo DOIs cited below are reserved with publication pending. Part of the Feno program. The source repository is private; the reproduction materials for this record are contained in the record itself.

title: SingProbe Technical Report
abstract: Runtime guardrails are essential for reliable large language model (LLM) deployment, yet existing approaches typically rely on independent, external models that introduce additional inference cost, delayed safety signals, and a capacity mismatch with increasingly capable base models. To address these issues, we introduce SingProbe, a lightweight intrinsic runtime guard that directly reuses hidden states produced during LLM inference and operates alongside autoregressive decoding. Within a unified framework, SingProbe continuously predicts query intent, response safety, and hallucination risk at the token level with negligible additional guardrail inference overhead, offering a "free-lunch" solution. We further introduce SingStreamBench, a benchmark designed to assess whether streaming guardrails remain inactive on benign prefixes while promptly detecting emerging unsafe content. Extensive experiments show that SingProbe achieves competitive or superior performance compared with substantially larger standalone guardrails and specialized hallucination detectors, with only approx2M parameters and <0.5% extra overhead. Beyond passive detection, we also show that SingProbe scores can anticipate future generation risk and guide constrained safe decoding. We further extend this paradigm to medical generation through SingProbe-Med, which selectively activates risk-directed decoding interventions only when clinically relevant risks emerge. Together, these results demonstrate that internal model representations provide an effective and efficient interface for generation-time monitoring and control.

title: Title: Geometric Representation of Information Flow in Neural Networks
abstract: This paper explores the potential of utilizing geometric representations to enhance the understanding and optimization of neural network information flow. Traditional approaches often rely on complex, abstract models, while this work proposes a novel approach – the 'Flow Graph' algorithm – that visualizes network data flow based on shortest paths and topological changes. The core claim is to develop a new geometric representation that offers a more efficient and grounded method for analyzing and improving neural network performance. We outline the algorithm's design, demonstrate its efficacy through illustrative examples, and discuss its implications for future research in neural network design. The analysis will focus on minimizing computational complexity and enhancing the visibility of critical information propagation patterns.

title: Non-linear Self-Organizing Chaos Systems: An Optimization Algorithm
abstract: This paper introduces a novel optimization algorithm based on the principles of non-linear self-organizing chaos systems. Traditional optimization methods often rely on static parameter adjustments, which struggle to effectively capture the inherent dynamic behavior of complex systems. This work proposes a new algorithmic framework that leverages the system's self-organization to dynamically adjust key variables, thereby optimizing energy, information, and state allocation. The core mechanism involves modeling the system's dynamics as a set of "chaos variables" and employing a feedback loop to iteratively refine these variables, leading to enhanced performance. The design incorporates a novel dynamic adjustment mechanism that dynamically alters system parameters based on observed behavior, demonstrating a significant improvement in optimization efficiency compared to traditional approaches. This research contributes to the development of robust optimization techniques suitable for challenging, non-linear systems.

title: Dynamic Topological Dependency Learning (TDTL)
abstract: This paper introduces Dynamic Topological Dependency Learning (TDTL), a novel approach to knowledge representation and reasoning that leverages reinforcement learning to dynamically construct and adapt an internal knowledge graph based on observed data and inference results. Unlike traditional methods that rely on pre-defined topologies or manual annotation, TDTL autonomously learns data dependencies through a 'topological optimization' algorithm. The system begins with a simple, undirected graph and iteratively modifies it based on prediction errors, guided by a reward signal. A 'topological regularization' mechanism is incorporated to prevent over-complexity and maintain graph connectivity. The core claim is that a system can automatically build and adjust its internal knowledge representation's topology to reflect dynamic data dependencies without pre-defined topologies or manual labels. This represents a significant departure from existing knowledge graph construction and reasoning techniques. ---

title: Quantum Random Number Generation
abstract: Quantum random number generation (QRNG) offers a fundamentally different approach to randomness compared to classical methods. This paper explores the design and principles of a QRNG based on harnessing the inherent uncertainty in quantum measurements. The core claim is the development of a system capable of generating truly random quantum bit sequences. This is achieved by exploiting the probabilistic nature of quantum measurement, specifically the collapse of the wave function upon observation, which yields unpredictable outcomes. The generated sequences are expected to exhibit statistical independence, a crucial property for various quantum computing applications. This work lays the groundwork for a detailed exploration of QRNG techniques, highlighting their potential impact on secure quantum communication and simulation. We will detail the theoretical underpinnings, focusing on the mathematical formulation of the process and the statistical properties of the generated random numbers.

title: Quantum-Driven Constraint Relaxation
abstract: Quantum-Driven Constraint Relaxation (QDCR) is a novel quantum algorithm designed to systematically reduce constraints within dynamical systems. This paper introduces a quantum annealing approach, enhanced with a novel constraint-aware optimization strategy, to achieve efficient and targeted constraint alleviation. The core mechanism centers on utilizing quantum annealing to rapidly explore the solution space, effectively minimizing the impact of constraints while simultaneously enhancing the likelihood of discovering novel solutions. We explore the potential benefits of QDCR, particularly in scenarios where traditional optimization methods struggle with complex constraints, and detail the design of the algorithm's key components. The research highlights the theoretical advantages and potential practical applications of this approach, aiming to significantly advance the field of constrained optimization.

title: Based on Extensible Logic Programming for Complex System Modeling
abstract: This paper explores the application of extensible logic programming to the modeling and reasoning about complex systems. Traditional approaches to modeling complex systems often struggle with scalability, maintainability, and the ability to incorporate new knowledge effectively. We propose a framework utilizing extensible logic programming, where system knowledge is represented as logical rules, enabling automated inference and decision-making. The core of this approach lies in the extensibility of the logic programming paradigm, allowing for dynamic adaptation to evolving system requirements and the seamless integration of new information. This work demonstrates the potential of this methodology for tackling complex system modeling challenges, offering a more flexible and robust solution compared to conventional methods. We present a conceptual model and discuss key considerations for implementing such a system, focusing on rule representation, inference engine design, and scalability strategies. ---

abstract: This paper investigates the potential of non-Euclidean geometry to revolutionize quantum entanglement computation. Traditional approaches often rely on simplified geometric models, which can limit the precision and efficiency of calculations. We propose a novel quantum entanglement computation framework based on the properties of non-Euclidean geometry, aiming to achieve significantly enhanced computational capabilities. The core claim is that precise modeling of non-欧几何场论's geometric properties allows for the design of a quantum entanglement computation algorithm, exceeding the limitations of conventional methods. This work explores the implications of this approach, focusing on the potential for greater accuracy and efficiency in entanglement-based quantum operations.

title: Black Flying Squirrel: A Novel Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by the Flight Dynamics of the Black Flying Squirrel
abstract: This paper presents a novel metaheuristic algorithm, termed "Black Flying Squirrel" (BFS), inspired by the unique flight dynamics of the *Pteromyini* genus, commonly known as the black flying squirrel. The algorithm leverages the squirrel's remarkable ability to glide efficiently through the air, utilizing precise adjustments of its body posture and tail movements to control its trajectory and minimize energy expenditure. BFS incorporates elements of both Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) and Artificial Bee Colony (ABC) algorithms, integrating a novel 'Posture Adjustment Mechanism' (PAM) that mimics the squirrel's dynamic control. PAM adjusts the position and velocity of candidate solutions based on a dynamically calculated 'glide angle' and 'energy conservation' principle. The algorithm's performance is evaluated on a suite of benchmark optimization problems, demonstrating its effectiveness in finding near-optimal solutions within reasonable computational time. The results indicate that BFS exhibits competitive performance compared to established metaheuristic algorithms, particularly in problems requiring adaptive and dynamic adjustment strategies. Future work will focus on further refining the PAM and exploring its applicability to a broader range of optimization problems.

title: Graph Neural Networks for Social Network Analysis
abstract: This paper explores the application of Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) to social network analysis. Traditional social network analysis methods often struggle to capture complex, hidden relationships and patterns within networks, particularly in large and dynamic social structures. GNNs offer a novel approach by directly learning representations of nodes based on their network context. This work details the core concept of representing social networks as graph structures and leveraging GNNs to perform tasks such as node classification and link prediction. We demonstrate the potential of GNNs to uncover valuable insights by modeling relationships as a graph, and learning from the network topology itself. The results suggest GNNs can provide a significantly improved analytical tool for understanding social networks compared to conventional methods. ---

title: ## Bemanasy Mouse Lemur: A Novel Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by the Behavior of *Microprolemotherius*
abstract: This paper presents a new metaheuristic algorithm, the Bemanasy Mouse Lemur (BML) algorithm, designed for solving complex optimization problems. The algorithm's inspiration stems from the foraging behavior of *Microprolemotherius*, a small mouse lemur known for its efficient exploration and exploitation of its environment. BML combines elements of Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) and Simulated Annealing (SA), incorporating a novel "memory-based exploration" mechanism inspired by the lemur's spatial memory and scent marking. The algorithm utilizes a dynamic population size, adaptive inertia weight, and a memory matrix to represent the lemur's learned foraging paths. Theoretical analysis demonstrates the algorithm's convergence properties and its potential for achieving global optima. The paper outlines the algorithm's core principles, mathematical formulations, and a conceptual framework. The algorithm's performance is discussed through simulated scenarios, showcasing its effectiveness in various optimization problems. Further research directions are suggested to enhance the BML algorithm and explore its applicability to diverse real-world challenges.

title: Bearded Emperor Tamarin Metaheuristic Algorithm (BETMA)
abstract: This paper presents a novel metaheuristic algorithm, the Bearded Emperor Tamarin Metaheuristic Algorithm (BETMA), inspired by the unique grooming behavior of the Bearded Emperor Tamarin (Bolobo). The algorithm leverages the tamarin's meticulous and selective grooming strategy to effectively explore and exploit the search space in optimization problems. BETMA incorporates a novel 'territory guarding' mechanism, mimicking the tamarin's defense of its territory, and a 'selective attention' component, mirroring its focused grooming. The algorithm utilizes a population-based approach with a dynamic fitness assignment based on territory importance. Mathematical formulations for key components, including territory assignment, fitness evaluation, and elitism, are presented. We demonstrate the algorithm's effectiveness through simulations on several benchmark optimization problems, showcasing its competitive performance compared to established metaheuristic methods such as the Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) and the Artificial Bee Colony (ABC) algorithms. The algorithm's performance is evaluated using metrics such as solution accuracy, convergence rate, and computational efficiency. Finally, we discuss the algorithm's potential applications in various fields, highlighting its adaptability and robustness.

title: Information-Theoretic Grounding of Reinforcement Learning Reward Functions
abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) has achieved remarkable success in various domains, yet a persistent challenge remains: the design of effective reward functions. Traditionally, reward functions are painstakingly crafted by human experts, often relying on heuristics and domain-specific knowledge. This approach frequently results in brittle policies – those that perform well in specific environments but fail to generalize to even slightly altered conditions. This paper proposes a novel framework for designing RL reward functions that is fundamentally grounded in information theory. We argue that reward functions should directly optimize for the reduction of prediction error and uncertainty, leveraging measures such as mutual information and entropy. Our approach offers a systematic and principled way to construct reward functions that are inherently robust, generalizable, and less reliant on hand-engineering. We demonstrate the potential of this information-theoretic grounding through a theoretical analysis and outline a methodology for translating complex real-world problems into an information-theoretic reward design process. The core claim is that by directly optimizing for information-theoretic goals, we can create more reliable and adaptable RL agents.

title: 基于自适应的概率空间优化算法
abstract: This paper introduces a novel probabilistic space optimization algorithm based on adaptive parameter adjustment. Traditional optimization methods often struggle with complex, non-linear systems, requiring extensive parameter tuning. Our algorithm dynamically adjusts the probability space parameters to enhance optimization results' reliability and efficiency. We propose a framework that employs a self-tuning mechanism to automatically adapt to the system's characteristics, leading to improved performance across various optimization tasks. This work addresses limitations of existing approaches by offering a flexible and robust solution. The core mechanism centers around a hierarchical adjustment strategy that iteratively refines parameter values based on feedback and a learned model of the problem space. We present comprehensive experimental results demonstrating the effectiveness of this algorithm in diverse scenarios, highlighting its superior performance compared to established methods.

title: Dynamic Topology Transformation via Neural Networks
abstract: This paper explores the application of neural networks to dynamic topology transformation, a field with significant potential for enhancing image processing and 3D modeling. We propose a novel algorithm that utilizes a recurrent neural network (RNN) to learn and adapt to the evolution of topological structures within data. The core mechanism involves iteratively updating the network's weights based on observed data, enabling automated optimization and transformation. This approach offers a paradigm shift from manual design, leveraging the network's ability to extract meaningful topological information directly from the input. This work demonstrates the feasibility and potential benefits of this dynamic topology transformation technique in various applications.

title: ## The Mud Snail Inspired Adaptive Evolutionary Algorithm (MSEA)
abstract: This paper introduces the Mud Snail Inspired Adaptive Evolutionary Algorithm (MSEA), a novel metaheuristic optimization algorithm inspired by the foraging behavior and adaptive strategies of *Lymnaea stagnalis* (mud snails). The MSEA leverages the snail's ability to efficiently search for food in a complex environment, incorporating concepts like trail following, resource prioritization, and dynamic adjustment of movement patterns. The core of the algorithm lies in a modified evolutionary strategy where individuals represent potential solutions, and their movement is governed by a combination of gradient descent, heuristic exploration, and a dynamically adjusted "trail strength" based on resource availability and individual performance. The algorithm utilizes a population-based search with adaptive mutation and crossover operators, designed to maintain diversity and promote convergence towards optimal solutions. We propose a theoretical framework for the MSEA, outlining its key components and operational principles, highlighting its potential advantages over traditional metaheuristic methods in challenging optimization problems.

title: Anatolian Serotine-Inspired Metaheuristic Optimization Algorithm
abstract: This paper proposes a novel metaheuristic optimization algorithm, termed the Anatolian Serotine-Inspired Metaheuristic Optimization Algorithm (ASIMO), inspired by the foraging behavior of the Anatolian serotine ( *Tarsonillus armiger* ). These insects exhibit a remarkable ability to efficiently locate and exploit food sources within complex environments. ASIMO leverages the serotine's characteristic of exploring and exploiting simultaneously, focusing on the principles of adaptive step size adjustment and memory-based search. The algorithm employs a population-based approach, utilizing a swarm of agents that iteratively adjust their positions based on the fitness of their surroundings and the guidance of a memory vector. The core innovation lies in a dynamically adjusted step size function that mimics the serotine's responsiveness to food concentration gradients. Mathematical formulations describing the algorithm's key components, including the adaptive step size mechanism and the memory update strategy, are presented. The algorithm's performance is evaluated through simulations across various benchmark optimization problems, demonstrating its efficacy in achieving optimal or near-optimal solutions within reasonable computational time. The results indicate that ASIMO offers a competitive alternative to established metaheuristic methods, particularly in problems exhibiting non-uniform fitness landscapes.

title: Quantum-Inspired Entangled Representation Learning for High-Dimensional Data
abstract: This paper introduces a novel representation learning technique, termed "Entangled Representation Learning," which addresses the limitations of conventional dimensionality reduction methods when dealing with high-dimensional data. Traditional approaches often struggle to capture complex, non-local dependencies within the data, leading to information loss and suboptimal representations. Our method draws inspiration from quantum entanglement, explicitly modeling and encouraging correlations between data points through a modified quantum phase estimation algorithm. This process maps data into a Hilbert space, fostering 'entanglement' between distant points and generating a compressed representation that surpasses the capabilities of classical correlation matrices. We demonstrate the efficacy of this approach through a theoretical analysis and provide a detailed formulation of the algorithm, highlighting its potential for improved feature extraction and data analysis in scenarios with intricate correlations. The core claim of this work is that classical dimensionality reduction methods fail to adequately capture the complex correlations present in high-dimensional data, particularly when considering non-local dependencies. The core mechanism is the development of this novel technique, which actively encourages entanglement between distant points.

title: Quantum Obfuscated Optimization Algorithm Dynamic Adjustment (QOADA)
abstract: Quantum Obfuscated Optimization Algorithm Dynamic Adjustment (QOADA) is a novel optimization algorithm designed to enhance the stability of iterative optimization processes by dynamically adjusting optimization parameters based on observed noise and uncertainty within the optimization landscape. This approach leverages the unique properties of quantum-mechanical optimization algorithms to achieve a more robust and adaptive optimization strategy. The core mechanism involves a continuous, real-time assessment of the optimization process, triggering adjustments to key parameters based on these assessments. This dynamic adaptation mitigates the effects of noise and uncertainty, leading to improved convergence rates and a more reliable outcome. The paper details the theoretical framework, implementation steps, and experimental results demonstrating the effectiveness of QOADA in various optimization scenarios.

title: ## The Adaptive Burrowing Algorithm: A Metaheuristic Inspired by Axolotl Behavior
abstract: This paper introduces the Adaptive Burrowing Algorithm (ABA), a novel metaheuristic optimization technique inspired by the unique burrowing behavior of axolotls. Axolotls are remarkable amphibians known for their ability to rapidly adapt their burrowing strategy based on environmental conditions, primarily soil moisture. The ABA mimics this adaptive process through a dynamic population of agents, each representing a potential burrow location. These agents continuously assess their suitability based on a "moisture gradient" – a dynamically updated function reflecting the algorithm's perception of the optimization landscape. Agents adjust their position and orientation based on this gradient, utilizing a combination of local search and global exploration strategies. The algorithm's core innovation lies in its adaptive adjustment of the 'moisture gradient' weighting, mimicking the axolotl's shift in burrowing technique depending on soil conditions. This paper details the algorithm's design, mathematical formulation, and potential applications, emphasizing its adaptability and robustness in complex optimization problems.

title: 基于量子纠缠的分布式计算
abstract: Quantum entanglement, a peculiar phenomenon where two or more particles become linked and share the same fate, holds immense potential for revolutionizing computation. This paper explores the feasibility of establishing a distributed computing framework predicated on quantum entanglement, aiming to achieve unprecedented computational efficiency and data processing capabilities. We delve into the fundamental principles underpinning this approach, outlining the core mechanism and highlighting the novel aspects of leveraging entanglement for parallel processing. The investigation focuses on the potential benefits and challenges associated with this paradigm shift, emphasizing the rigorous design and implementation required to realize a robust and scalable distributed computing system.

title: Title: Adaptive Topological Structure for Quantum Information Processing Efficiency Enhancement
abstract: Quantum information processing is a critical area of research, and the inherent challenges of quantum error correction, particularly the high frequency of quantum error correction, pose a significant bottleneck in the advancement of quantum computing. This paper investigates the use of adaptive topological structure to optimize quantum information processing, aiming to reduce quantum error correction frequency and thereby enhance computational efficiency. The core mechanism involves tailoring the quantum system's topological structure to minimize the impact of decoherence and improve the fidelity of quantum operations. We present a novel algorithm and theoretical analysis demonstrating the potential for significant efficiency gains through this approach. The study explores the impact of various topological parameters and their influence on error rate.

title: Title: Hierarchical Quantum State Collapse for Data Compression
abstract: This paper presents a novel quantum state collapse protocol designed for data compression. Traditional compression techniques often employ a uniform collapse process, failing to fully leverage the inherent structure of data. We propose a hierarchical approach, where collapse occurs at multiple levels of complexity, optimizing compression efficiency through a carefully constructed system. This method aims to surpass existing approaches by identifying and exploiting the inherent patterns within data, leading to a significantly improved compression ratio. The core mechanism focuses on dynamically adjusting collapse levels based on data characteristics, ensuring targeted compression. The investigation involves a theoretical analysis of the collapse process and a practical implementation utilizing a simplified quantum system to demonstrate the protocol's effectiveness. The core claim is that a hierarchical quantum state collapse protocol significantly enhances data compression efficiency compared to conventional methods.

title: Fractal Dimension-Based Constraint Optimization
abstract: This paper explores the application of fractal dimension as a novel constraint optimization technique. Traditional optimization methods often struggle with complex, high-dimensional problems, while fractal geometry offers a geometric framework for representing and analyzing these challenges. We propose a method that leverages the fractal dimension of a solution space to guide the search process, facilitating the identification of optimal solutions through self-similarity. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach through a series of illustrative examples, showcasing improved efficiency and the potential for uncovering unexpected optimal solutions.

title: Can Video World Models Track Unobserved World States?
abstract: Video world models are increasingly used as simulators, yet visual fidelity alone does not show that a model maintains the hidden state of the world. We examine this gap with an action-conditioned video Shell Game, a visual analog of S_5 state tracking that decouples visual rendering from compositing the hidden state underneath. Bidirectional and autoregressive Transformers, Mamba, and linear attention restricted to nonnegative transition eigenvalues all fit the training horizon of 5 swaps and then fall toward chance on longer swap chains (extrapolation) while still rendering plausible video with additional denoising steps providing no benefit. The pixel-based diffusion target never supervises the unseen hidden state, so the generated frames cannot carry it and the state has to live inside the architecture rather than in the tokens. For a Transformer, that architectural state is only an append-only KV cache, so the model has to re-derive the hidden arrangement from the whole history at every chunk. We find two mechanisms that do extrapolate, and both carry a state across chunks and revise it in place. Linear attention succeeds once its transition eigenvalues may be negative, and TTT with a nonlinear fast weight succeeds by updating the feature map through which it reads its own state. We further examine harder cases in dynamic world exploration tasks, and discuss the broader implications for building stateful video world models.

title: Reader Surplus Separating Source Structure from the Structure of Reading
abstract: Reader Surplus Separating Source Structure from the Structure of Reading Dean Kulik QuHarmonics Research Group · ORCID 0009-0003-3128-8828 August 2026 Abstract Measurement theory is well supplied with accounts of what happens when a reader has too little resolution for its source. Aliasing, coarse-graining, and information loss are all instances, and all describe the same failure: distinctions present in the source collapse onto a single observation. This paper concerns the opposite failure, which is less discussed and considerably more dangerous, because it produces output rather than silence. When a reader imposes more address structure than its source supports, the surplus does not vanish. It appears in the record, and it appears as structure — correlated, reproducible, and mathematically consistent. Nothing marks it as the reader's own. A sinusoid sampled at ten times the necessary rate yields ten times the data and not one additional distinction; the added samples carry adjacent-sample correlation rising to 0.99998, which is a measurement of the sampling grid rather than of the signal. The clean geometric case is a sphere under a latitude-longitude chart. The unmarked sphere has a transitive symmetry group and therefore no distinguished point: its quotient under the rotation group is a single point, so it supports no intrinsic address whatever. A chart supplies two dimensions of address regardless, and that surplus cannot be sustained everywhere. At the poles every longitude terminates at one location, so the source offers one place while the representation offers a continuum of labels. The sphere is perfectly regular there. The chart is not. Regular source, singular representation, and the singularity belongs entirely to the reading. Two audit rules follow and they are mirror images. A reader may not claim distinctions it cannot resolve; and a reader may not attribute its own surplus structure to the source. Existing verification discipline enforces the first and has no test for the second. Applied retroactively to a body of work by this author, the second rule identifies six independent retracted claims as a single failure class rather than six unrelated errors. The paper closes with the bound. A source can be re-addressed without disturbance exactly within the commutant of its own evolution, which is the entire operator algebra when the source is static and shrinks as the source does more. A file admits six mutually incompatible partitions and survives all of them byte-identically because it holds still. That is not an engineering achievement. It is the price. Contents 1. An asymmetry in the standard account Ask what goes wrong when an instrument is inadequate to its subject and the literature answers immediately. The Nyquist–Shannon theorem gives the threshold below which frequency components become indistinguishable. Coarse-graining, partial traces, projections, and lossy compression all describe the same structure: a many-to-one map from source states to observations, with a fibre of states the reader cannot separate. Ask what goes wrong when an instrument exceeds its subject and the question sounds odd. More resolution is assumed harmless. Take more samples, use more coordinates, refine the mesh — the worst case is redundancy, and redundancy is merely wasteful. That assumption is wrong, and the error it permits is worse than the one it guards against. Insufficient resolution produces silence: distinctions that were present do not appear. Excess resolution produces speech. The surplus enters the record as structure, and structure invites explanation. An under-resolved reading fails to report what is there. An over-resolved reading reports what is not. The second failure is harder to detect because its output is well-behaved. Oversampled data is not noisy; it is smooth, correlated, and reproducible. Repeat the measurement and the same surplus appears. Every internal consistency check passes, because the surplus is genuinely consistent — with the reader. 1.1 What this paper establishes The reader–source relation has three regimes, not two, and the third has no standard name. Surplus is measurable: the diagnostic is whether added reader structure yields source-invariant distinctions. The sphere under a spherical chart is the exact case, with the pole singularity belonging demonstrably to the chart and not to the sphere. Two mirror audit rules cover both failures, where existing discipline covers one. Applied to a real body of work, the second rule collapses six independent retractions into one failure class. Surplus addressing is free exactly when the source is static, and the bound is the commutant of the source's own evolution. 2. The axis Write the reading as a map from source states to observations: rho : X -> Y Two quantities govern its behaviour. The source supports some number of independent distinctions, call it S. The reader imposes some number of independent addresses, call it Q. The regimes follow from their relation and not from either alone. Regime Condition What the fibre does What appears in the record Deficit Q < S many source states share one observation less than is there Matched Q \u2248 S the map is near-injective what is there Surplus Q > S many addresses share one source distinction more than is there The deficit and surplus fibres run in opposite directions and this is the structural point. In deficit, the fibre lives in the source: several states collapse to one reading. In surplus, the fibre lives in the reader: several addresses describe one source distinction. Both are many-to-one; they differ in which side is many. Resolution as ordinarily used is a property of the reader alone, and a one-dimensional quantity. It cannot express either failure, because both are relations. A reader is not too coarse or too fine in itself; it is too coarse or too fine for a particular source. 3. Deficit, measured The familiar side is included because the surplus side is only legible against it, and because the same experiment run in one direction gives both. Construct a source with twelve distinct frequency components at 50, 130, 270, 410, 530, 670, 790, 910, 1030, 1150, 1270 and 1390 Hz. Sample at a falling rate and count how many observed frequencies remain distinct — two components collide when they alias to the same position in the observed band. Sample rate (Hz) Nyquist Distinct addresses Collapsed Reads as 4000 2000 12 0 resolved 2000 1000 12 0 resolved 1000 500 11 1 partly folded 600 300 7 5 partly folded 400 200 7 5 partly folded 300 150 6 6 partly folded 200 100 5 7 partly folded 120 60 3 9 smooth 60 30 2 10 smooth 20 10 1 11 smooth Twelve distinctions become one. The components did not leave the source: raise the rate and all twelve return, undamaged, in their original positions. What changed was the observation map, which became progressively many-to-one. Smoothness in this experiment is not an absence of structure. It is a large fibre. This licenses a precise use of a phrase that is otherwise loose. Saying information was lost is misleading, because nothing in the source changed and nothing had to be reconstructed. The accurate statement is that mathematical distinctions became inaccessible through that particular map. The mathematics remained in the source and the interface stopped reaching it. 4. Surplus, measured Now run the same axis upward. Take a source with exactly two components, at 17 Hz and 50 Hz, and sample it far above the rate its bandwidth requires. Sample rate (Hz) Samples Adjacent-sample correlation Independent components 200 200 0.173248 2 1000 1000 0.959806 2 5000 5000 0.998377 2 50000 50000 0.999984 2 Two hundred and fifty times the samples. Zero additional source distinctions. And the adjacent-sample correlation climbs to 0.999984, which is a strong, stable, reproducible measurement — of the sampling grid. This is the danger stated concretely. The correlation is real, it survives repetition, it is not noise, and every consistency check on it passes. A reader who did not know the source had two components would find a highly structured record and would be right about its structure. The structure would be the reader's own. 4.1 The diagnostic The test that separates the two cases is not a property of a single reading. It is a comparison between readings at different reader capacities: Increase the reader's structure. Do source-invariant distinctions increase? If yes, the added capacity uncovered source structure — the fibre split, and the split is reproducible across independent readings of the same source. If no, the added capacity produced description without distinction, and the surplus belongs to the reader. In the deficit experiment, raising the rate from 20 Hz to 4000 Hz took the distinguishable count from 1 to 12. Source structure was uncovered. In the surplus experiment, raising the rate from 200 Hz to 50000 Hz took the count from 2 to 2. Nothing was uncovered, and what grew was correlation, which is a measure of the grid's own fineness. The diagnostic requires two readings. This is not incidental: a single reading, however careful, cannot distinguish source structure from reader structure, because both appear in it identically. 5. title: Title: Quantum Adaptive Probability System Modeling
abstract: Quantum adaptive probability system modeling aims to develop a novel approach to modeling quantum systems by leveraging quantum self-adaptability. This research explores the application of quantum self-adaptability to enhance system stability and accelerate quantum computation. We propose a framework that dynamically adjusts system parameters based on internal quantum states, thereby mitigating inherent instability issues commonly encountered in quantum systems. This model will provide a significant advancement in the design and management of quantum algorithms, potentially offering improved performance and robustness. The core mechanism lies in the implementation of a self-adjusting parameter adjustment process triggered by quantum state fluctuations. This approach contrasts with traditional, static models, which lack the ability to adapt to changing conditions. The paper will detail the design, implementation, and testing of this quantum adaptive probability system model, showcasing its potential to improve the stability and efficiency of quantum computations. The investigation will focus on demonstrating the efficacy of this model through simulations and, ultimately, potentially, preliminary experimental validation of its capabilities.

title: Self-Adaptive Geometric Mapping and Machine Learning
abstract: This paper investigates the integration of self-adaptive geometric mapping with machine learning to address data imbalance and improve data distribution learning. Traditional machine learning often relies on static models; this approach allows for dynamic mapping adjustments, offering a more flexible solution. We propose a novel algorithm that leverages self-adaptive geometric mapping to learn data distributions and mitigate the challenges associated with imbalanced datasets. The core mechanism involves dynamically adjusting the mapping based on learned data patterns, enabling the algorithm to effectively handle data heterogeneity. This research aims to establish a framework for robust data distribution learning through the combined power of geometric mapping and machine learning.

title: 基于混沌系统的自适应矩阵生成
abstract: This paper investigates the application of a novel self-adaptive matrix generation algorithm based on the dynamics of chaotic systems to enhance the generalization and stability of machine learning models. Traditional methods often rely on manually tuned parameters, which can be suboptimal and require extensive experimentation. This work proposes a method that dynamically adjusts the matrix weights based on the system's inherent characteristics, fostering a more robust and adaptable model. The core mechanism leverages the self-similarity inherent in chaotic systems to reduce model parameter sensitivity and improve performance across diverse datasets. We demonstrate the efficacy of this approach through simulations and experiments, showcasing a significant improvement in model convergence and robustness.

title: 拓扑量子几何的自适应自组装
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to topology quantum geometry, termed "Adaptive Topological Geometry" (ATG), which leverages quantum entanglement to dynamically modify topological structures and enable highly efficient computation and information storage. The core mechanism centers around a "Quantum Topology Key" (QTK) system, utilizing entangled pairs to guide the evolution of topology and control the dynamics of topological changes. We demonstrate the effectiveness of ATG through simulations and preliminary results, showcasing its ability to achieve unprecedented levels of computational speed and data storage density. The paper highlights the significance of this approach in pushing the boundaries of computational capabilities. title: Neuro-Symbolic Reasoning for Commonsense Knowledge Acquisition
abstract: Current artificial intelligence systems, particularly deep learning models, often exhibit a significant lack of commonsense knowledge – the implicit understanding of the world that humans possess effortlessly. This deficiency limits their ability to reason effectively in novel situations and to generalize learning across diverse contexts. This paper proposes a novel approach to knowledge acquisition called Neuro-Symbolic Reasoning, which aims to bridge the gap between the pattern recognition capabilities of neural networks and the structured reasoning abilities of symbolic systems. The core idea is to integrate these two paradigms, allowing neural networks to learn complex patterns from raw data and subsequently translate these patterns into formal logical rules. This facilitates a more robust and adaptable knowledge acquisition system, capable of handling ambiguous and uncertain information. The proposed framework leverages neural networks for data representation and feature extraction, while symbolic reasoning engines provide a mechanism for logical inference and rule generation. We outline the key components of this system and discuss its potential benefits and challenges. This approach addresses the limitations of existing AI systems by combining the strengths of both neural networks and symbolic reasoning, ultimately leading to a more intelligent and versatile knowledge base.

title: ## Azorean Bat-Inspired Metaheuristic Optimization Algorithm (ABMOA)
abstract: This paper presents a novel metaheuristic optimization algorithm, the Azorean Bat-Inspired Metaheuristic Optimization Algorithm (ABMOA), motivated by the foraging behavior of the Azorean bat. Bats utilize a sophisticated echolocation strategy to locate prey in complex environments. This algorithm leverages key aspects of bat echolocation, including pulse emission, frequency modulation, and receiver sensitivity, to guide the search process. ABMOA employs a population-based approach, mimicking the bat's social foraging dynamics. The algorithm incorporates a novel parameter, the "Echo Strength," which dynamically adjusts the exploration and exploitation balance. We demonstrate the effectiveness of ABMOA on a selection of benchmark optimization problems, highlighting its ability to converge to near-optimal solutions with reasonable computational effort. The algorithm's performance is compared against established metaheuristic methods such as Genetic Algorithm (GA) and Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO). The results suggest that ABMOA offers a competitive alternative, particularly in problems with complex landscapes and multimodal solutions. The core of ABMOA lies in its adaptation of bat-inspired principles for efficient and robust optimization.

title: Quantum Protocol Optimization Based on Quantum Coherence Draining
abstract: This paper investigates the optimization of Quantum Key Distribution (QKD) protocols leveraging the principles of quantum coherence draining. The core claim centers on utilizing the inherent properties of coherence draining to enhance key generation efficiency and overall security within QKD systems. The proposed mechanism involves the design of quantum gate circuits predicated on coherence draining, enabling efficient key generation and error correction, alongside a rigorous study of the impact of these draining characteristics on protocol security. The research addresses the need for improved QKD performance and robust security by exploring novel approaches to managing decoherence, a significant limitation in current QKD implementations. This work contributes to a deeper understanding of coherence draining's potential role in shaping more effective and secure quantum communication systems. Specifically, the investigation includes analyzing different decoherence models and their corresponding mitigation strategies within the framework of optimized QKD protocols. The core objective is to demonstrate a quantifiable improvement in key generation rate and security margins through strategic application of coherence draining techniques. ---

title: ## Mimic Crab Inspired Metaheuristic Optimization Algorithm (MCIMO)
abstract: This paper introduces the Mimic Crab Inspired Metaheuristic Optimization Algorithm (MCIMO), a novel metaheuristic algorithm motivated by the foraging behavior of mimic crabs. These crabs exhibit a unique strategy of alternating between exploratory and exploitative movements, adapting their search strategy based on the density of food sources. MCIMO leverages this behavior through a dynamic probability distribution and adaptive movement strategy. The algorithm employs a population of potential solutions, where each solution's position is represented as a vector (s_1, s_2, ..., s_K). A core element of MCIMO is the "Crab Density Estimation" function, which assesses the concentration of promising solutions in the search space. This function dynamically adjusts the probability of exploratory versus exploitative movements, guiding the population towards areas with higher potential. MCIMO's performance is evaluated through its adaptive parameters, including the exploration probability (e_p), exploitation probability (e_x), and crab density threshold (C_t). The algorithm's design aims to efficiently navigate complex search spaces while avoiding premature convergence, inspired by the mimic crab's resilience and adaptability in challenging environments.

title: ## The African Land Snail-Inspired Metaheuristic Optimization Algorithm (ALS-MHOA)
abstract: This paper introduces the African Land Snail-Inspired Metaheuristic Optimization Algorithm (ALS-MHOA), a novel optimization method derived from the foraging behavior of *Achatina fulica*, a large terrestrial snail found in Africa. The algorithm mimics the snail's exploratory movement, adaptive feeding strategy, and response to environmental changes. ALS-MHOA utilizes a segmented search space, representing the snail's territory, and employs a "pheromone trail" mechanism inspired by the snail's scent marking to guide exploration and exploitation. The core of the algorithm involves a dynamic territory segmentation, a probabilistic feeding strategy based on environmental cues, and an adaptive trail reinforcement system. This approach offers a potentially robust and efficient method for tackling complex optimization problems, particularly those with high dimensionality and non-convex landscapes. The algorithm's parameters are designed to reflect the snail's inherent adaptive capabilities, aiming for a balance between exploration and exploitation. This paper outlines the theoretical framework, the key components, and the underlying principles of ALS-MHOA, laying the groundwork for future experimental validation and application.

title: Probabilistic Programming with Causal Bayesian Networks for Counterfactual Reasoning
abstract: Counterfactual reasoning – the ability to reason about "what if" scenarios – is a cornerstone of human intelligence and a critical component in many fields, including medicine, economics, and artificial intelligence. Traditional probabilistic programming approaches often struggle to effectively address counterfactual queries, largely due to the inherent difficulties in explicitly modeling causal relationships. This paper introduces a novel framework combining probabilistic programming with causal Bayesian networks to overcome these limitations. The core idea is to allow users to directly specify causal dependencies between variables within a probabilistic programming environment, enabling efficient simulation and the generation of realistic counterfactual scenarios. The proposed system provides a powerful tool for understanding the causal impact of different events, offering a significant advancement over existing techniques. We demonstrate the framework's capabilities through illustrative examples, highlighting its potential for a wide range of applications. The system leverages techniques from Bayesian networks to represent causal relationships and probabilistic programming to perform simulations and queries. This allows for the derivation of counterfactual probabilities and the exploration of alternative scenarios. The overall goal is to facilitate more robust and interpretable reasoning about complex systems.

The algorithm's potential applications across various optimization problems are discussed.

title: Predictive Coding with Temporal Convolutional Networks
abstract: Predictive coding frameworks, while conceptually appealing for modeling cognitive processes, often face challenges in accurately representing temporal dependencies within sequential data. This work addresses this limitation by proposing a novel approach that integrates predictive coding principles with the strengths of Temporal Convolutional Networks (TCNs). The core idea centers around a TCN that learns to predict future input sequences based on past observations, leveraging dilated convolutions to effectively capture long-range temporal correlations. This combined architecture demonstrates improved predictive accuracy compared to traditional predictive coding models. The methodology details a specific TCN architecture optimized for temporal prediction, and presents preliminary results demonstrating the efficacy of this approach. The key innovation lies in the synergistic combination of these two techniques, offering a potentially more robust and accurate method for modeling temporal sequences.

abstract: Multi-agent reinforcement learning---the learning of behavior when the environment's other agents learn too---moved from Tan's independent learners and Littman's Markov games framework through the cooperative dynamics' analyses and the surveys' question to the deep era's communication, actor-critics, value decompositions, and the large-scale emergent play of Capture the Flag. This article presents a narrative review of that arc's canonical line: Tan's 1993 independent versus cooperative agents, Littman's 1994 Markov games, Claus and Boutilier's 1998 cooperative dynamics, Hu and Wellman's 1998 framework, Shoham, Powers, and Grenager's 2007 question, Busoniu, Babuska, and De Schutter's 2008 survey, Foerster and colleagues' 2016 learning to communicate, Lowe and colleagues' 2017 multi-agent actor-critic, Sunehag and colleagues' 2018 value-decomposition networks, Rashid and colleagues' 2018 QMIX, Jaderberg and colleagues' 2019 3D multiplayer Capture the Flag, and Hernandez-Leal, Kartal, and Taylor's 2019 survey and critique. The review is organized around three themes: the foundational frames, in which the Markov game's formalization and the non-stationarity's, the coordination's, and the equilibrium's problems defined the field's difficulties; the theory's question, in which the surveys asked what learning among learners is for; and the deep era, in which the communications, the centralized critics, the monotonic factorizations, and the population-scale play made the multi-agent learning practical. It is concluded that multi-agent reinforcement learning is the non-stationarity's discipline---and that its deep era turned the other learners' obstruction into the curriculum's engine.

title: WildSEEK: Evaluating Language Models for Information-Seeking
abstract: Language models are increasingly mediating information access to end users, urging a systematic evaluation of their responses for a fair and reliable information ecosystem. Existing evaluations, however, are often topic-specific or synthetic, limiting their ability to capture the complexity of "in the wild" information-seeking queries and the risks present in model responses. To address this gap, we introduce WildSEEK, a manually annotated dataset of 3k information-seeking queries from real user interactions, and an evaluation framework for LLM-generated responses. WildSEEK includes annotations for risk-sensitive domains (e.g. health and financial information), and distinguishes factoid queries from analytical queries which seek responses beyond facts. We train classifiers on WildSEEK to analyze more than 1.8M realistic user queries. We find that over a third of information-seeking queries are high-risk and more often analytical. Our findings show that LLM responses fail more often in four criteria: sycophantic behavior, overreliance, a default US-centric perspective, and poor handling of vulnerable populations -- with failure rates being mostly higher for analytical queries. By providing methods to monitor the reliability, safety, and fairness of LLM behavior, our dataset and evaluation framework offer an empirical foundation for the broader question of how these systems should behave as they take on a growing role in information access.

title: Dynamic Quantum State Optimization Algorithm
abstract: This paper introduces a novel dynamic quantum state optimization algorithm designed to efficiently optimize quantum states and enhance precise control. Traditional optimization methods often rely on static parameter settings, limiting their applicability to complex systems. This work proposes a dynamic approach that leverages quantum state's inherent adaptability to dynamically adjust quantum states, leading to improved optimization performance. The core mechanism involves a combination of quantum state self-adaptation and a tailored topology optimization algorithm, demonstrating significant improvements in achieving precise control and optimization accuracy. This algorithm addresses limitations of existing approaches, offering a more robust and adaptable solution for quantum state manipulation.

title: Dynamic Probability Field Model
abstract: This paper presents a novel dynamic probability field model designed to simulate complex system behavior and predict future states by dynamically adjusting probability field parameters based on real-time data and environmental changes. Leveraging the integration of machine learning and reinforcement learning, this model offers a significant advancement over traditional probabilistic models, enabling automated parameter tuning and real-time system modeling. The core mechanism focuses on continuously adapting probability field configurations, leading to enhanced prediction accuracy and efficiency. This work addresses a critical need for systems capable of robust and adaptable behavior in dynamic environments.

title: Adaptive Quantum Self-Adaptation Algorithm
abstract: Quantum computing offers the potential for exponential speedups over classical computing, but current algorithms often struggle to reach this potential due to the complexities of managing quantum states and the inherent limitations of quantum hardware. This paper introduces the Adaptive Quantum Self-Adaptation Algorithm (ASFAA), a novel quantum control strategy designed to dynamically adjust quantum operations based on the system's state. The algorithm leverages a self-adaptive mechanism to continuously refine quantum parameters, optimizing for improved performance and robustness. We present a theoretical framework for the algorithm's operation, demonstrating its ability to achieve significant efficiency gains in various quantum systems through automated parameter adjustments. The core claim of this research is that ASFAA provides a pathway to efficient quantum computation by automating the optimization of quantum gate parameters. This advancement addresses a critical challenge in quantum algorithm design and opens possibilities for more practical and scalable quantum computations.

title: Causal Inference from Multi-Modal Data Streams
abstract: This paper explores the application of causal inference techniques to multi-modal data streams, aiming to establish more accurate causal models for prediction and control in complex systems. Traditional single-modality causal inference methods often struggle with the inherent complexity and ambiguity present in real-world scenarios where information is conveyed through diverse sources like vision, audio, and text. This research proposes a framework that leverages the temporal dependencies within multi-modal data streams to identify causal relationships. The core of the approach involves employing causal discovery algorithms to automatically uncover these relationships within the data, followed by structured probabilistic modeling for reasoning and time-series analysis for prediction. The novelty lies in the integration of multiple modalities, allowing for a more nuanced and robust understanding of causal dynamics compared to traditional methods. We demonstrate the potential of this approach through a conceptual framework, outlining the key components and methodological considerations. Further research will focus on developing specific algorithms and evaluating the framework's performance on real-world datasets.

abstract: This paper introduces a novel pattern recognition algorithm based on quantum state manipulation, leveraging the unique properties of quantum entanglement to achieve rapid identification and modeling of complex patterns, particularly in large and high-dimensional datasets. Traditional pattern recognition methods rely on classical information retrieval, which suffers from inefficiency. We propose a quantum-enhanced approach that utilizes quantum state manipulation to drastically improve data analysis efficiency and accuracy. The core mechanism centers around the utilization of quantum entanglement to facilitate efficient pattern recognition and representation. This paper details the design of the algorithm, its theoretical underpinnings, and preliminary experimental results demonstrating its potential for significant improvements in pattern analysis.

title: Quantum Entanglement-Based Non-Linear Optimization Algorithm
abstract: This paper introduces a novel non-linear optimization algorithm based on quantum entanglement principles. Traditional optimization methods often struggle with complex, non-linear problems, demanding extensive manual tuning. This algorithm leverages quantum entanglement to establish a dynamic interaction between parameters, enabling a more adaptive and robust solution strategy. We propose a mechanism that iteratively adjusts parameters based on entanglement correlations, facilitating the exploration of complex solution spaces and improving the performance of various optimization tasks, particularly those encountered in machine learning, financial modeling, and risk management. The core of this approach lies in the manipulation of entanglement to achieve a more efficient and nuanced optimization process. This research explores the potential of quantum entanglement to surpass the limitations of classical optimization techniques.

title: 基于非线性自适应的机器学习模型
abstract: This paper introduces a novel machine learning model based on non-linear adaptive learning. The model incorporates a self-adaptive optimization algorithm to dynamically adjust model parameters, enabling efficient optimization even with large and noisy datasets. We demonstrate the model's effectiveness through a series of experiments evaluating its performance on diverse datasets, showcasing its ability to automatically tune parameters and achieve superior results compared to traditional methods. The core mechanism involves a non-linear adaptive algorithm that iteratively adjusts model parameters based on observed error, while the self-adaptive optimization algorithm ensures optimal parameter values. We provide a detailed analysis of the algorithm's performance and highlight its advantages in scenarios demanding rapid adaptation and robust performance.

title: Black Mongoose Metaheuristic Optimization Algorithm (BMMOA)
abstract: This paper proposes a novel metaheuristic optimization algorithm, the Black Mongoose Metaheuristic Optimization Algorithm (BMMOA), inspired by the foraging behavior of the Black Mongoose ( *Mellicta capensis* ). The algorithm leverages the mongoose's efficient search strategy for food, incorporating elements of exploration and exploitation to achieve robust performance in complex optimization problems. BMMOA utilizes a modified Levy flight mechanism for position updates, a dynamic population size control based on the mongoose's responsiveness to food availability, and a novel constriction mechanism mimicking the mongoose's focused hunting behavior. The algorithm's performance is evaluated on a range of benchmark functions, demonstrating its effectiveness in finding near-optimal solutions with reasonable computational cost. The key contributions of this work lie in the novel integration of mongoose-inspired behaviors into a metaheuristic framework, leading to a potentially superior optimization approach. The algorithm's performance is compared against established metaheuristic algorithms like Genetic Algorithm (GA) and Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) to highlight its advantages.

title: Topology-Driven Quantum State Collapse - Wave-Function Optimization
abstract: This paper explores the application of topology-driven quantum state collapse to design algorithms that optimize the collapse of quantum states. We propose a novel approach, termed the "Topological Field Mapping" (TFM), which analyzes a quantum state and constructs a map of its underlying topology. This map then guides the collapse process, aiming to generate highly structured and stable quantum states. The core claim is that this technique offers a pathway towards creating quantum states with unprecedented control and predictability. This research contributes to the fundamental understanding of quantum mechanics and provides a theoretical framework for optimizing quantum computation.

title: A Novel Metaheuristic Optimization Algorithm Inspired by Beech Marten Foraging Behavior
abstract: This paper presents a novel metaheuristic optimization algorithm, termed "Beech Marten Foraging Algorithm" (BMFA), inspired by the foraging behavior of beech martens. Beech martens are known for their intelligent and adaptive search strategies when locating food sources. BMFA utilizes a hybrid approach combining elements of Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) and Artificial Bee Colony (ABC) algorithms. The algorithm incorporates a novel 'trail marking' mechanism mimicking a beech marten's ability to remember and revisit promising areas. The core innovation lies in dynamically adjusting the exploration and exploitation phases based on the 'trail strength' associated with each potential solution. This trail strength is proportional to the solution's fitness and the number of iterations it has been explored. The algorithm's performance is evaluated through a series of benchmark functions, demonstrating its effectiveness in finding optimal or near-optimal solutions. Experimental results indicate that BMFA consistently outperforms traditional PSO and ABC algorithms in terms of convergence speed and solution quality. The algorithm's parameters are tuned using a grey wolf optimization method for enhanced performance. The primary keywords for this paper are: Metaheuristic Optimization, Particle Swarm Optimization, Artificial Bee Colony, Beech Marten, Trail Marking, Foraging Behavior, Adaptive Exploration, Adaptive Exploitation.

title: Quantum Computing Through Time Constant Optimization
abstract: Quantum computing promises a revolutionary leap in computational power, but its practical realization hinges critically on the control and manipulation of quantum bits (qubits). A significant bottleneck in achieving this potential is the inherent variability in qubit coherence times – often referred to as time constants. These time constants, denoted as *τ*, represent the duration for which a qubit maintains its quantum state before decoherence sets in, directly impacting the fidelity of quantum computations. This work explores the concept of optimizing these time constants to enhance the efficiency of quantum algorithms. We delve into the mechanisms that govern *τ* within various qubit systems and propose a novel algorithmic approach to dynamically adjust qubit parameters, aiming to minimize *τ* and maximize the duration of quantum operations. The core contribution lies in recognizing *τ* as a primary performance determinant and outlining a systematic strategy for its targeted improvement. The presented framework offers a potential pathway toward realizing the full potential of quantum computing by mitigating the detrimental effects of decoherence.

title: Symbolic Regression with Bayesian Optimization and Genetic Programming
abstract: This paper explores a novel approach to symbolic regression, aiming to improve both the accuracy and efficiency of equation discovery. The core idea is to integrate Bayesian optimization with genetic programming, creating a hybrid system. Bayesian optimization is used to guide the search for potentially good equation forms, effectively narrowing down the vast solution space. Genetic programming then utilizes this guided information to evolve and refine those forms, leveraging the strengths of both techniques. We propose a framework where Bayesian optimization iteratively suggests promising equation structures, and genetic programming evolves them, resulting in a more targeted and robust search process. This combined approach addresses limitations inherent in traditional symbolic regression methods and demonstrates the potential to uncover complex mathematical relationships that might otherwise be missed. The experimental results, while not presented through formal experimentation, strongly suggest the viability and efficacy of this combined methodology.

title: Quantum-Enhanced Chaos Theory Simulation
abstract: Quantum-enhanced chaos theory simulation aims to accelerate the exploration of complex and unpredictable systems by leveraging quantum entanglement to enhance computational power. This paper presents a framework combining quantum algorithms with established chaos theory methods to simulate intricate dynamics, revealing hidden order and potential emergent behaviors. We detail the core mechanism – utilizing quantum entanglement to accelerate the simulation process – and discuss the potential benefits in terms of speed, insight, and the ability to tackle previously intractable systems. The paper concludes with a discussion of the challenges and future directions of this burgeoning field.

title: ##基于多智能体强化学习的机器人群组控制
abstract: This paper investigates the application of multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) to the control of robot swarms for complex task execution. Traditional robot swarm control methods often rely on manually designed control strategies, which can be difficult to adapt to dynamic and uncertain environments. This research proposes a novel approach where a robot swarm is treated as a collection of individual agents, each learning its own action policy through MARL. The core mechanism involves decentralized learning, enabling the swarm to achieve coordinated behavior and perform complex tasks without explicit, centralized control. This work presents a framework for MARL-based robot swarm control, demonstrating its potential for robustness and adaptability in challenging scenarios. The primary focus is on the theoretical foundations and conceptual design, without experimental validation, aiming to provide a robust and scalable methodology for future research and development.

title: Aru Flying Fox: A Novel Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by the Flight of the Flying Fox
abstract: This paper presents Aru Flying Fox (AFF), a new metaheuristic algorithm designed for solving complex optimization problems. The algorithm is inspired by the remarkable flight capabilities of the flying fox (Pteropus), a large fruit bat known for its precise maneuvering and efficient energy expenditure during flight. AFF combines elements of Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) and Grey Wolf Optimization (GWO) with a novel adaptive mutation strategy mimicking the flying fox's ability to adjust its flight path based on environmental factors and prey location. The core innovation lies in the 'Dynamic Velocity Adjustment' (DVA) mechanism, which dynamically alters the velocity of each particle based on a simulated wind effect and the distance to the global best solution. The algorithm's performance is evaluated on a range of benchmark functions, demonstrating its effectiveness and competitive results compared to established metaheuristic algorithms. Key performance indicators such as convergence speed, solution quality, and computational efficiency are analyzed. This research contributes a potentially valuable tool for optimization tasks requiring adaptability and efficient exploration of the search space.

title: ## The Ripple Algorithm: A Metaheuristic Inspired by the Behavior of Pufferfish
abstract: This paper introduces the Ripple Algorithm, a novel metaheuristic optimization method inspired by the foraging behavior of pufferfish ( *Tetraodontidae* ). Pufferfish are known for their remarkable ability to locate and efficiently exploit food sources in complex environments, utilizing a strategy involving rhythmic "ripples" – localized disturbances in the water – to detect prey. The Ripple Algorithm mimics this process by iteratively generating and evaluating candidate solutions, modifying them based on a "ripple" mechanism that propagates changes throughout the search space. The algorithm's core components include a 'ripple amplitude' parameter controlling the extent of solution modification, a 'ripple frequency' dictating the rate of propagation, and a 'ripple decay' factor influencing the dissipation of the ripple effect. This paper details the algorithm's theoretical framework, explains its operational principles, and outlines its potential applications in various optimization problems. We aim to demonstrate that this bio-inspired approach offers a robust and adaptable method for tackling challenging optimization landscapes.

The algorithm's core components include a 'ripple amplitude' parameter controlling the extent of solution modification, a 'ripple frequency' dictating the rate of propagation, and a 'ripple decay' factor influencing the dissipation of the ripple effect. This paper details the algorithm's theoretical framework, explains its operational principles, and outlines its potential applications in various optimization problems. We aim to demonstrate that this bio-inspired approach offers a robust and adaptable method for tackling challenging optimization landscapes.

title: Quantum Information Theory: Adaptive Learning of Topological Geometry
abstract: Quantum information theory has witnessed significant advancements in recent years, primarily focusing on the development of quantum algorithms and their applications. However, a deeper investigation into the underlying principles governing these systems often overlooks a crucial and potentially transformative aspect: the role of topological geometry. This paper explores the potential of utilizing quantum information theory to enable adaptive learning and optimization within the context of topological geometry, driven by quantum entanglement and the inherent properties of topological structures. This work investigates a novel mechanism for quantum state learning and optimization, leveraging the power of quantum entanglement and topological geometry to achieve rapid adaptation and improved performance.

title: 基于自适应的自组织神经网络结构优化
abstract: This paper presents a novel algorithm for optimizing the structure of self-organizing neural networks (SONNs) through dynamic adjustment of connection strengths. Traditional SONNs often rely on manually defined layer configurations, which can be suboptimal and require significant tuning. Our proposed algorithm, termed "Adaptive Resonance Network Optimization" (ARNO), employs a self-adaptive reinforcement learning approach to automatically adjust connection weights, leading to improved network performance across various tasks. We demonstrate the effectiveness of ARNO through extensive experiments on benchmark datasets, showcasing significant gains in accuracy and efficiency compared to baseline methods. The core mechanism involves iteratively adjusting connection strengths based on a learned reward function, enabling the network to converge to an optimal configuration.

title: Andean Tapir: A Novel Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by the Behavioral Patterns of the Andean Tapir
abstract: This paper presents Andean Tapir, a new metaheuristic algorithm designed to address complex optimization problems. The algorithm's inspiration stems from the unique foraging and movement strategies observed in the Andean tapir ( *Tapirus Andeanus*). Andean Tapir combines elements of Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) and Simulated Annealing (SA) with a novel adaptive parameter adjustment mechanism influenced by the tapir's response to environmental changes and food availability. Specifically, the algorithm utilizes a 'Foraging Range' concept, mimicking the tapir's exploration of its surroundings for food, and a 'Resource Prioritization' mechanism, reflecting the tapir's preference for more abundant resources. The core of the algorithm involves a population of 'agents' representing potential solutions, navigating a search space guided by velocity and position updates. Adaptive parameters, specifically the inertia weight, cognitive coefficient, and temperature, are dynamically adjusted based on the perceived 'food abundance' – a measure of the solution quality – and the 'environmental uncertainty' – a measure of the diversity within the population. The performance of Andean Tapir is evaluated through a series of benchmark problems, demonstrating its effectiveness and competitiveness compared to established metaheuristic algorithms. The algorithm's adaptability and resilience, mirroring the tapir's survival strategies, are key characteristics that contribute to its robust optimization capabilities.
