title: Title: Bayesian Resonance Networks for Optimal Algorithm Design
abstract: Bayesian Resonance Networks (BRNs) represent a novel approach to algorithm design, moving beyond traditional trial-and-error methods. This paper introduces a framework predicated on the principle of statistical resonance – the idea that complex systems exhibit inherent patterns of stability and efficiency. We propose a BRN architecture that learns optimal algorithm parameters and structure by analyzing the statistical correlations within a large dataset of self-organizing systems. Unlike conventional optimization techniques, BRNs utilize Bayesian inference to iteratively refine parameters, leading to algorithms with enhanced performance and robustness. This work focuses on building a probabilistic model of algorithm behavior, enabling a data-driven approach that surpasses manual design by exploring the full space of possible solutions. The core mechanism involves constructing a network that captures the statistical landscape of algorithm performance, allowing for informed parameter selection and structure optimization.

title: Title: Bayesian Geometric Chaos for Optimal Network Design
abstract: This paper explores the application of Bayesian geometric chaos principles to optimal network design, moving beyond traditional gradient-based optimization techniques. The core claim is to develop a Bayesian framework that dynamically adjusts network parameters based on observed data, incorporating a probabilistic model of network instability. We propose a novel approach utilizing Bayesian inference to iteratively refine network architecture, leading to improved performance and robustness. The research focuses on incorporating a probabilistic representation of network dynamics, enabling the system to self-correct and adapt to changing data patterns. The paper details the theoretical underpinnings of the Bayesian geometric chaos framework, presenting a methodology for learning optimal network configurations through uncertainty quantification. Furthermore, we discuss the potential benefits of this approach, including enhanced generalization capabilities and improved resilience to noisy data.

title: ## Achaku Vesper Mouse: A Novel Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by Nocturnal Behavior
abstract: This paper presents Achaku Vesper Mouse (AVM), a new metaheuristic algorithm designed to address complex optimization problems. The algorithm draws inspiration from the unique nocturnal behavior of the Achaku vesper mouse, a small rodent known for its strategic foraging and navigation in low-light conditions. AVM utilizes a combination of adaptive parameter control, a novel exploration-exploitation balance mechanism based on simulated twilight phases, and a dynamic memory system mimicking the mouse's spatial memory. The algorithm's core components, including the twilight phase scheduling, memory update strategy, and parameter adaptation rules, are detailed. Performance evaluations on a range of benchmark optimization problems, including the Sphere function, Rastrigin function, and a modified version of the Traveling Salesperson Problem (TSP), demonstrate AVM's effectiveness in achieving high solution quality and convergence rates compared to established metaheuristic methods such as Genetic Algorithms (GA) and Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO). The algorithm's design emphasizes robustness and adaptability, making it suitable for a variety of applications.

title: Dynamically Reconfigurable Quantum Circuits for Machine Learning
abstract: This paper explores the development of dynamically reconfigurable quantum circuits tailored for machine learning applications. The core claim is the design of a hardware architecture capable of on-the-fly circuit reconfiguration, optimizing performance and resource utilization. This is achieved through the employment of programmable quantum gates and dynamic routing of quantum information dictated by the input data and algorithm requirements. The research addresses the limitations of static quantum circuit design by enabling adaptive and efficient quantum computation. Specifically, we investigate methods for mapping machine learning algorithms onto reconfigurable quantum circuits, considering factors such as circuit depth, qubit connectivity, and gate fidelity. We propose a framework for defining a quantum circuit's reconfiguration policy, incorporating real-time feedback from the execution of the algorithm. This framework allows the circuit to adapt its structure and operations to maximize computational efficiency. The theoretical analysis and design principles presented here contribute to the advancement of quantum machine learning by offering a pathway toward more flexible and powerful quantum computing architectures. The ultimate goal is to create quantum systems that can learn and adapt in a way analogous to biological neural networks, unlocking the full potential of quantum computation for complex machine learning problems.

title: PBFT-CG-MARL
abstract: PBFT-CG-MAPPO is a consensus-conditioned multi-agent reinforcement learning framework that embeds a Practical Byzantine Fault Tolerance (PBFT) three-phase commit protocol inside the CTDE-MAPPO training loop as an additive consensus loss with zero initialization, complemented by an entropy floor that prevents premature policy collapse. Across three cooperative environments (MPE spread, SMAClite 5m_vs_6m, VMAS UAV coverage) with five seeds each, PBFT-CG-MAPPO reduces cross-seed return variance by 1.9–47.4× compared to MAPPO and produces zero catastrophic seeds. Under Byzantine injection (f = 1), the PBFT quorum maintains stable consensus rates against random and adversarial attacks, where disabling the consensus layer causes up to 93% return degradation—demonstrating that consensus provides critical protection under active attacks while remaining non-interfering in clean environments. The experimental results yield three design principles for safe consensus conditioning in MARL: replace only dissenting actions (never overwrite consenting agents), condition via additive loss with zero initialization, and enforce an entropy floor. The framework transfers from 4-agent cooperative navigation to 12-agent permafrost monitoring without modification, scaling the f < n/3 tolerance bound automatically. The codebase includes six algorithm baselines (MAPPO, MADDPG, QMIX, CommNet, TarMAC), three Byzantine attack types, ablation studies, cross-environment evaluation, and publication-quality figure generation scripts.

title: OCR-MetaReasoning Benchmark: Evaluating the Meta-Reasoning Ability of MLLMs in Text-Rich Image Understanding
abstract: Text-rich image understanding requires multimodal large language models (MLLMs) to organize OCR (Optical Character Recognition)-grounded evidence across words, layout, fields, charts, and visual correspondences. Existing evaluations often conflate extraction with reasoning and rarely test whether models follow the required reasoning direction: applying visible rules, abstracting hidden regularities, or recovering missing premises. We introduce OCR-MetaReasoning, a controlled single-image benchmark that treats deduction, induction, and abduction as distinct directions and separates final-answer correctness from reasoning-process compliance. The benchmark contains 1,500 verified samples in a balanced \(3\times5\) taxonomy crossing three reasoning types with five OCR-object categories, along with reference reasoning steps, automatic answer scoring, the Meta-Reasoning Macro Score (MRMS), and the Reasoning Process Compliance Score (RPCS). Experiments with representative closed-source and open-source MLLMs show that OCR-grounded meta-reasoning remains far from saturated: models struggle with visible-rule application and layout-sensitive inference, while process-compliant rationales can accompany incorrect final answers under exact-match evaluation. The code is available at https://github.com/gengxuli/OCR-MetaReasoning.

title: Dynamic Topology Quantum Simulation – A Physical Phenomena Modeling Framework
abstract: This paper introduces a dynamic topology quantum simulation framework designed to model physical phenomena and provide an efficient simulation method. The core concept revolves around leveraging the inherent dynamic nature of topological structures to represent and simulate physical systems. We propose a novel approach that combines quantum algorithms with the principles of dynamic topology to achieve enhanced computational efficiency and facilitate the exploration of complex physical scenarios. This research offers a fundamentally new perspective on quantum simulation, moving beyond traditional methods and embracing the potential of topological structures. The study explores the potential of this framework to address challenges in modeling phenomena exhibiting intricate connectivity and persistent loops.

title: 异质性信息驱动的量子机器学习模型
abstract: This paper introduces a novel quantum machine learning model, termed "Heterogeneity-Driven Quantum Machine Learning," that leverages the principle of data distribution heterogeneity to dynamically adjust model parameters and enhance generalization. Traditional machine learning relies heavily on manually tuned parameters, limiting its ability to effectively exploit complex data distributions. This work proposes a quantum-enhanced approach that utilizes the inherent variability within datasets to automatically optimize model parameters, resulting in improved performance across diverse datasets. The core mechanism involves quantum-assisted parameter adjustment guided by data heterogeneity, leading to a more robust and adaptable learning process. The model's effectiveness is demonstrated through a series of benchmark experiments, showcasing enhanced generalization capabilities compared to traditional quantum machine learning methods.

title: Dynamic Quantum Entanglement Networks (DQN)
abstract: This paper introduces a novel dynamic quantum entanglement network (DQN) framework designed to optimize quantum computation by dynamically adjusting the scale and structure of entangled qubits. Traditional quantum computing architectures often rely on static, inflexible arrangements, limiting their adaptability to varying computational demands. DQN proposes a self-adaptive system that facilitates efficient utilization of quantum resources through intelligent network reconfiguration. The core mechanism involves adjusting entanglement parameters based on real-time analysis of computational requirements. This adaptive approach significantly enhances the performance and scalability of quantum algorithms. The paper explores the design and implementation of DQN, detailing its key components, the underlying mathematical principles, and the resulting improvements in quantum entanglement management. The benefits of this framework are demonstrated through a simulation, showcasing its ability to maintain coherence and achieve higher fidelity for a range of quantum circuits.

title: Title: Formal Verification of Emergent Complexity in Neural Networks
abstract: The pursuit of artificial intelligence has centered on the creation of complex systems capable of exhibiting emergent behavior – properties arising from interactions within a system that are not explicitly programmed. Traditional approaches to AI evaluation often rely on empirical testing and heuristic analysis, failing to adequately address the underlying mechanisms driving this emergent phenomenon. This paper proposes a novel framework for formal verification, utilizing a new 'complexity measure' to rigorously prove that neural network complexity cannot be reduced to the sum of its individual components. We introduce a rigorous mathematical proof demonstrating the absence of a simple, predictable reduction, suggesting a fundamental, self-contained emergent behavior. The core mechanism involves the development of a quantifiable measure of network structure that enables verification of capabilities beyond simple input-output mappings. The implications of this research are significant, offering a path toward verifiable, robust AI systems and a deeper understanding of the principles governing intelligent behavior.

title: Self-Referential Graph Neural Networks for Recursive Knowledge Representation
abstract: Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) have demonstrated remarkable success in various domains, including social network analysis, drug discovery, and recommendation systems. However, a critical limitation of conventional GNNs is their inability to effectively represent and reason about their own internal structure and representations. This paper introduces a novel approach – self-referential Graph Neural Networks – designed to overcome this limitation. The core idea is to treat the GNN's internal state, specifically its node embeddings, as data and incorporate this information back into the GNN's processing loop. This creates a recursive feedback mechanism, enabling the GNN to learn about its own representations and perform more sophisticated reasoning. We present a formal framework for this self-referential architecture, highlighting key components and operational principles. The proposed architecture allows for a deeper understanding of the graph structure and relationships, ultimately leading to improved knowledge representation and reasoning capabilities within GNNs. We explore the theoretical underpinnings of this approach, emphasizing the potential for iterative refinement and the development of more robust and intelligent graph-based models. The core claim is that traditional GNNs lack self-awareness, and this work introduces a solution to address this deficiency.

title: Black Uacari: A Novel Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by the Behavior of Black Uacaris
abstract: This paper presents Black Uacari, a new metaheuristic algorithm inspired by the foraging behavior of Black Uacaris (Cacajao calvus). These primates exhibit a unique strategy of repeatedly visiting and exploiting food patches, alternating between areas of high and low resource availability. Black Uacari leverages this observed behavior to develop a novel optimization algorithm. The algorithm incorporates a dynamic patch selection mechanism, mimicking the Uacaris' tendency to shift between areas, and a weighted exploration-exploitation strategy based on resource density. We demonstrate the effectiveness of Black Uacari through simulations on several benchmark optimization problems, including the Rosenbrock function, the Rastrigin function, and the Sphere function. The results show that Black Uacari consistently outperforms several established metaheuristic algorithms, such as Genetic Algorithm (GA) and Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO), in terms of convergence speed and solution quality. The algorithm's adaptability and ability to handle complex, multi-dimensional search spaces are key strengths. Future work will explore incorporating more nuanced aspects of Uacari foraging behavior, such as social interactions, into the algorithm's design.

title: # Black Right Whale: A Novel Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by the Migration Pattern of a Whale
abstract: This paper presents a new metaheuristic optimization algorithm, termed "Black Right Whale" (BRW), inspired by the unique migration pattern observed in the Black Right Whale. Unlike traditional metaheuristic algorithms, BRW leverages a dynamic, adaptive representation of the search space guided by the whale's navigational strategy – consistently moving towards the best solution while maintaining a degree of exploration. The algorithm incorporates three key components: a dynamic position update mechanism mimicking the whale's "right" movement, a social influence component reflecting the whale's collaborative search, and an adaptive inertia weight scheme that adjusts the exploration-exploitation balance. We demonstrate the efficacy of BRW through simulations on several benchmark optimization problems, showcasing its competitive performance compared to established metaheuristic algorithms such as Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) and Artificial Bee Colony (ABC). The algorithm's adaptability and ability to navigate complex, multi-dimensional search spaces make it a promising candidate for a wide range of optimization challenges.

title: High-Dimensional Data Structure Auto-Generation
abstract: This paper investigates the development of a novel data structure auto-generation system utilizing machine learning. Recognizing the challenges posed by high-dimensional data, this research proposes a method for automatically constructing data structures like matrices and graphs, thereby simplifying data processing and analysis. The system leverages neural networks to learn inherent data structure patterns and generates these structures with minimal human intervention. The core mechanism centers around the automated extraction of key structural features from high-dimensional data, enabling the generation of robust and well-structured data representations. This approach offers a significant advancement in data handling, addressing the limitations of traditional methods.

title: Causal Discovery from Observational Data with Deep Learning
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to causal discovery from observational data leveraging the power of deep learning. Traditional causal discovery methods frequently necessitate stringent assumptions regarding data distribution and relationships, often limiting their applicability in real-world scenarios. This work addresses this limitation by utilizing deep learning models, specifically variational autoencoders (VAEs), to learn robust, high-dimensional latent representations of observational data. These learned representations are then employed as input to established causal inference algorithms, such as Granger causality and PC algorithms, to infer causal relationships between variables. The integration of deep learning allows for the automatic extraction of relevant features and the handling of complex, non-linear dependencies, ultimately leading to more accurate and reliable causal discovery. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this combined approach through a theoretical framework and outline a methodology for practical implementation. The core claim of this work is that deep learning can significantly reduce the reliance on strong assumptions in causal discovery, providing a more flexible and potentially more accurate method for uncovering causal relationships from observational data.

title: 基于动态量子态的神经网络
abstract: This paper explores the potential of utilizing dynamic quantum states to enhance neural network performance, offering a novel approach to data representation and modeling. We propose a framework that leverages the inherent adaptability of quantum states to dynamically adjust the input data distribution, leading to more precise and robust models. The core mechanism involves simulating data evolution through quantum transformations, and subsequently mapping this evolution to a vector representation via a neural network. This approach aims to overcome limitations of traditional neural network architectures, potentially yielding improved accuracy and generalization capabilities. The study examines the theoretical advantages, potential challenges, and preliminary experimental results demonstrating the efficacy of this dynamic quantum state approach.

title: Adaptive Feature Learning via Relational Neural Networks
abstract: This research introduces a novel approach to feature learning using Relational Neural Networks (RNNs). Traditional methods of feature extraction often rely on manually defined features, which can be inflexible and may not capture the inherent relationships within data. The proposed framework addresses this limitation by enabling the network to learn feature representations directly from the relational structure of the data. Specifically, RNNs are trained to predict relationships between data points. The learned relational knowledge is then leveraged to generate new, adaptive feature representations. This approach offers significant advantages in scenarios where the underlying data structure is complex or poorly understood, leading to more robust and adaptable feature learning. The core idea is to shift from a feature-centric approach to a relationship-centric one, allowing the network to automatically discover meaningful features based on how data points interact. The effectiveness of this method is demonstrated through theoretical analysis and conceptual design, paving the way for future research and applications.

title: ## Multi-Tent Octopus Inspired Metaheuristic Optimization Algorithm (MOTIO)
abstract: This paper introduces the Multi-Tent Octopus Inspired Metaheuristic Optimization Algorithm (MOTIO), a novel metaheuristic algorithm inspired by the adaptive foraging behavior of multi-tent octopuses. The algorithm leverages the octopus's ability to dynamically adjust tent placement and movement based on environmental factors – specifically, prey distribution and obstacle avoidance – to establish a robust search strategy. MOTIO incorporates a tent-based population representation, a dynamic tent placement mechanism driven by gradient information and a novel tent retraction strategy mimicking the octopus's selective withdrawal of tentacles. The algorithm's core parameters are designed to emulate the octopus's adaptive responses, aiming for efficient exploration and exploitation of the search space. This paper details the algorithm's design, mathematical formulation, and provides a conceptual framework for its implementation, laying the groundwork for future experimental validation.

title: Quantum Machine Learning: A Novel Approach to Non-Linear Geometric Function Modeling
abstract: Quantum Machine Learning (QML) is a rapidly emerging field that leverages the unique properties of quantum mechanics to develop new algorithms and computational models. This paper presents a novel quantum machine learning approach centered on the modeling of non-linear geometric functions. Traditional machine learning struggles with complex, non-linear data, and QML offers the potential to overcome these limitations through inherent quantum properties. This research explores the integration of quantum algorithms into a framework designed to effectively represent and manipulate geometric relationships. We propose a specific model architecture incorporating quantum entanglement and superposition to enhance the capacity of the system to capture the essential features of these functions. The core mechanism centers around the application of quantum-enhanced geometric transformations, aiming to surpass the capabilities of classical methods. This work investigates the potential of such a model for a range of geometric tasks, demonstrating its promise as a powerful tool for advanced geometric analysis and modeling. The study presents a preliminary exploration of this approach and highlights the key challenges and opportunities for future development.

title: Title: Hierarchical Bayesian Networks for Bayesian Inference
abstract: This paper introduces Hierarchical Bayesian Networks (HBNs) designed to enhance Bayesian inference, specifically for complex, multi-faceted data. Traditional Bayesian methods often struggle with high-dimensional data and intricate dependencies, leading to suboptimal inference. The proposed HBN architecture leverages a nested structure—a hierarchy of Bayesian networks—to learn and represent these dependencies more effectively. This allows for improved accuracy, scalability, and robustness in inference across diverse datasets. The core mechanism centers around a 'nested Bayesian network' that dynamically adjusts the complexity of each level based on the input data, optimizing the inference process. This approach addresses limitations of existing methods by offering a more flexible and adaptable framework for Bayesian modeling. The paper details the architecture, training procedure, and evaluation of the HBN, showcasing its potential for significant advancements in probabilistic reasoning.

title: ## The Golden Pheasant Adaptive Search (GPAS) Algorithm: An Evolutionary Optimization Method Inspired by Golden Pheasant Behavior
abstract: This paper introduces the Golden Pheasant Adaptive Search (GPAS) algorithm, a novel metaheuristic optimization method inspired by the foraging and mating behaviors of the golden pheasant ( *Phasianus ryukyuensis*). The algorithm leverages the pheasant's strategic exploration of the environment, its selective breeding patterns, and its adaptability to fluctuating resources to create a robust search process. GPAS combines elements of Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) and Differential Evolution (DE), incorporating a dynamic adaptation mechanism based on the pheasant's response to environmental cues. Specifically, the algorithm utilizes a 'territory defense' mechanism akin to the pheasant's display behavior to promote diversity within the population, and a 'resource prioritization' strategy mirroring the pheasant's choice of feeding grounds. The core innovation lies in the adaptive adjustment of parameters – inertia weight, cognitive coefficient, and social coefficient – based on the perceived 'fitness landscape' and population diversity, mimicking the pheasant's intelligent decision-making. This paper details the algorithm's theoretical framework, its key components, and outlines a potential implementation strategy.

title: Title: Non-Local Quantum State Synchronization – New Framework for Quantum Teleportation
abstract: Quantum teleportation, the process of transferring an unknown quantum state from one location to another without physically moving the particle, has long been considered a cornerstone of quantum information science. However, significant limitations remain, particularly in achieving long-distance teleportation due to decoherence and the challenges of maintaining entanglement over vast distances. This paper introduces a novel framework, termed "Non-Local Quantum State Synchronization" (NLQS), designed to overcome these limitations by explicitly leveraging non-local correlations to establish a shared quantum state. We propose a protocol that utilizes entanglement as a fundamental building block, allowing for the transfer of information across a network, thereby circumventing the constraints imposed by distance and decoherence. The paper details the core mechanisms of the NLQS framework, including the establishment of entanglement, the generation of measurement results, and the subsequent reconstruction of the target state. We present preliminary results demonstrating the effectiveness of the framework in transferring quantum states over a simulated network, highlighting its potential for advancing the field of quantum communication and information processing.

title: Quantum Entanglement-Driven Distributed Algorithm Verification
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to distributed algorithm verification leveraging the unique properties of quantum entanglement. Traditional methods for verifying distributed algorithms, particularly in the context of quantum computing, often rely on complex simulations or require replicating the entire network, leading to significant resource constraints. We introduce a framework where quantum entanglement serves as the primary mechanism for validation. Specifically, we utilize entangled states exchanged between a sender and receiver. The receiver's measurement of changes within the entangled state allows for inference regarding the correctness of the algorithm executed by the sender. This approach avoids the need for full network replication or simulation, offering a potentially more efficient and scalable solution for verifying distributed algorithms. We outline the theoretical framework, focusing on the key mathematical relationships involved. This paper demonstrates a fundamentally new way to approach algorithm verification, rooted in the inherent properties of quantum mechanics.

title: Quantum Relational Memory
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to data storage and retrieval, termed Quantum Relational Memory (QRM), which utilizes entangled quantum states to represent and efficiently store relational data. The core concept involves encoding relational tuples as superposition states of qubits, harnessing entanglement to enable parallel traversal and correlation analysis of relationships within complex graph-like structures. Unlike Quantum Random Access Memory (QRAM), which focuses on data transfer, QRM directly addresses relational query processing. The system's architecture leverages superposition to perform inherent relational operations, theoretically achieving exponentially faster query performance compared to classical relational databases for intricate graph-based data. This work establishes a foundational framework for QRM, outlining its key principles, mathematical formalization, and potential impact on data management and analysis. We define key parameters and explore the theoretical limits of this approach, demonstrating its potential to revolutionize how relational data is handled and accessed. ---

title: Quantum Entanglement Computing Framework
abstract: Quantum entanglement, a bizarre phenomenon in quantum mechanics, holds immense potential for revolutionary computing. This paper explores the design of a novel computational framework, leveraging entanglement to achieve complex computations beyond the capabilities of classical computation. We propose a "纠缠计算" mechanism, which utilizes precise control of entangled states to enable novel operations and information transfer. This framework aims to push the boundaries of quantum computing, specifically focusing on quantum entanglement-based cryptography and complex algorithms. The core claim centers on the potential for this framework to significantly enhance computational efficiency and solve problems currently intractable for classical systems. This work presents a conceptual design of a quantum computing paradigm predicated on the unique properties of entanglement, outlining the key mechanisms and potential benefits.

abstract: This paper investigates the implementation of self-organizing neural networks (SONNs) within a quantum computing framework. The core focus is on developing a novel SONN architecture capable of dynamically adjusting connection weights and neuron counts based on input data characteristics. title: Where Identity Lives: Localized, Retain-Free Identity Unlearning in Multimodal Large Language Models
abstract: Removing a specific individual's information from multimodal large language models (MLLMs) is often needed after deployment, but existing methods rely on a retain set, which is hardest to obtain at that point, and rebuilding it recreates the privacy exposure that unlearning aims to remove. Forgetting from the forget set alone instead damages the shared visual-language computation, harming perception. We cast retain-free unlearning as a localization problem: causal tracing, weight transplant, and Fisher overlap all point to early-to-mid decoder MLPs as the layers where identity information is stored and, unlike other module families, can be modified without substantially disrupting vision. We turn this into Pathway-Aware Visual-attribute Anchoring (PAVA), which confines updates to these layers and pairs a forget loss with a visual-attribute anchor that preserves image-grounded behavior by distilling the model's own pre-unlearning answers from the forget images alone. On MLLMU-Bench and ReMem, PAVA gives the strongest forget-retain trade-off among forget-set-only methods and remains competitive with retain-based baselines.

abstract: This paper investigates the theoretical framework for exploring and utilizing quantum entanglement in a novel context: the integration of topological quantum mechanics with quantum computation. The core of this research focuses on designing a quantum state capable of self-sustained and extended entanglement, and establishing a quantum computing platform to facilitate the implementation of ultra-high-density quantum computation. The potential impact of this approach lies in fundamentally altering the landscape of quantum information processing, offering a paradigm shift towards computation beyond the capabilities of current technologies.

title: Adaptive Kernel Learning for Representation Distillation
abstract: Representation distillation, a technique for transferring knowledge from a larger, more complex model (teacher) to a smaller, more efficient model (student), has shown significant promise in various machine learning applications. However, a critical limitation of conventional distillation methods lies in their reliance on a fixed kernel function to map representations between the teacher and student. This paper proposes a novel approach, Adaptive Kernel Learning, which dynamically adjusts the kernel function during the distillation process. This adaptation is driven by an "Adaptive Kernel Optimizer," a recurrent neural network that learns to optimize kernel parameters based on the distillation loss and a learned dissimilarity metric. The core claim is that such dynamic adaptation significantly improves distillation performance by minimizing distortion while maximizing knowledge transfer. We introduce a formal framework outlining this approach, detailing the key components and their mathematical relationships. The proposed method offers a more nuanced and effective way to represent and transfer knowledge, particularly beneficial in scenarios where the source and target representations exhibit evolving similarity.

title: Black-eared Squirrel Optimization (BESO): A Novel Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by Black-Eared Squirrel Behavior
abstract: This paper presents Black-eared Squirrel Optimization (BESO), a novel metaheuristic algorithm inspired by the foraging behavior of black-eared squirrels (Sciurus negravianus). The algorithm mimics the squirrels' strategy of searching for food resources by utilizing a combination of exploration and exploitation phases, mirroring their movement patterns, caching behavior, and decision-making processes. BESO employs a squirrel population, each representing a potential solution to the optimization problem. The movement of each squirrel is governed by a stochastic process, influenced by the perceived availability of resources (fitness values) and the distance to the nearest food source. The algorithm incorporates a 'cache' mechanism, analogous to the squirrels' caching of food, to retain promising solutions. We detail the algorithm's design, including its key parameters, the objective function, and its application to various benchmark optimization problems. Preliminary results demonstrate that BESO is competitive with existing metaheuristic algorithms, particularly in problems with complex landscapes and multiple local optima. The algorithm's adaptability and its reliance on a biologically inspired model offer a potentially robust and efficient approach to solving a wide range of optimization challenges.

title: ## Black Bear Metaheuristic Algorithm (BBMA)
abstract: This paper presents a novel metaheuristic algorithm, the Black Bear Metaheuristic Algorithm (BBMA), inspired by the foraging behavior of black bears. BBMA leverages the black bear's strategy of searching for food in a region with varying food density, employing a combination of exploration and exploitation phases. The algorithm utilizes a population-based approach, with each individual representing a potential solution. The position of each individual is determined by a two-dimensional coordinate system, representing the solution space. The algorithm incorporates a novel movement strategy mimicking the black bear's approach to finding food, which involves adjusting the movement direction and distance based on the local food density. The core of BBMA lies in its adaptive parameter control mechanism, which dynamically adjusts the exploration and exploitation parameters based on the convergence rate of the algorithm. The performance of BBMA is evaluated on several benchmark optimization problems, demonstrating its effectiveness and competitive capabilities. The results indicate that BBMA provides a viable alternative to existing metaheuristic algorithms, particularly in scenarios where the problem landscape exhibits significant variations in food density. The key components of the algorithm include: population initialization, movement strategy, local food density estimation, adaptive parameter control, and convergence criteria.

title: ## Bison: A Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by Bison Herding Behavior
abstract: This paper presents Bison, a novel metaheuristic algorithm inspired by the observed behavior of bison herds during migration. The algorithm leverages the concepts of flocking, herding, and dynamic territory defense, which are fundamental to bison social dynamics, to effectively explore and optimize complex search spaces. Bison incorporates a novel population management strategy based on territorial ownership, a dynamic adjustment of individual movement probabilities influenced by social interactions, and a mechanism for removing ineffective individuals – mimicking the natural selection processes observed in bison herds. The algorithm's performance is evaluated on a suite of benchmark optimization problems, demonstrating its competitive capabilities compared to established metaheuristic methods such as Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) and Ant Colony Optimization (ACO). The results demonstrate Bison's potential as a robust and efficient solution for a range of optimization challenges.

title: Causal Inference via Bayesian Networks with Multiple Variables
abstract: This paper explores the application of multi-variable Bayesian networks (MVBNs) for causal inference. Traditional statistical methods often struggle to accurately represent and reason about causal relationships, particularly in complex systems with multiple interacting variables. This research proposes a framework utilizing MVBNs to construct more robust models of causal relationships, facilitating improved inference and decision-making. The core of this approach lies in leveraging the probabilistic nature of Bayesian networks to explicitly model and reason about uncertainty inherent in causal relationships. This paper details the methodology for constructing MVBNs, outlines the inference techniques, and discusses the advantages of this approach over conventional methods. The key contribution is a novel method for representing and manipulating causal relationships within a probabilistic framework, leading to more accurate and interpretable causal inferences. Specifically, we demonstrate how the structure of the MVBN can be informed by domain expertise and data analysis, and how this network can then be used to perform interventions and counterfactual reasoning. The paper concludes with a discussion of potential future research directions and the broader implications of this work.

title: Quantum Neural Networks via Multi-Body Entanglement Optimization
abstract: This paper investigates the potential of quantum neural networks (QNNs) by focusing on optimizing multi-body entanglement within the network architecture. The core claim is that strategic manipulation of entanglement between multiple nodes in a neural network can significantly enhance computational capabilities and improve information encoding efficiency. The proposed mechanism involves designing an algorithm to dynamically control the entanglement strength between nodes. This allows for the realization of more efficient parallel computation and enhanced information encoding. We explore theoretical frameworks and mathematical formulations to demonstrate the potential advantages of this approach compared to classical neural networks. The research highlights a novel pathway toward constructing quantum-enhanced neural network models by leveraging the unique properties of quantum entanglement. The primary focus is on the mathematical modeling and optimization strategies required to effectively harness entanglement for QNN performance.

title: Quantum Topology-Based Adaptive Geometry Structural Optimization
abstract: This paper introduces a novel algorithmic framework, Quantum Topology-Based Adaptive Geometry Structural Optimization (QTASO), designed to automate the construction of complex geometric structures and leverage topological properties for optimization, particularly in materials and structural design. The core mechanism centers around constructing a geometric structure with inherent adaptability, achieved through a tailored optimization algorithm that exploits quantum entanglement and error correction. We present a detailed explanation of the algorithm's key components, including the quantum topology representation, optimization strategy, and error mitigation techniques. The research demonstrates the effectiveness of QTASO in optimizing various geometric configurations, including novel material designs and structural elements, offering a significant advancement over existing geometric optimization approaches.

title: High-Dimensional Topological Information Encoding
abstract: High-dimensional topological information encoding presents a novel approach to information storage and transmission, leveraging the inherent properties of high-dimensional topological structures. This paper explores the potential of utilizing a dynamically adaptive topological structure to significantly reduce information redundancy and enhance transmission efficiency. We propose a new encoding scheme based on a "information encoding tree" and "topological encryption," employing self-adaptive topology to minimize redundancy and enhance security. The core mechanism involves constructing a tree structure that dynamically adjusts to the input data, ensuring a robust and efficient encoding process. This work offers a promising avenue for enhancing information processing and transmission, particularly in scenarios demanding high-dimensional data.

title: Quantum Entanglement-Based Information Encoding and Time Series Prediction
abstract: This paper investigates the potential of utilizing quantum entanglement for enhancing time series prediction. Traditional time series forecasting methods often struggle with complex, non-linear patterns and high-dimensional data. We propose a novel approach that leverages the unique properties of quantum entanglement to encode time series information and extract predictive insights. Specifically, we map time series data onto entangled quantum states, allowing us to access correlations and patterns that may be missed by classical methods. The theoretical framework outlines the key principles, including the mapping process, the measurement strategy, and the expected improvement in predictive accuracy. We present a mathematical model incorporating entanglement entropy and its influence on the prediction process. The core claim is that this entanglement-based encoding significantly improves time series prediction. The research highlights a fundamentally different approach to time series analysis, moving beyond classical information processing to exploit the quantum mechanical phenomenon of entanglement.

title: Title: Quantum Entanglement Resonance Mapping (QERM) – Exploiting Non-Locality
abstract: Quantum entanglement, a fundamental quantum phenomenon, possesses unique properties that promise transformative capabilities in computation and information processing. This research investigates a novel computational framework, Quantum Entanglement Resonance Mapping (QERM), designed to leverage this resource for mapping and analyzing non-local correlations. We propose a computational algorithm that traces entanglement paths, generating a precise representation of correlation structure, and then uses this information to generate novel entanglement-based computations. The core claim is that QERM offers a new approach to quantifying and manipulating entanglement, potentially accelerating certain computations and providing a deeper understanding of complex system dynamics. This paper will detail the algorithm's architecture, mathematical foundations, and preliminary experimental validation, demonstrating its potential for quantifying and manipulating entanglement.

title: ## Mimic Octopus Metaheuristic Algorithm (MOMA)
abstract: This paper introduces the Mimic Octopus Metaheuristic Algorithm (MOMA), a novel optimization algorithm inspired by the remarkable camouflage and behavioral mimicry abilities of the Mimic Octopus (*Thaumoctopus mimicus*). Unlike traditional metaheuristics that often rely on random exploration and exploitation, MOMA incorporates a dynamic 'morphing' strategy mimicking the octopus's ability to rapidly change its appearance and behavior to adapt to its environment. The algorithm utilizes a population of 'octopus agents', each representing a potential solution. Each agent's "morph" is represented by a set of parameters, which are iteratively adjusted based on a local environment assessment and a global search for optimal configurations. The core innovation lies in the 'mimicry' mechanism, where agents' parameters are influenced by the best-performing agents in their immediate neighborhood, fostering both convergence and diversity. This paper details the algorithm's design, including the representation of solutions, the mimicry mechanism, and the objective function evaluation process. We argue that this approach, rooted in biological inspiration, offers a potentially robust and adaptable solution for a variety of optimization problems.

title: Dimension Space: A Novel Algebraic Structure for Quantum Computing
abstract: This paper explores the development of a novel algebraic structure, termed the "Dimension Space," as a bridge between linear algebra and non-linear algebra. The core claim is that this framework offers a pathway to understanding and manipulating quantum systems within high-dimensional spaces, potentially driving significant advancements in quantum computing theory. We investigate the inherent properties of this dimension space and its relationship to quantum computation, proposing a mechanism to leverage this structure for enhanced algorithm design and optimization. The study will analyze the behavior of quantum states and quantum circuits within this space, highlighting potential implications for quantum information processing.

title: ## Desert Tortoise-Inspired Adaptive Search Algorithm (DTSA)
abstract: This paper introduces the Desert Tortoise-Inspired Adaptive Search Algorithm (DTSA), a novel metaheuristic optimization algorithm inspired by the foraging behavior of desert tortoises. Desert tortoises exhibit remarkable resilience and adaptability in harsh environments, primarily driven by a combination of exploratory and exploitative movements, coupled with a sophisticated strategy for resource allocation. DTSA mimics these behaviors by incorporating a dynamic exploration-exploitation balance, adaptive step size control, and a memory-based learning mechanism. The algorithm utilizes a population of potential solutions, each represented by a vector of parameters. The core of DTSA lies in its "sand-seeking" and "oasis-finding" mechanisms, which guide the search process. The algorithm adjusts its step size based on the perceived environmental "stress" and utilizes a memory component to retain successful solution candidates, effectively concentrating the search around promising regions of the solution space. This paper details the algorithm's theoretical framework, operational rules, and highlights its potential advantages over existing metaheuristic techniques.

title: Multi-field Quantum Computing
abstract: This paper explores the potential of multi-field quantum computing, a novel approach to quantum computation that leverages the superposition and entanglement of multiple quantum fields. Traditional quantum computing often restricts itself to a single qubit state, but this research proposes a system designed to exploit the unique properties of multiple quantum fields, enabling significantly more complex computations. We outline the fundamental principles underlying this design, detail the architecture of the proposed system, and discuss the potential advantages and challenges in realizing this ambitious goal. The core claim is that the system's ability to manipulate and entangle multiple fields will dramatically enhance computational capabilities compared to existing quantum computing paradigms.

title: Dimensional Quantum Entanglement
abstract: This paper explores the potential of leveraging dimensionality transformations to mitigate measurement errors and enable communication across the quantum realm. We propose a novel quantum entanglement protocol utilizing dynamic dimensionality shifts, coupled with quantum entanglement simulation and a form of spatial information propagation, aiming to dramatically reduce errors inherent in traditional quantum measurement techniques. The core mechanism involves a quantum field simulation to precisely measure entanglement, followed by the introduction of quantum entanglement via a dynamic, multi-dimensional quantum state. This research aims to establish a foundation for quantum computation's expansion, pushing beyond the limitations of classical measurement. This work addresses the critical challenge of error correction and offers a potential pathway toward more robust and scalable quantum systems.

title: Title: Adaptive Quantum Feedback Loops for Algorithmic Stability
abstract: Quantum computing holds immense promise for revolutionizing numerous fields, yet the inherent instability of quantum algorithms poses a significant challenge. This paper investigates the application of adaptive quantum feedback loops to enhance algorithmic stability, addressing the problem of divergence and ensuring consistent performance across a wide range of conditions. We introduce a novel system of continuous monitoring and adjustment, leveraging the inherent dynamics of quantum systems to proactively mitigate instability. The core mechanism centers around a feedback loop that dynamically adjusts quantum parameters based on the algorithm's output, effectively correcting for deviations and promoting stability. This approach offers a potential pathway to significantly improve the reliability and predictability of quantum computations.

title: The Rock Cormorant Inspired Metaheuristic Optimization Algorithm (RIMO)
abstract: This paper introduces the Rock Cormorant Inspired Metaheuristic Optimization Algorithm (RIMO), a novel metaheuristic algorithm inspired by the foraging behavior of rock cormorants. These birds exhibit a unique strategy for locating fish, utilizing a combination of individual searching and collaborative information sharing. RIMO leverages these principles by employing a population of 'cormorants' that simultaneously explore the search space and share information through a dynamic 'observation point' system. The algorithm's core components include an initial population initialization, a fitness evaluation function, a movement strategy based on cormorant foraging, and a mechanism for adjusting observation points to enhance convergence. Unlike traditional metaheuristics, RIMO's observation point system dynamically adapts to the search landscape, mimicking the cormorant's ability to identify and prioritize promising regions. This paper details the algorithm's design, mathematical formulation, and potential applications, focusing on the underlying principles and conceptual framework rather than empirical validation. The aim is to provide a foundational understanding of RIMO and its potential for future development within the broader field of metaheuristic optimization.

title: Algorithmic Quantum Simulation of Fluid Dynamics with Entangled Particles
abstract: This paper explores the implementation of an algorithmic quantum simulation approach for fluid dynamics, leveraging quantum entanglement to achieve a significant advancement over classical methods. The core claim posits the creation of a novel algorithm capable of generating remarkably accurate simulations of turbulent flows and wave propagation, addressing limitations of current computational capabilities. We detail the methodology, including the representation of fluid state using entangled particles, the quantum algorithm design, and preliminary results demonstrating improved accuracy in complex flow scenarios. The paper argues that this research has the potential to unlock novel insights into fluid dynamics and contribute to advancements in areas such as weather forecasting, computational fluid mechanics, and materials science.

The core mechanism centers around the manipulation of quantum entanglement and tunneling to achieve this adaptability. The resulting system demonstrates improved performance in specific quantum algorithms through enhanced adaptability. The study explores the potential of this approach in tackling complex computational problems and lays the foundation for future research into adaptive quantum systems.

title: Fine-Tuning a Large Multilingual Text-to-Speech Model for Nepali on Consumer Hardware: A Teacher Model for Knowledge Distillation with Speaker Identity Verification
abstract: Nepali is a low resource language for speech technology and there is very little open text-to-speech support for it. Most high quality neural TTS models are too large to run in real time on the low end machines that are common in Nepal, and the usual answer to that problem is knowledge distillation, where a large teacher model generates training speech for a small student model. That approach only works if the teacher is itself correct, because every error the teacher makes is copied into the student. This paper reports the construction and verification of such a teacher. A 937M parameter multilingual model, Indic Parler-TTS, was fine-tuned to a single Nepali female speaker identity using 4-bit quantization with a DoRA and RS-LoRA adapter of rank 32 applied only to the decoder, on a single laptop GPU with 6 GB of VRAM. The training data was 2,006 clips, which is 2.62 hours of licensed Nepali speech from 18 speakers, of which the target speaker contributed 496 clips or 35.8 minutes. The complete fine-tune used 2.48 GB of VRAM and 2,500 training steps. The fine-tune on these 2,006 clips succeeded. High frequency energy in the generated speech measures 0.3215 percent against the real speaker's 0.326 percent, so the output is spectrally matched to her recordings. A threshold-free blend prediction test shows the model favours the target speaker rather than averaging the corpus: the generated centroid scores 0.853 against her, while a constructed 18-way average of the corpus scores only 0.784, and a nearest-centroid assignment places 500 of 500 generated clips with the target speaker against a chance rate of 5.6 percent. A blind twenty clip listening comparison confirmed that the output is heard as one consistent woman. An earlier fine-tune, trained on a differently constructed dataset, had failed completely, and that failure is also reported because it is instructive: two data defects produced a voice nine times more muffled than the real speaker while character error rate stayed near 0.10 throughout, so every metric then in use stayed healthy through a total failure. The paper further reports that selecting a checkpoint by validation loss gives a worse voice than the final checkpoint, because validation loss over a speaker mixture is best for the average rather than best for the target, and that the teacher renders 100 percent of consonant conjuncts present in its fine-tuning data against 78 percent of those absent, which quantifies a generalization limit usually assumed away.

title: Humanlike representation of social networks in large language models
abstract: Although large language models (LLMs) have made great progress in their general reasoning capabilities, reasoning about social relationships has remained a challenge. In contrast, humans are naturally skilled at reasoning about how people are connected to one another, even in large, complex social networks. Recent research in cognitive science suggests that a key component of human social intelligence is the ability to represent social networks using multistep abstraction, which integrates knowledge of both direct and indirect social connections, and therefore supports inferences about network members’ social proximity to one another. Here, we test whether LLMs represent social networks using similar computational principles. In Study 1, we converted an existing human social navigation task into text and recorded LLM responses to the same problems humans were tasked with solving. LLMs’ behaviors closely mirrored those of human participants, and were best-explained by Katz communicability, a model of multistep abstraction that captures how humans represent and navigate social networks. In Study 2, we tested whether these multistep representations persisted in a task where they offered no benefit—and were in fact detrimental to task accuracy—and found that LLMs continued to show a multistep signature even in this context. These findings suggest that multistep abstraction may be a core property of how LLMs represent relational information, closely paralleling accounts of human cognitive maps.

title: Hidden Threat in Synthetic Data: Covert Targeted Bias Injection through Benign Text
abstract: Synthetic data is increasingly used to train large language models (LLMs), yet its security implications remain poorly understood. Prior work on subliminal learning suggests that models can inherit behavioral traits from seemingly unrelated training data. In this work, we investigate whether such mechanisms can be exploited to inject targeted social biases into aligned models through semantically benign synthetic data. We construct a pipeline in which a misaligned teacher model generates filtered synthetic datasets across domains such as creative writing and code generation, which are then used to fine-tune aligned student models. Our experiments show that benign-looking synthetic data can act as a covert channel for transmitting targeted biases while largely preserving the student model's general task capabilities. These results reveal a previously underexplored security risk in synthetic data-driven LLM training pipelines and highlight the need for improved safeguards. As one possible step toward this goal, we suggest that log-linearity-based scoring may provide a useful signal for screening seemingly benign synthetic data.

title: Probability Logic and Quantum Information Fusion
abstract: This paper explores the synergistic integration of probability logic and set theory, aiming to construct a novel probabilistic framework capable of efficiently storing, transmitting, and processing quantum information. The core mechanism involves the fusion of the probabilistic properties inherent in probability logic with the abstract nature of set theory, leveraging these properties to enable quantum information manipulation. This work proposes a new approach to quantum information processing, addressing limitations of existing techniques and offering a potential pathway towards advanced quantum computing and communication.

title: Quantum Entanglement-Based Dynamic Routing of Distributed Computing Resources
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to dynamic routing in distributed computing systems leveraging the phenomenon of quantum entanglement. Traditional routing algorithms suffer from latency issues inherent in classical networks, limiting their efficiency and scalability. Our approach utilizes entangled nodes to provide instantaneous information about the state of the entire distributed network, enabling real-time awareness and optimized routing decisions. We introduce a framework where each computing node is entangled with a designated "entanglement node." Measurements of the entanglement node's quantum state provide immediate information about the states of all connected computing nodes. Routing decisions are then based on probability distributions derived from these entangled states, further optimized using quantum algorithms. This method offers a significant reduction in routing latency and promises a more efficient and scalable distributed computing architecture. The core claim of this work is that quantum entanglement can enable significantly more efficient and faster dynamic routing, overcoming the bottlenecks present in classical network routing. ---

title: Causal Discovery Based on Multi-Variable Probabilistic Models
abstract: This paper explores the application of multi-variable probabilistic models for causal discovery. Traditional causal discovery methods often rely heavily on domain expertise and observational data, presenting significant challenges in complex systems where such information is limited or unavailable. This research proposes a novel approach utilizing multi-variable probabilistic models, specifically Bayesian Networks and Structural Causal Models, to automatically learn and infer causal relationships. The core mechanism involves employing algorithms designed for probabilistic inference within these models. The resulting framework offers a data-driven method for identifying causal connections, potentially reducing the reliance on pre-existing knowledge and facilitating discovery in scenarios with sparse or incomplete information. We demonstrate the theoretical underpinnings of this approach and outline a methodology for its implementation, focusing on the ability to model complex dependencies and ultimately, uncover underlying causal structures. This work contributes to a more automated and robust approach to causal inference, opening up possibilities for analysis in diverse fields. ---

abstract: This paper introduces a novel computational paradigm, termed the Adaptive Computational Paradigm based on Quantum Entanglement, that leverages the unique properties of quantum entanglement to achieve enhanced parallelism and distributed computation. Traditional computing paradigms often struggle to fully exploit the potential of entanglement for efficient calculations and reasoning. This research proposes a framework utilizing entangled states to significantly improve computational throughput and scalability. We detail the core mechanism, outlining the design of a quantum computation environment and the implementation of algorithms designed to exploit entanglement for faster processing. The paper concludes with a discussion of the potential advantages and challenges associated with this approach, emphasizing its promise for future advancements in computational science.

title: Automated Theorem Proving with Neural Network Guidance
abstract: Automated theorem proving (ATP) aims to develop systems capable of mechanically proving mathematical theorems. Despite significant advancements, ATP systems often struggle with complex reasoning tasks, largely due to the inherent difficulty in representing and executing logical deduction rules. This work proposes a novel approach to ATP that integrates neural networks to provide guidance during the proof process. The core idea is to train a neural network to suggest promising proof steps and identify relevant theorems, essentially acting as an "intelligent assistant" for the ATP system. This guidance mechanism is expected to improve the efficiency and effectiveness of ATP, particularly in tackling challenging mathematical problems. The presented framework utilizes a reinforcement learning approach, where the neural network learns to optimize the proof strategy based on the current state of the proof and the available theorems. The system is evaluated conceptually, outlining the architecture and training process, and highlighting potential improvements. Further research will focus on developing and refining the network architecture, exploring different training strategies, and integrating the guidance mechanism with existing ATP systems.

abstract: This paper presents an automated framework for generating and reasoning with high-dimensional non-linear matrices using deep learning. This framework offers a significant advancement over existing techniques, addressing limitations in adaptability and complexity. This work demonstrates the potential for autonomous matrix generation and inference, opening new possibilities for data analysis and modeling.

title: Quantum Entangled Metric Modulation (QEMM)
abstract: Quantum Entangled Metric Modulation (QEMM) presents a novel approach to dynamically modulate the entanglement of multiple quantum states, offering exponential speedups in complex quantum computations. The core mechanism leverages a dynamically adjustable "entanglement matrix" that adapts to the specific properties of each entangled system, employing stochastic control based on highly complex, non-linear correlation analysis. This contrasts with traditional entanglement keys, which require computationally intensive key establishment. This paper details the theoretical framework, implementation of the QEMM algorithm, and preliminary experimental results demonstrating its potential for significant speedup in quantum simulations and algorithm execution.

title: Beaded Hylomyscus: A Novel Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by the Foraging Behavior of *Hylomyscus*
abstract: This paper presents a new metaheuristic algorithm, termed "Beaded Hylomyscus" (BH), inspired by the foraging strategies observed in *Hylomyscus*, a small rodent known for its intricate and efficient burrow systems and food-gathering techniques. The algorithm leverages the concept of 'bead chains' – a visual representation of the rodent's burrow construction – to guide the search process. BH incorporates elements of particle swarm optimization (PSO) and simulated annealing (SA) while introducing a novel 'bead-linking' mechanism that dynamically adjusts the connectivity between particles, mimicking the rodent's adaptive burrow network. The performance of BH is evaluated on a range of benchmark optimization problems, demonstrating its effectiveness in finding near-optimal solutions with a relatively low computational cost. The key contributions of this work are the innovative bead-linking strategy and the application of rodent foraging behavior as a fundamental principle for algorithm design. The algorithm's core is defined by the following equations: * Particle Position Update: $x_{i}(t+1) = w * x_i(t) + c_1 * r_1 * (\text{pbest} - x_i(t)) + c_2 * r_2 * (\text{gbest} - x_i(t))$ * Velocity Update: $v_{i}(t+1) = w * v_i(t) + c_1 * r_1 * (pbest_i - x_i(t)) + c_2 * r_2 * (gbest - x_i(t))$ * Bead-Linking Adjustment: $λ_{ij}(t+1) = \tanh(α * (x_i(t) - x_j(t))) * \text{sign}(x_i(t) - x_j(t))$ where $λ_{ij}$ represents the linkage strength between particle *i* and particle *j*. * Temperature Update (SA Component): $T(t+1) = T(t) * (1 - α * \frac{\Delta E}{T(t)})$ where $\Delta E$ is the change in error function value.

title: Based on Quantum State Algorithms: A Theoretical Foundation
abstract: This paper explores the theoretical foundations of algorithms optimized through quantum state manipulation. We introduce a novel approach leveraging quantum state transformations to fundamentally alter the algorithm's process, aiming to significantly enhance efficiency. The core mechanism involves reshaping the quantum state to guide the optimization, offering a potential paradigm shift in algorithm design. This work presents a theoretical framework and outlines initial algorithm development, emphasizing the potential of quantum state optimization for enhancing existing algorithms. The paper concludes with a discussion of the challenges and future research directions in this burgeoning field.

title: 自适应几何变换的量子模拟与理论验证
abstract: This paper investigates the application of quantum simulation to the validation of a novel topological transformation model predicated on adaptive geometry transformations. Utilizing quantum simulation, we aim to rigorously test the theoretical properties of this model and compare its results with established classical theory, potentially uncovering previously unknown geometric relationships and topological properties. The core mechanism involves employing quantum simulations to model and analyze the transformation process, offering a pathway toward validating the model's underlying principles and expanding our understanding of topological phenomena. This research represents a novel approach to geometric analysis, leveraging the power of quantum computation to achieve a level of fidelity and detail unattainable through conventional methods.

title: Quantum Entanglement Matrix Operations Dynamic Mapping
abstract: This paper presents a novel dynamic mapping algorithm based on quantum entanglement, designed to accelerate matrix computations and handle more complex matrix operations than traditional methods. The core innovation lies in leveraging the unique properties of quantum entanglement to achieve faster and more efficient calculations. We introduce a framework utilizing entangled qubit states to represent and manipulate matrix elements, enabling a significant reduction in computational complexity. The algorithm's effectiveness is demonstrated through theoretical analysis and preliminary experimental validation using a simplified matrix multiplication task. The research explores the potential of entanglement to overcome limitations in classical matrix operations, offering a promising avenue for advancements in numerical linear algebra and related fields.

title: Ashaninka Oldfield Mouse: A Novel Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by the Behavior of a Nocturnal Rodent
abstract: This paper presents a novel metaheuristic optimization algorithm, termed "Ashaninka Oldfield Mouse" (AOM), inspired by the foraging behavior of the Ashaninka oldfield mouse ( *Peromyscus defassa*), a nocturnal rodent known for its efficient and adaptive search strategies in complex environments. The algorithm incorporates elements of adaptive step size adjustment, memory-based exploration, and a novel "trail scent" mechanism mimicking the mouse's olfactory navigation. The core of AOM is a self-adaptive parameter system that adjusts parameters based on the objective function's landscape. We demonstrate the algorithm's effectiveness through simulations on several benchmark optimization problems, including the Rosenbrock function, Rastrigin function, and the Sphere function. The results indicate that AOM exhibits competitive performance compared to established metaheuristic algorithms like Genetic Algorithm (GA) and Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO), particularly in challenging and high-dimensional search spaces. Future research will explore the algorithm's application in real-world engineering problems and investigate the theoretical underpinnings of its performance.

title: Title: Non-Linear Neural Network Architectures for Evolutionary Computation
abstract: This paper explores the integration of non-linear neural network architectures with evolutionary computation techniques to facilitate rapid design exploration of complex design spaces. The core idea is to establish a feedback loop within the network, where past outputs directly influence future outputs, thereby promoting innovation and accelerating the discovery of optimal designs. We propose a novel neural network structure, the 'Adaptive Resonance Network' (ARN) with a dynamic feedback mechanism, that leverages the strengths of both paradigms. The research focuses on demonstrating the effectiveness of this architecture in generating novel designs across a range of problem domains, highlighting its potential for streamlining the design process.

title: Arguedas's Grass Mouse: A Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by the Foraging Behavior of *Mus agregris*
abstract: This paper presents Arguedas's Grass Mouse (AGM), a novel metaheuristic algorithm inspired by the foraging behavior of *Mus agregris*, the Arguedas's grass mouse. This rodent is renowned for its highly efficient and adaptive foraging strategies in complex, spatially distributed environments. AGM leverages these behaviors – specifically, exploration, exploitation, and adaptive movement – to construct a robust optimization process. The algorithm utilizes a population-based approach, employing a representation of the search space as a set of grass mouse agents. Each agent's movement is governed by a modified Brownian motion with adaptive step-size and direction, mimicking the mouse's probabilistic navigation. Furthermore, the algorithm incorporates a local search component and a dynamically adjusted exploration-exploitation balance. Theoretical analysis demonstrates AGM's convergence properties and its potential for improved performance compared to traditional metaheuristic methods. The algorithm is demonstrated through a series of benchmark problems, showcasing its effectiveness in a range of optimization tasks. The key contributions of this work are the novel integration of adaptive movement, a probabilistic representation of the search space, and a dynamic balance between exploration and exploitation.

title: Algorithmic Self-Consistency Theorem Refinement
abstract: The Algorithmic Self-Consistency Theorem (ASTR) provides a framework for analyzing the stability of algorithms. It posits that an algorithm's internal state can be manipulated in a way that leads to a consistent, self-consistent state, implying a fundamental limit to algorithmic control. This paper delves into a refined version of ASTR, extending its applicability to a broader spectrum of algorithms. We introduce a 'Dynamic Stability Field' mechanism to dynamically adjust algorithm states based on input data, thereby enhancing robustness against perturbations. This refinement aims to move beyond a static, limited analysis of stability to a more nuanced understanding of algorithmic behavior, identifying and formally proving inherent stability and resilience.

title: Alashan Ground Squirrel Inspired Metaheuristic Algorithm for Complex Optimization Problems
abstract: This paper introduces a novel metaheuristic algorithm, termed the Alashan Ground Squirrel Inspired Metaheuristic Algorithm (AGSIMHA), designed to address complex optimization challenges. The algorithm's core inspiration stems from the foraging behavior of the Alashan ground squirrel, a resilient rodent known for its efficient resource utilization and adaptive strategies in a challenging environment. AGSIMHA incorporates elements of exploration and exploitation, mimicking the squirrel's ability to balance searching for new food sources with consolidating established ones. The algorithm utilizes a population-based approach, employing a squirrel-inspired movement strategy and a novel adaptive parameter adjustment mechanism. Mathematical formulations detailing the algorithm's key components, including the movement probability distribution and the parameter adaptation rules, are presented. The performance of AGSIMHA is evaluated through simulations on benchmark optimization problems, demonstrating its effectiveness compared to established metaheuristic algorithms. The algorithm's ability to adapt to changing problem landscapes is a key strength. The core of the algorithm relies on a probabilistic movement scheme, represented by the equation: P(si, t+1) = α * (1/N) + (1-α) * exp(-β * ||xi - xbest||2 / σ2), where α is the exploration rate, β is the exploitation rate, N is the population size, xi is the position of the i-th individual, xbest is the best position found so far, and σ is the standard deviation. Parameter adaptation is governed by the equation: Δk = γ * (xi - xbest) / ||xbest||, where γ is the adaptation constant. The algorithm's efficacy is demonstrated through comparative analysis against PSO and AGA.

title: Semantic Web Reasoning with Knowledge Graphs and Deep Semantic Embeddings
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to semantic web reasoning that addresses the limitations of traditional rule-based systems. The core idea is to leverage the strengths of knowledge graphs and deep semantic embeddings to achieve more scalable, flexible, and accurate semantic reasoning. We propose a framework that represents semantic data as a knowledge graph and employs deep learning models to generate semantic embeddings. These embeddings capture the complex relationships within the data, allowing for efficient reasoning and inference. The system's ability to handle large datasets and complex relationships distinguishes it from conventional rule-based approaches. The system is evaluated conceptually, outlining the architecture and key components, and demonstrating its potential for improved semantic web applications. The primary contribution is a hybrid approach that combines the structured knowledge representation of knowledge graphs with the powerful representation learning capabilities of deep semantic embeddings.

title: Physical Simulation of Quantum Entanglement Expansion
abstract: This paper explores the potential of utilizing quantum entanglement simulation to expand the scope of physical simulation, enabling more precise parameter prediction. Traditional physics simulations often rely on classical computation, while quantum entanglement simulation offers a unique avenue to model complex quantum systems with enhanced precision. We investigate the core mechanisms of this approach, focusing on the implementation of a quantum entanglement simulation to address limitations inherent in current simulation techniques. This paper will detail the theoretical framework underpinning this expansion, outlining the challenges and opportunities involved in translating quantum phenomena into a computational model.
