title: Prabhasa-BabyLM: Matched-Budget Tests of Paninian Structure in Small-Model Pretraining
abstract: Under a fixed pretraining budget, which inductive biases actually improve a small languagemodel, and which only appear to until they are tested against a matched control? Prabhasa-BabyLManswers this for Paninian morphosyntax through a controlled study on the BabyLM 2026 benchmark.Three mechanisms are tested: morpheme-boundary N-hot embeddings, karaka role-stratified masking,and a supervised role-prediction objective. Because Paninian parsers exist for Sanskrit and not for English, the deterministic mapping from Universal Dependencies relations to karaka roles thatsupplies every English label in this work is specified in full, situated against semantic role labelling, and measured for what it loses: only 68.3% of the subword positions the model sees carry the roleits own parse assigned. A 114M-parameter bidirectional encoder is trained on the Strict (100M-word) and Strict-Small (10M-word) budgets and every claim is tested with three to five seeds, pairedbootstrap inference, and Holm–Bonferroni correction. The Strict entry scores 74.56 BLiMP againsta GPT-2 baseline of 74.53 and stands third on the Strict track by Overall Average (45.21) at the timeof writing. The gains are attributable to the training objective, the architecture, the training budget,and completeness of evaluation coverage, not to the Paninian mechanisms. Pure masked languagemodelling is indistinguishable from a hybrid MLM+CLM objective at 10M words but exceeds it by5.49 points at 100M. At matched mask budget, karaka-stratified masking is causally inert, and the karaka auxiliary objective yields only +0.76 points over five seeds. The result is a controlled separationof the design choices that help at this scale from a linguistically motivated prior that does not.

title: AQ3D: Adaptive Query Transformer for 3D Instance Segmentation
abstract: Transformer-based decoders for 3D instance segmentation typically commit to a fixed number of queries and positional modeling calibrated on the training distribution rather than on the scene at hand. Indoor scans vary widely in spatial extent and object count, so a fixed query set over-initializes small scenes and under-initializes large ones, while learned absolute and relative encodings are bound to the training scenes' extents and can saturate. We present AQ3D, which is designed to handle scenes of various sizes during training and inference. Queries are instantiated at a fixed ratio of the scene's superpoints, forming an overcomplete set whose background rejection is entirely left to the decoder. Positional information is encoded using 3D RoPE over quantized metric coordinates, replacing learned bounded lookup tables of prior decoders. Further, we improve the decoder itself by using attribution-based superpoint pooling, a mask refinement branch, and a cosine classifier for background rejection. Experiments show our method sets a new state-of-the-art on validation and hidden test splits across the datasets ScanNetV2, ScanNet200, and ScanNet++V2 among decoder methods trained without additional data augmentation. Code is available at https://github.com/kenomo/aq3d{github.com/kenomo/aq3d}.

title: Quantum Topology Optimization: An Adaptive Optimization Approach
abstract: Quantum Topology Optimization (QTO) is a novel optimization technique based on the principles of quantum topology, offering a promising avenue for addressing complex optimization problems. This paper explores the application of QTO to optimize quantum systems, highlighting its unique capabilities and potential advantages over conventional optimization methods. We present a core mechanism utilizing quantum topology to dynamically adjust system parameters, leading to improved performance. The paper details the methodology, provides a conceptual overview of the underlying physics, and offers a preliminary assessment of the method's effectiveness through theoretical analysis and simulation. The core claim is that QTO provides a more precise and robust optimization approach, particularly for systems exhibiting intricate topological structures.

title: Quantum Entanglement Information Optimization Algorithm
abstract: Quantum entanglement, a bizarre phenomenon where two or more particles become linked and share the same fate regardless of the distance separating them, holds immense potential for revolutionizing computation. This paper explores the development of a novel optimization algorithm leveraging quantum entanglement to enhance the efficiency and stability of quantum computing. We propose a new approach that utilizes entanglement to facilitate complex computations, potentially unlocking new capabilities in quantum information processing. The core mechanism revolves around designing an algorithm that exploits the unique properties of entangled states to guide the optimization process, leading to improved results and a deeper understanding of quantum entanglement's role in computation. This work investigates both the theoretical foundations of this approach and preliminary experimental investigations into its potential impact.

title: Non-Local Quantum State Manipulation through Entanglement Tunneling
abstract: Quantum state manipulation represents a significant challenge in quantum computing and communication. Current methods, often reliant on classical communication, restrict the ability to transmit information across distances. This paper proposes a novel approach to quantum state manipulation leveraging entanglement tunneling – a mechanism where quantum states instantaneously transfer across distances, circumventing the limitations of local interactions. We detail a "Entanglement Tunneling Protocol" – a meticulously designed algorithm – that demonstrates the potential for instantaneous communication and control over quantum states, fundamentally altering the landscape of information transfer. The paper explores the theoretical foundations, algorithmic implementation, and preliminary experimental validation of this groundbreaking technique. The core claim is that entanglement tunneling offers a pathway towards long-distance quantum communication and control, opening doors to unprecedented capabilities.

title: Title: Dynamic Topology for Quantum State Reconstruction
abstract: Quantum state reconstruction is a fundamental challenge in quantum information processing, particularly when dealing with incomplete measurements. Traditional methods often struggle with large datasets and complex systems. This paper introduces Dynamic Topology for Quantum State Reconstruction (DTQSR), a novel approach leveraging a dynamic topology to intelligently adapt to measurement outcomes, thereby significantly enhancing the reconstruction process. We propose a system that iteratively refines the measurement process, employing a feedback loop driven by a topology optimization algorithm. This adaptive approach overcomes limitations of existing methods by providing a robust and efficient solution to reconstruct quantum states from incomplete data. The core mechanism focuses on dynamically adjusting the quantum state's topology to maximize information extraction, offering a promising path towards more reliable and scalable quantum state reconstruction. This work presents a complete theoretical framework and preliminary implementation demonstrating the effectiveness of DTQSR in reconstructing specific quantum states.

title: Probability Neural Networks: Adaptive Parameter Tuning for Enhanced Performance and Generalization
abstract: Probability Neural Networks (PNNs) represent a novel approach to neural network design, leveraging adaptive parameter tuning to optimize performance across diverse datasets. This paper introduces a novel PNN architecture predicated on a self-adaptive parameter adjustment mechanism, aiming to address the limitations of traditional parameter optimization techniques. We detail the design of the PNN, outlining the core algorithm and its implications for improved generalization. The paper explores the benefits of this approach, demonstrating its efficacy through a series of experiments across multiple datasets, showcasing a significant enhancement in performance compared to existing methods. The research highlights the potential of adaptive parameter adjustment to unlock the full potential of PNNs, particularly in scenarios with complex data distributions.

title: Probability Association Graph for Reinforcement Learning
abstract: This paper introduces a novel reinforcement learning model based on Probability Association Graphs (PAGs). Traditional reinforcement learning often struggles with effectively capturing the complex relationships between environment states and potential states, hindering learning efficiency and generalization. Our approach leverages the inherent structure of PAGs to reduce the difficulty of learning, especially in environments with intricate dependencies. We propose a framework that dynamically integrates information from the PAG, enabling agents to learn more robust and adaptable policies. The core mechanism focuses on employing a graph-based representation to improve the representation learning process and enhance the model's ability to generalize across diverse scenarios. We present preliminary results demonstrating the effectiveness of this approach, highlighting its potential for advancing reinforcement learning in challenging environments.

title: Recursive Fractal Resonance Network (RFRN)
abstract: This paper introduces the Recursive Fractal Resonance Network (RFRN), a novel self-organizing network architecture designed to leverage fractal patterns for optimized resonance and amplification. The RFRN operates on a meta-algorithm that iteratively generates fractal structures, dynamically adjusting their scale and complexity based on real-time data input. The core claim is that this approach fosters self-organization and optimization through a resonant feedback loop, leading to enhanced network functionality. We analyze the potential of RFRN across various application domains, demonstrating its ability to achieve significant improvements in performance and stability. This work presents a fundamentally new method for network design, moving beyond static architectures towards a dynamically responsive system.

title: Black-eared Rice Rat Inspired Metaheuristic Algorithm for Complex Optimization Problems
abstract: This paper presents a novel metaheuristic algorithm, termed the "Black-eared Rice Rat Algorithm" (BERRA), inspired by the foraging behavior of the black-eared rice rat (Neotoma megalopora). Rice rats are known for their efficient and adaptive foraging strategies, particularly their ability to exploit resources in complex and changing environments. The BERRA algorithm leverages these characteristics to develop a robust and effective solution approach for complex optimization problems. The algorithm incorporates key elements of rice rat foraging, including resource prioritization, adaptive exploration, and memory-based decision making. Specifically, the algorithm utilizes a novel representation of the search space based on resource availability and a dynamic adjustment of exploration and exploitation parameters. The performance of the BERRA algorithm is evaluated on a range of benchmark optimization problems, demonstrating its competitive ability compared to established metaheuristic algorithms such as the Genetic Algorithm (GA) and Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO). The algorithm's adaptability and efficiency make it a promising tool for tackling diverse optimization challenges. The core mathematical representation of the algorithm is detailed, outlining the key components and their interactions.

title: Adaptive Kernel Learning via Evolutionary Strategies
abstract: Support Vector Machines (SVMs) are powerful kernel-based classifiers, but their performance is highly sensitive to the choice of kernel function and its associated parameters. Traditional methods for kernel selection involve manual tuning, a time-consuming and often suboptimal process. This paper introduces a novel approach to adaptive kernel learning using evolutionary strategies. The core idea is to directly optimize the kernel function's parameters through an iterative evolutionary algorithm, guided by a differentiable reward function derived from SVM performance. This eliminates the need for manual tuning and allows the algorithm to explore a wider range of kernel configurations. We define a population of kernel functions, each characterized by its parameters, and employ an evolutionary algorithm to select and evolve the best-performing kernels. The algorithm's fitness function is based on the SVM's accuracy on a given dataset. The key contribution lies in the automated kernel learning process and the efficient exploration of the kernel parameter space. This approach offers a potentially significant improvement in SVM performance compared to traditional methods, especially for complex datasets.

title: 基于自适应的机器学习的神经元网络结构优化
abstract: This paper presents a novel algorithm for optimizing the structure of neural networks, employing a self-adaptive learning approach to dynamically adjust connection weights. Traditional methods often require manual tuning of parameters, which can be time-consuming and suboptimal. Our proposed algorithm leverages the power of self-learning to automatically adjust weights, leading to improved model generalization. We introduce a framework that iteratively adjusts weights based on a learned loss function, minimizing the error across the entire network. The core mechanism centers around a reinforcement learning-inspired optimization strategy, utilizing a gradient-based approach to iteratively refine the network's structure. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach through several benchmark datasets, showcasing significant improvements in accuracy and stability compared to existing methods. This work represents a significant step toward automated and adaptive neural network design, potentially unlocking new capabilities in complex modeling tasks.

title: Title: Non-Linear Dynamical Systems – The Adaptive Resonance Network (ARN)
abstract: This paper explores the application of the Adaptive Resonance Network (ARN) framework to the study of non-linear dynamical systems. Traditional approaches often struggle to accurately model systems exhibiting complex, self-organizing behavior, particularly those where the state is not directly proportional to its input. This work proposes a novel model that leverages the ARN's inherent ability to maintain a continuous, adaptive state based on feedback loops, offering a potential pathway to capture and understand these intricate dynamics. The core mechanism involves designing an ARN-based framework that allows for the system's state to evolve continuously, driven by its internal dynamics and the interplay of its own state, circumventing the limitations of linear models. The paper details the model's architecture, explores initial implementation and validation through simulation, and discusses the potential implications for modeling diverse complex systems.

title: Dynamic Programming with Quantum-Inspired Exhaustion
abstract: Dynamic programming, a powerful algorithmic technique for solving optimization problems, often faces limitations when dealing with large state spaces, leading to significant memory requirements and computational complexity. This research proposes a novel approach that integrates dynamic programming with quantum-inspired exhaustion techniques. The core idea is to mimic quantum measurement processes—specifically, the concept of probabilistic pruning—to intelligently reduce the search space within a dynamic programming framework. We introduce a method where subtrees are pruned based on estimated probabilities derived from probabilistic sampling, effectively simulating a measurement process that favors regions with higher potential for optimal solutions. This combined approach aims to alleviate the memory bottleneck associated with traditional dynamic programming, offering a more scalable solution for complex optimization problems. The paper details the methodology, explores the underlying principles, and presents a theoretical framework for this integration. The results suggest a significant reduction in computational cost and memory usage compared to standard dynamic programming, demonstrating the viability of this quantum-inspired exhaustion strategy. ---

title: Political Stance Pseudo-Labels for January 8th, 2023 Brazilian Crisis Tweets (BERTimbau)
abstract: This dataset contains political stance pseudo-labels for individual tweets related to the January 8, 2023 attack on the headquarters of Brazil's Three Powers in Brasília. Each tweet was classified independently by a fine-tuned BERTimbau model (`neuralmind/bert-base-portuguese-cased`, macro-F1 = 0.85 on held-out test data), trained on a manually annotated subset (Tweets8JanSPI, ALABARSE et al., 2025) and applied to the full January 8th tweet corpus (raw data from CIBERDEM). Before stance classification, tweets flagged as ironic or sarcastic by an auxiliary BERTimbau-based binary classifier (probability of irony ≥≥ 0.10) were removed from the pool. This decision was made because irony consistently reduces stance-classification precision. Based on internal validation, we adopted an “ignore” strategy rather than flipping the labels. Each row is one tweet, assigned one of three stance labels — a_favor [in favor], contra [against], neutro [neutral] — with the classifier's confidence score. To control noise, we kept only predictions passing per-class confidence thresholds calibrated on a human-labeled validation set (the smallest grid value in {0.90, 0.95, 0.97, 0.99, 0.995} reaching ≥0.90 precision per class, with neutro falling back to the largest grid value since it never reaches that bar): 0.99 for a_favor, 0.95 for contra, 0.995 for neutro. This yields 285,160 high-confidence labeled tweets (27.9% retention over the classified pool). In compliance with the X platform's Terms of Service, which prohibit redistribution of full post content, this repository provides `conversation_id` and predicted labels only, not raw tweet text — the same dehydrated format used by the human-annotated dataset this one derives from (Tweets8JanSPI, https://zenodo.org/records/17555457). Columns - `conversation_id` — X/Twitter conversation (thread) identifier the tweet belongs to, a standard field of the X/Twitter API v2 Tweet object- `predicted_label` — predicted stance (`a favor` / `contra` / `neutro`, kept in Portuguese as produced by the classifier)- `confidence` — classifier confidence for the predicted label (0–1) Class distribution contra = 212,336 (74.5%); neutro = 56,373 (19.8%); a favor = 16,451 (5.8%).

title: Explainable Deep Reinforcement Learning through Concept Inference
abstract: This paper explores the critical need for explainable and robust deep reinforcement learning (DRL) agents. Current DRL models often operate as "black boxes," lacking transparency and hindering trust and adaptation in real-world scenarios. We propose a novel framework for incorporating concept inference into DRL, enabling agents to "understand" underlying concepts and leverage this understanding for improved planning and decision-making. Our approach utilizes knowledge graphs to formalize concepts and integrates logical reasoning techniques within the DRL architecture. This allows the agent to not only learn optimal policies but also to reason about the relationships between concepts, leading to enhanced generalization and interpretability. We outline a system architecture and key components, emphasizing the integration of symbolic and connectionist approaches. The core claim of this work is to design a mechanism that allows DRL models to 'understand' concepts, thereby improving their planning and decision-making abilities. The core mechanism relies on the use of knowledge graphs and logical reasoning to formalize concepts and integrate them into the reinforcement learning model. This work contributes to advancing the field by addressing the limitations of current DRL methods and paving the way for more reliable and trustworthy AI systems.

title: Quantum Teleportation Advances: Energy Transfer and 1,400 km Space Tests — E8 Intelligence Research
abstract: FINDING: Quantum teleportation transmits quantum *states* (information), not matter or energy; recent experiments extend this to energy teleportation on superconducting hardware and Earth-to-space distances up to 1,400 km. | MATH: Core formalism: Bell-state measurement (BSM) + classical communication (2 bits) + local unitary correction. State transfer fidelity F = |⟨ψ|ρ_out|ψ⟩|²; for ideal teleportation F=1. Energy teleportation (arXiv:2301.02666) uses local operations and classical communication (LOCC) to extract positive energy from a vacuum-like entangled state, quantified by energy density ⟨T₀₀⟩ and conditional entropy S(A|B) = S(ρ_AB) − S(ρ_B). No mass/energy moves — only correlations. | CONNECTION: The 2-bit classical channel per teleported qubit maps to the binary tetrahedral group (order 24) — the symmetry of the F4 lattice root system. The four Bell states correspond to the four cosets of the Pauli group {I, X, Y, Z} modulo phases, which is isomorphic to the Klein four-group V Author: Andrew Stewart Caldin, Independent Researcher, UK. Part of the E8 Intelligence Research series. Platform: e8intelligence.com

title: ## The Nautilus Algorithm: A Metaheuristic Inspired by Oyster Shell Morphology
abstract: This paper introduces the Nautilus Algorithm, a novel metaheuristic optimization method inspired by the intricate and adaptive morphology of oyster shells. The algorithm leverages the self-organizing, iterative growth patterns observed in oyster shells, particularly the spiral arrangement of the shell's ridges, to guide the search process. The Nautilus Algorithm employs a multi-dimensional representation of the search space, utilizing a 'shell' structure to encapsulate candidate solutions. The algorithm's core mechanism, termed 'Ridge Propagation,' simulates the growth of shell ridges based on a combination of gradient descent and a stochastic element, mimicking the natural process of shell formation. This approach aims to provide a robust and efficient method for solving complex optimization problems. The paper details the algorithm's theoretical framework, key parameters, and a conceptual overview of its operation, highlighting its potential advantages over existing metaheuristic techniques.

title: Andersen's Fruit-eating Bat: A Novel Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by the Fruit-eating Bat
abstract: This paper presents a novel metaheuristic algorithm, Andersen's Fruit-eating Bat (AFEB), inspired by the foraging behavior of fruit-eating bats. The algorithm mimics the bats' ability to locate fruit through echolocation, utilizing a combination of pulse emission, echo reception, and movement strategies. AFEB employs a population-based search approach, where each individual represents a potential solution. The algorithm's core components include a pulse emission strategy, an echo reception mechanism, and a movement mechanism, all designed to guide the population towards promising regions of the search space. Specifically, the pulse emission rate is dynamically adjusted based on the estimated distance to the target, and the echo reception strength is proportional to the similarity between the received echo and the emitted pulse. Movement is determined by the gradient of the received echo strength. The algorithm's performance is evaluated on a range of benchmark optimization problems, demonstrating its effectiveness and efficiency. The key contributions of this work are the novel integration of these bat-inspired mechanisms into a cohesive and effective metaheuristic algorithm, and the demonstration of its superior performance compared to established methods. The algorithm's parameters are tuned using a self-adaptive strategy, further enhancing its robustness and adaptability. The ultimate goal is to provide a robust and efficient solution for a variety of complex optimization problems.

title: Quantum State Transformation of Non-Linear Topology
abstract: Quantum state transformation, a fundamental concept in quantum mechanics, offers a powerful framework for manipulating and understanding quantum systems. This paper investigates the application of non-linear topology to quantum state description, proposing a novel method for optimizing quantum states and exploring its potential within quantum information processing, particularly in the context of quantum key distribution. The core mechanism centers around utilizing topological transformations to guide the evolution of quantum states, offering a potential path towards enhanced quantum information processing. The paper discusses the theoretical foundations, implementation details, and preliminary experimental investigations of this approach. We present a model that leverages topological transformations to enhance the fidelity of quantum states and explore its implications for various quantum algorithms. The research highlights the potential of this methodology to significantly impact the development of quantum technologies.

title: Quantum Error Correction Codes for Distributed Databases
abstract: This paper explores the application of quantum error correction (QEC) codes to construct a distributed database with enhanced resilience and reliability. Traditional distributed databases face challenges regarding data durability and security due to potential hardware failures and malicious attacks. This work proposes a novel approach where database data is encoded into quantum states utilizing QEC codes. The system employs error detection and correction mechanisms inherent within the chosen QEC code, enabling robust data storage and retrieval, even in the presence of errors. The core claim of this research is to leverage the inherent properties of QEC codes to build a distributed database with fault-tolerance capabilities. The mechanism relies on encoding data into quantum states and leveraging error correction techniques for efficient data management. This approach offers a new paradigm for database systems, potentially improving their reliability, security, and scalability in demanding environments. The system's architecture is designed to minimize the impact of errors, ensuring data integrity and availability. The exploration focuses on the theoretical aspects and potential implementation strategies, highlighting the advantages of this quantum-based approach.

title: Red-Crested Finch Metaheuristic Optimization Algorithm (RCFMOA)
abstract: This paper proposes a novel metaheuristic optimization algorithm, the Red-Crested Finch Metaheuristic Optimization Algorithm (RCFMOA), inspired by the foraging behavior of red-crested finches. The algorithm utilizes a combination of territory defense, mate selection, and resource competition mechanisms to effectively navigate complex search spaces. RCFMOA incorporates a novel 'Dominance Radius' parameter to refine territory boundaries and a 'Proximity Fitness' function to bias mate selection towards solutions with higher overall fitness. The algorithm's core components – territory establishment, defense, mate selection, and resource allocation – are designed to promote exploration and exploitation simultaneously, leading to improved convergence and robustness. This paper details the algorithm's theoretical foundations, operational rules, and potential applications, highlighting its advantages over existing metaheuristic techniques.

title: Fractal Information Theory for Quantum State Tomography
abstract: Quantum state tomography (QST) is a fundamental technique for characterizing the state of a quantum system. However, traditional QST protocols often suffer from significant measurement complexity and resource demands, particularly when dealing with high-dimensional quantum states. This work proposes a novel approach to QST that leverages the inherent fractal structure observed in measurement outcomes. We introduce a framework utilizing fractal dimension analysis to guide the acquisition of more efficient and accurate tomography protocols. The core idea is to adaptively refine measurement strategies based on the fractal characteristics revealed in the measurement data. This approach aims to reduce the overall number of measurements required while simultaneously improving the fidelity of the reconstructed quantum state. We demonstrate the theoretical feasibility and potential benefits of this methodology, offering a promising direction for advancing QST techniques.

title: RealCAD: Towards Real-World Image-to-CAD Reconstruction under Domain Shift and Parameter Bias
abstract: Reconstructing editable Computer-Aided Design (CAD) models from images is essential for downstream modification, manufacturing, and design reuse. However, existing image-to-CAD methods are developed predominantly on synthetic renderings and face two coupled obstacles: a substantial appearance domain gap between synthetic and real images, and a previously overlooked parameter bias in widely used CAD data. We show that the local normalization adopted by DeepCAD concentrates several geometric parameters around a few discrete values while encoding substantial information in a single scale factor. Consequently, a model can achieve deceptively high parameter accuracy by exploiting these frequent values rather than inferring geometry from the input image. In this paper, we propose RealCAD, a unified framework that addresses these limitations at the representation, image, and feature levels. At the representation level, we redistribute scale information to the corresponding geometric parameters, producing less concentrated parameter distributions in a shared scale space. At the image level, geometry-constrained translation converts synthetic renderings toward the real-image domain while conditioning on object contours. At the feature level, a multi-positive contrastive objective aligns representations of the same CAD model across viewpoints and image domains, enabling CAD sequence prediction from each individual view. We further introduce OpenRealCAD, comprising four-view photographs of 392 3D-printed objects paired with ground-truth command sequences. Experiments show that the revised representation substantially reduces the accuracy attainable from parameter-frequency priors, making parameter accuracy a more reliable measure of image-conditioned geometric inference. RealCAD further improves real-domain command and parameter accuracy, while retaining competitive synthetic-domain performance.

title: Impact of AI-Powered Personalization in Influencing Consumer Purchase Intention and Brand Loyalty
abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI)-powered personalization is transforming online retail by tailoring product recommendations, promotional messages, search results, and customer interactions to individual preferences. This study examines the impact of AI-powered personalization on consumers' purchase intention and brand loyalty among online shoppers. A descriptive and quantitative research design is proposed, using a structured questionnaire and a five-point Likert scale. Following the structure of the supplied model paper, an illustrative sample of 200 respondents is used for the model analysis. Descriptive statistics, Chi-square, and one-way ANOVA are applied. The illustrative results indicate a significant association between exposure to AI-powered recommendations and purchase intention, as well as significant differences in brand loyalty across levels of perceived personalization. The study suggests that retailers should improve recommendation relevance, provide transparent personalization, protect consumer data, and combine AI-enabled service with human support. The paper concludes that responsible AI personalization can strengthen purchase intention and brand loyalty when consumers perceive the experience as useful, accurate, convenient, and trustworthy.

title: Graph-Based Semantic Relation Extraction
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to semantic relation extraction leveraging graph embedding techniques. Traditional relation extraction methods often suffer from limitations such as reliance on manually annotated data, the need for complex rule-based systems, and inherent subjectivity. This research proposes a method that transforms graph structures into continuous vector representations (graph embeddings) and utilizes these embeddings for relation extraction. The core claim is that this approach significantly enhances both the accuracy and efficiency of relation extraction. We explore various graph embedding models and demonstrate their effectiveness in capturing semantic relationships within graphs. The presented method offers a more scalable and potentially more accurate alternative to existing approaches, addressing the shortcomings of previous methods. This work lays the foundation for further research into utilizing graph embeddings for diverse semantic understanding tasks.

title: 自适应量子计算的混沌控制
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to quantum computation utilizing adaptive chaos control. Traditional chaos control methods often rely on fixed parameters, limiting the potential for optimized performance. We propose a system that employs machine learning to dynamically adjust the parameters of a chaotic control algorithm, resulting in improved stability and efficiency. The core mechanism involves learning a mapping between quantum state evolution and control parameters, enabling automated optimization of the chaos control process. The paper details the design of the adaptive control strategy, its implementation, and the resulting performance improvements observed through simulations. We demonstrate that this approach offers a significant advancement over traditional methods, addressing the limitations of fixed-parameter chaos control.

title: Core Claim: This paper presents a novel geometric model validation method predicated on quantum entanglement, designed to enhance the security of quantum computation. The core mechanism leverages entanglement to rigorously test geometric models, offering a pathway to more robust verification processes.
abstract: Quantum entanglement, a cornerstone of quantum mechanics, holds immense potential for secure communication and computation. Traditional verification methods, reliant on classical computation, often struggle to comprehensively assess the security of complex geometric models. This paper introduces a new geometric model validation technique employing quantum entanglement to provide a more rigorous and secure verification process. The core mechanism involves establishing entangled states with geometric models, enabling the detection of subtle inconsistencies that might be missed with conventional methods. The resulting entanglement properties are then analyzed to ascertain the model's security characteristics. This work represents a significant advancement in quantum verification, offering a promising approach to bolstering the resilience of quantum systems.

title: Self-Organizing Neural Networks: Dynamic Topology Control
abstract: This paper introduces a novel dynamic topology control algorithm for self-organizing neural networks (SNNs). Traditional neural network training methods often rely on static architectures, limiting flexibility and potential performance. This work proposes a dynamic approach that leverages the inherent topology of the network to optimize its performance through strategic adjustments to connections and weights. We detail the core mechanism, outlining how the algorithm dynamically reshapes the network's topology to achieve desired outcomes. The paper concludes with a discussion of the advantages and potential applications of this dynamic topology control method, highlighting its potential to surpass the limitations of conventional approaches.

title: Neural Network Dynamics: Topological Learning
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to neural network learning centered around dynamic topological structures. The core idea is to construct a neural network with locally adaptive synaptic plasticity and a dynamically evolving topology, enabling continuous learning and adaptation to complex, non-static environments without explicit structural specification. The methodology integrates adaptive synaptic plasticity, topological evolution rules, and fine-grained neuronal state encoding. Adaptive synaptic plasticity adjusts synaptic weights based on local neuronal activity, strengthening important connections and suppressing irrelevant ones. Topological evolution rules dynamically modify connection strengths based on information transmission efficiency and local activity patterns, altering the network's topology. Fine-grained neuronal state encoding captures richer temporal information, enhancing neuronal dependencies. This dynamic topological learning mechanism contrasts significantly with traditional static neural networks and rule-based reinforcement learning, offering a potential pathway to building more intelligent and robust systems. ---

title: Bearcat: A Novel Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by Bearcat Behavior
abstract: This paper presents Bearcat, a new metaheuristic optimization algorithm inspired by the foraging behavior of Bearcats ( *Melogale moschata*). Bearcats are known for their strategic approach to food gathering, utilizing a combination of systematic searching and opportunistic exploitation. Bearcat leverages these behaviors through a novel search operator and a dynamically adjusted adaptive inertia weight mechanism. The algorithm's core components include a position representation, a global best position, and a local best position. The primary innovation lies in the "Pounce" operator, which mimics the Bearcat's sudden shifts in direction when encountering a promising food source. Furthermore, the algorithm incorporates a dynamically adjusted inertia weight scheme based on the distance between the current position and the global best position. We evaluate Bearcat on a range of benchmark optimization problems, demonstrating its competitive performance compared to established metaheuristic algorithms such as Genetic Algorithm (GA) and Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO). Experimental results show that Bearcat exhibits robust performance across diverse problem landscapes, indicating its potential applicability in various real-world optimization scenarios. The key performance metrics considered are convergence speed and solution quality.

title: Geometric Complexity Metric for Machine Learning
abstract: This paper introduces a novel geometric complexity metric designed to enhance the training and evaluation of machine learning models. Traditional metrics often focus on surface area or volume, neglecting the fundamental geometric properties of data points. We propose a new metric that quantifies the complexity of data points – the arrangement of edges, angles, and curves – and utilizes this measure to guide model learning, potentially improving accuracy and interpretability. The core mechanism involves calculating a "complexity score" for each data point, which is then incorporated into the model's optimization process. This approach aims to capture subtle patterns and relationships within the data that may be missed by conventional metrics. The paper details the metric's construction, demonstrates its effectiveness through illustrative examples, and discusses potential future directions for research.

title: Quantum-Inspired Bayesian Inference for Causal Discovery
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to causal discovery leveraging principles inspired by quantum mechanics. Traditional Bayesian network learning methods often struggle with the vastness of possible causal structures, leading to computational bottlenecks and potentially inaccurate results. We propose a framework that incorporates probabilistic amplitudes, analogous to quantum superposition, to represent and explore multiple potential causal pathways concurrently. This "quantum-inspired" Bayesian inference aims to significantly enhance the exploration process, ultimately leading to improved accuracy in identifying causal relationships within observational data. The core idea is that by allowing for multiple potential pathways to be actively explored simultaneously, we can overcome the limitations of classical methods that typically rely on sequential searching. This approach is evaluated conceptually, outlining the key components and anticipated benefits. The paper focuses on the theoretical underpinnings and the potential impact of this methodology, paving the way for future research and development.

title: Adaptive Dynamic Programming Algorithm for Reinforcement Learning
abstract: Reinforcement Learning (RL) has demonstrated remarkable success in various domains, but its application is often hindered by the "curse of dimensionality," specifically the state space explosion problem. Traditional dynamic programming methods, while theoretically sound for solving Markov Decision Processes (MDPs), struggle with large state spaces due to the exponential growth of the value function computation. This paper proposes an Adaptive Dynamic Programming Algorithm for Reinforcement Learning (ADP-RL), designed to mitigate this issue. ADP-RL dynamically adjusts the parameters of the dynamic programming algorithm based on the observed dynamics of the environment, effectively reducing computational complexity. The core mechanism involves a feedback loop that monitors the convergence rate of the value function approximation and modifies parameters accordingly. We demonstrate the effectiveness of ADP-RL through a theoretical analysis and a simplified numerical example, highlighting its ability to handle complex environments more efficiently than standard dynamic programming approaches. The key innovation lies in the adaptive nature of the algorithm, offering a practical solution for scaling dynamic programming to real-world RL problems.

title: ## The Bioluminescent Navigation Algorithm (BLNA): A Metaheuristic Inspired by Blue Dragonfish Behavior
abstract: This paper introduces the Bioluminescent Navigation Algorithm (BLNA), a novel metaheuristic optimization algorithm inspired by the unique navigation strategies employed by blue dragonfish ( *Cynoglossus mola*) in the deep ocean. These fish utilize a sophisticated bioluminescent communication system to navigate and locate prey in dark environments. BLNA leverages concepts such as 'beaconing' (localized bioluminescence), 'gradient following' (movement towards brighter signals), and 'group cohesion' (collective movement) to achieve efficient global optimization. The algorithm operates within a search space, representing potential solutions, and iteratively adjusts these solutions based on a dynamically updated 'illumination' metric, mimicking the dragonfish's bioluminescent signals. We outline the core principles, mathematical formulation, and key components of BLNA, demonstrating its potential applicability across a range of optimization problems.

title: Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning for Resource Allocation
abstract: This paper investigates the application of Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (MARL) to the problem of resource allocation. Traditional resource allocation methods often struggle with complex scenarios involving multiple agents with varying priorities and constraints. MARL offers a promising approach by allowing agents to learn optimal allocation strategies through interaction and competition. This work proposes a framework utilizing multiple reinforcement learning agents to dynamically manage and distribute resources. The core claim is that MARL can achieve optimized resource allocation and enhanced fairness compared to traditional centralized approaches. The core mechanism involves constructing a multi-agent system where agents cooperate and compete to maximize their individual rewards while considering the overall system performance. The system learns through trial and error, adapting to changing conditions and agent behaviors. We present a detailed formulation of the problem, outlining the key components of the MARL system including agent representation, reward functions, and the learning algorithm. The potential benefits of this approach, particularly in dynamic and uncertain environments, are discussed, highlighting the adaptability and scalability of MARL for complex resource management challenges. ---

title: Geometry Topology Structure Optimization
abstract: This paper introduces a novel algorithm, Geometry Topology Structure Optimization, designed to address complex optimization problems by dynamically adjusting geometric topology. Traditional optimization methods often struggle with evolving topological structures, necessitating complex and computationally intensive adjustments. Our algorithm leverages the inherent properties of geometric topology to iteratively refine the problem space, leading to more accurate and robust solutions. We detail the core mechanism, outlining how the algorithm analyzes the topological landscape and intelligently modifies it to guide the search process. The paper provides a comprehensive explanation of the algorithm's design, including the mathematical framework underpinning its operations and its potential impact on various optimization scenarios.

title: ## The Giant Tortoise-Inspired Adaptive Search Algorithm (GTSA)
abstract: This paper introduces the Giant Tortoise-Inspired Adaptive Search Algorithm (GTSA), a novel metaheuristic optimization algorithm inspired by the navigational strategies and foraging behaviors of giant tortoises. The algorithm leverages the tortoise's ability to maintain a consistent direction, adapt to environmental changes, and selectively adjust its pace based on resource availability. GTSA employs a multi-faceted approach combining a directional movement strategy, a dynamic adaptation mechanism, and a resource-based pacing system. The core of the algorithm lies in a novel 'Orientation Vector' representation of the search space, coupled with a 'Terrain Map' that dynamically adjusts based on exploration progress. The algorithm's performance is evaluated theoretically, demonstrating its potential for efficiently exploring complex search landscapes. Keywords: Metaheuristic Optimization, Giant Tortoise, Adaptive Search, Search Landscape, Orientation Vector, Terrain Map.

title: Quantum State-Based Non-Linear Computing and Quantum Algorithm Optimization
abstract: Quantum state-based non-linear computing offers a fundamentally different approach to computation compared to classical approaches. This paper explores the potential of leveraging quantum mechanics' inherent non-linear properties to design novel algorithms and optimize existing classical algorithms, particularly within the context of machine learning. We propose a new algorithm framework centered around the manipulation of quantum entangled states, focusing on accelerating computations and enhancing the performance of machine learning models. The core mechanism involves introducing controlled quantum entanglement to guide the computation process, ultimately leading to improved results. This work highlights the transformative potential of this paradigm shift in computational power and explores its practical implications for advanced machine learning applications.

title: ## Agag Gerbil: A Novel Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by Agag Gerbil Behavior
abstract: This paper presents Agag Gerbil, a novel metaheuristic optimization algorithm inspired by the foraging behavior of *Agag gerbil* (also known as the desert gerbil). *Agag gerbil* exhibit a remarkable ability to efficiently locate and exploit food sources in challenging desert environments. This paper details the algorithm's core principles, focusing on a novel exploration-exploitation strategy based on the gerbil's tendency to randomly explore while simultaneously prioritizing areas with previously observed high food concentrations. The algorithm incorporates a dynamic memory component to retain information about promising regions, mimicking the gerbil's recollection of successful foraging routes. Mathematical formulations are provided to describe the key components of the algorithm, including the probability function for exploration and exploitation, the memory update mechanism, and the parameter adaptation scheme. The performance of Agag Gerbil is evaluated through a series of benchmark problems, demonstrating its competitive capabilities across a range of optimization tasks. Keywords: Metaheuristic Algorithm, Optimization, Agag Gerbil, Foraging Behavior, Exploration, Exploitation, Dynamic Memory, Parameter Adaptation. ### 1. Introduction Metaheuristic algorithms have become a cornerstone of modern optimization techniques, offering robust solutions to a wide variety of complex problems. Algorithms such as Genetic Algorithms (GAs), Simulated Annealing (SA), and Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) have consistently demonstrated success in tackling challenges across diverse domains, including engineering design, machine learning, and financial modeling. However, many metaheuristic algorithms struggle with premature convergence, particularly in problems with intricate landscapes and multiple local optima. The ability to maintain a balance between effective exploration and efficient exploitation is crucial for achieving optimal solutions. This research explores a new metaheuristic algorithm, Agag Gerbil, drawing inspiration from the remarkable foraging behavior of *Agag gerbil* (*Gerbillus campbelli*). These small rodents inhabit arid environments and possess an extraordinary ability to locate and exploit scarce food resources. Their foraging strategy is characterized by a combination of systematic exploration and targeted exploitation – they will randomly move across the landscape, but will preferentially visit areas where they have previously found food. This behavior has been observed to be highly effective in maximizing food intake in environments where food distribution is uneven and unpredictable. The core motivation behind developing Agag Gerbil is to translate this observed foraging strategy into a robust metaheuristic algorithm. The algorithm's design prioritizes maintaining a balance between exploring new regions of the search space and refining solutions in promising areas. This paper presents a detailed description of Agag Gerbil, including its mathematical formulation, algorithm design, and performance evaluation. ### 2. Algorithm Design Agag Gerbil is designed around three primary components: a population of candidate solutions, an exploration-exploitation mechanism, and a dynamic memory system. #### 2.1 Population Initialization The algorithm begins with an initial population of *N* candidate solutions. Each solution *si* is represented as a vector *xi = (x1, x2, ..., xD)*, where *D* is the dimensionality of the problem. The initial population is generated using a random sampling technique, ensuring a diverse range of starting points. #### 2.2 Exploration-Exploitation Mechanism The core of Agag Gerbil lies in its exploration-exploitation mechanism, which governs the movement of individuals within the population. This mechanism is based on two key probabilities: * Exploration Probability (Pe): This probability determines the likelihood of an individual moving to a randomly selected neighboring solution. The probability is calculated as: *Pe = 1 - exp(-α * R(si))* where *α* is a parameter controlling the exploration rate, and *R(si)* is a random number uniformly distributed between 0 and 1. A higher *α* value leads to increased exploration. * Exploitation Probability (Px): This probability determines the likelihood of an individual moving to a neighboring solution that is considered promising, based on a local evaluation function. The probability is calculated as: *Px = exp(-β * F(si))* where *β* is a parameter controlling the exploitation rate, and *F(si)* is the value of the evaluation function for solution *si*. A higher *β* value leads to increased exploitation. The overall probability of movement to a neighboring solution is the sum of the exploration and exploitation probabilities: *P = Pe + Px* The algorithm then selects a neighboring solution according to this probability distribution.

title: African Giant Free-tailed Bat Inspired Metaheuristic Algorithm for Complex Optimization Problems
abstract: This paper presents a novel metaheuristic algorithm, termed the "Bat Echo Adaptation Method" (BEAM), inspired by the foraging behavior of African Giant Free-tailed bats. These bats utilize sophisticated echolocation techniques to navigate and locate food in complex environments. The algorithm leverages the concept of 'echoes' – the variations in the received signal – to guide the search process, mimicking the bats' adaptation to environmental changes. BEAM employs a population-based approach, similar to Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) and Artificial Bee Colony (ABC), but incorporates a unique mechanism for adaptive parameter adjustment based on echo intensity and frequency variations. The algorithm's performance is evaluated on a range of benchmark optimization problems, demonstrating its effectiveness in finding near-optimal solutions within reasonable computational time. Key elements of the algorithm include: a dynamic inertia weight calculation, a novel echo intensity adaptation strategy, and a frequency-dependent exploration-exploitation balance. The results indicate that BEAM exhibits competitive performance compared to established metaheuristic algorithms, particularly in problems with high dimensionality and complex landscapes. Further research will focus on extending BEAM to handle multi-objective optimization and real-time adaptive control applications.

title: Quantum Stealth Computing Topology Optimization
abstract: Quantum Stealth Computing, a paradigm shift in computation, necessitates robust security measures. Traditional approaches often focus on algorithm optimization, neglecting the fundamental role of topology in enhancing security. This research investigates the utilization of topological structures as a core optimization strategy for quantum stealth computing, specifically leveraging their inherent anti-interference properties to bolster security and explore potential applications. We propose a novel framework that dynamically adjusts topological parameters to mitigate potential attacks and enhance the overall computational resilience. This work presents a comprehensive analysis of the impact of topological optimization on quantum computation's security, demonstrating significant improvements in resilience against known attack vectors.

title: User-Centred Development of a Trustworthy E-Voting Application
abstract: Developing a secure and reliable remote electronic voting (e-voting) application presents critical challenges, particularly in ensuring system integrity, security, and user trust. This chapter focuses on designing and evaluating an e-voting system for student leader elections to address key factors influencing voter confidence. The development process followed a structured set of phases: analysis, design, development, implementation, and evaluation. Key concerns, such as transparency, voter anonymity, prevention of duplicate voting (singularity), and integrity of results, were addressed. A survey was conducted with 1,000 randomly selected students to assess their primary concerns and level of trust in the system. Results indicate that transparency, singularity, integrity, and anonymity are the most crucial requirements for an e-voting system. To enhance trust, efforts were made from the design phase through socialisation, including educational campaigns, application demonstrations, and user training. Rigorous testing was conducted by internal developers and external stakeholders, followed by a public trial. Out of 3,527 survey respondents, 68.04% expressed trust in the application, deeming it “feasible” for adoption. However, areas such as transparency and feedback mechanisms require further improvement to fully address user concerns. It contributes to the field of e-voting by underscoring the importance of user involvement and extensive testing in developing a trustworthy system for student elections.

title: Wrapped Gaussian process neural network model for manifold-valued data
abstract: In modern regression analysis tasks, an increasing amount of data exhibits non-Euclidean characteristics. Modeling methods based on traditional Euclidean space are no longer effective in adapting to the intrinsic geometric features of manifold-structured data. To address this issue, this paper proposes a neural network modeling framework for manifold-valued response variables. The proposed method, on the one hand, achieves a local correspondence between manifold space and Euclidean space through exponential mapping and its inverse mapping, constructing a geometrically compatible connection bridge for the association between predictor variables and manifold-valued response variables. On the other hand, considering the complex nonlinearity and unknown nature of this association, it utilizes the powerful nonlinear fitting capability of neural networks to accurately model it, breaking through the limitations of traditional linear assumptions. In addition, for potential random effects in the data, a wrapped Gaussian process prior is introduced to probabilistically characterize them, enhancing the model's adaptability to random fluctuations. In the parameter estimation stage, this paper adopts a penalized maximum likelihood estimation method to simultaneously solve neural network parameters and kernel function parameters, ensuring the global effectiveness and computational stability of the estimation process. The proposed model also has extensibility: (1) by designing a reasonable metric kernel function, it can directly handle complex scenarios where predictor variables are also in non-Euclidean space; (2) it can achieve uncertainty quantification of manifold-valued response variables based on a probabilistic framework. Simulation studies and real data analysis show that the proposed method is more competitive than Euclidean regression methods that do not consider the intrinsic structure of Riemannian manifolds.

title: Multi-Unary: a dense input encoding scheme for the quantum circuit model
abstract: Abstract The choice of a given encoding scheme for the problem variables, represented by a set of input qubits of a quantum circuit, substantially influences its design, as well as the quantity and nature of quantum resources (qubits and gates) employed by it. Quantum programmers have access to a variety of encoding strategies, such as one-hot, binary, Gray, amplitude encoding, or Schmidt decomposition, but each of them allows encoding just a single value for each problem variable. This article introduces a novel encoding scheme based on one-hot encoding, termed Multi-Unary, which enables the representation of multiple values within the input qubits, hence the descriptor ‘dense encoding scheme.’ The application of Multi-Unary is demonstrated in the context of the graph coloring problem using Grover’s algorithm, although its applicability extends to a broader class of quantum algorithms. By increasing the informational density on the input qubits, the multi-unary encoding offers potential advantages in terms of circuit compactness and resource efficiency, while at the same time enables an output value to contain more than one solution to a problem. Given its simple implementation, it can even replace the one-hot encoding scheme.

title: OCR-Based Field Extraction for Archaeological Pottery Metadata: The CENTURIA Dataset
abstract: Pottery is a primary source for reconstructing the chronological and economic dimensions of past societies. Archaeologists often document ceramic finds through technical drawings and handwritten metadata. This metadata is critical for dating, provenance attribution, and cross-site comparison, but remains inaccessible to computational analysis, requiring manual transcription of every record. We investigate whether state-of-the-art document analysis models can address this task, and introduce CENTURIA, a dataset of 507 pottery records from the Roman site of Carnuntum, providing transcriptions, bounding boxes, and structured field-level labels across seven metadata categories. Benchmarking five OCR models reveals a substantial domain gap: zero-shot transcription error reaches 15-32% SpACER-M, far exceeding rates on printed archival documents, with domain-specific fields recovered in fewer than 3% of cases. LoRA fine-tuning on just 57 samples, reflecting a realistic archival annotation budget, closes this gap, reducing transcription error to below 1.5% and recovering overall field-level accuracy above 87%. Our results show that a small expert-validated fine-tuning set suffices to convert handwritten pottery documentation into structured, searchable metadata ready for archaeological databases.

title: Quantum Topology Dynamic Topology Network Structure Optimization Algorithm
abstract: Quantum topology, a fascinating field of physics, has recently garnered significant interest in areas of computation and materials science. This paper introduces a novel algorithm, Quantum Topology Dynamic Topology Network Structure Optimization Algorithm, designed to address the challenges of optimizing complex topological network structures. Leveraging the unique properties of quantum entanglement and self-organization, this algorithm aims to achieve significant improvements in system performance through intelligent network manipulation. The core mechanism centers around utilizing quantum entanglement to guide the evolution of network topology, employing quantum algorithms to optimize the resulting network structure. We propose a new framework for optimizing network topology based on these principles, demonstrating its potential for enhanced computational efficiency and performance in scenarios where traditional optimization methods fall short.

title: Title: Adaptive Bayesian Network for Dynamical System Modeling
abstract: This paper presents an Adaptive Bayesian Network (ABN) for dynamical system modeling, designed to enhance predictive accuracy and real-time control capabilities. Traditional Bayesian networks struggle with evolving systems, requiring manual parameter adjustments and limiting adaptability. Our proposed ABN leverages a "Neural Bayesian Network" – a novel learning approach – to dynamically update the network's structure based on observed data, resulting in improved predictive performance. The paper details the architecture, training process, and performance evaluation of the ABN, demonstrating its efficacy in modeling complex dynamical systems.

title: Title: Topological Information Theory Quantum Machine Learning Integration
abstract: This paper explores the integration of Topological Information Theory (TIT) with Quantum Machine Learning (QML) to achieve quantum acceleration and data compression in machine learning. Traditional machine learning relies on explicit parameter tuning, while this integration leverages the inherent structure of topological information theory for adaptive learning. We propose a novel method for utilizing the topological structure of quantum models as a source of noise, optimizing model parameters through topological analysis to improve efficiency and generalization. The core claim is that utilizing this approach will result in enhanced quantum acceleration and data compression compared to traditional machine learning. This work presents a framework for incorporating topological information into the quantum machine learning pipeline, demonstrating a potential paradigm shift in model optimization and efficiency.

title: Quantum Entanglement-Driven Distributed Memory (QDM)
abstract: This paper proposes a novel distributed memory architecture, termed Quantum Entanglement-Driven Distributed Memory (QDM), which leverages quantum entanglement to achieve ultra-long-distance, low-latency data access, circumventing the limitations imposed by physical distances in conventional distributed systems. The core concept involves multiple "quantum nodes" interconnected via entangled particles, forming a quantum channel for instantaneous data transmission and synchronization. Data is read and written through entangled measurements, eliminating the data replication and synchronization bottlenecks inherent in traditional distributed memory systems. We present a theoretical framework outlining the QDM architecture, focusing on the key mathematical concepts and operational principles. This architecture has the potential to revolutionize data processing and communication, especially in scenarios demanding extreme low latency and high bandwidth.

Data is read and written through entangled measurements, eliminating the data replication and synchronization bottlenecks inherent in traditional distributed memory systems. We present a theoretical framework outlining the QDM architecture, focusing on the key mathematical concepts and operational principles. This architecture has the potential to revolutionize data processing and communication, especially in scenarios demanding extreme low latency and high bandwidth.

title: Core Claim: Develop a method based on adaptive quantum state geometry that automatically adjusts the geometric deformation of quantum states, enabling precise control, particularly in the handling of quantum state evolution.
abstract: Quantum state geometry offers a powerful framework for controlling and manipulating quantum systems, and the ability to dynamically adjust geometric parameters is crucial for achieving precise operations. This paper presents a novel algorithm for quantum state geometry, leveraging adaptive geometry to automatically adjust the shape of quantum states. We introduce a self-adaptive geometric deformation module that learns from the quantum state's characteristics, enabling precise control and efficient handling of complex quantum state evolution. The proposed approach offers a significant advancement over existing methods, particularly in scenarios requiring dynamic geometric adjustments. This work focuses on the development of a method that dynamically adjusts geometric parameters during quantum state evolution, leading to improved control and a more robust framework for quantum system manipulation. The core mechanism involves a self-learning module that adapts geometric parameters based on the quantum state's inherent properties, addressing a key challenge in precise quantum state engineering.

title: ## Black Myotis-Inspired Metaheuristic Algorithm for Optimization Problems
abstract: This paper introduces a novel metaheuristic algorithm, termed the "Black Myotis Algorithm" (BMA), inspired by the foraging behavior of the Black Myotis bat. The algorithm leverages the bat's echolocation and flight patterns to develop a stochastic search strategy for solving optimization problems. The BMA incorporates key aspects of bat behavior, including pulse emission, frequency modulation, and flight adjustments based on food source detection. The algorithm utilizes a population of "bats" representing potential solutions, employing a dynamic parameter adjustment mechanism mirroring the bats' response to environmental changes. We demonstrate the application of the BMA to several benchmark optimization problems, showcasing its effectiveness and competitiveness compared to established metaheuristic algorithms. The algorithm's performance is evaluated based on convergence speed, solution quality, and computational efficiency. The core of the BMA is the 'Echo-Response' mechanism, which dynamically adjusts the search range and probability of movement based on the perceived "echo" strength – a measure of the fitness of a potential solution. The algorithm's design prioritizes adaptability and robustness, aiming to provide a versatile tool for tackling diverse optimization challenges. The primary goal is to create an algorithm that exhibits efficient exploration and exploitation capabilities, leading to robust solutions across various problem landscapes.

title: 基于量子退相干的分布式密钥生成
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to secure distributed key generation (DKG) leveraging the principles of quantum decoherence. Traditional DKG protocols are vulnerable to single-point attacks. This work introduces a protocol designed to mitigate this vulnerability by incorporating quantum decoherence into the key generation process. The core of the scheme relies on the creation and distribution of entangled states followed by a controlled decoherence phase. This process ensures that any attempt to intercept or monitor the key generation process introduces detectable errors, thereby guaranteeing security. The proposed method offers a significant improvement in security compared to conventional DKG systems, particularly against attacks targeting individual nodes. We detail the protocol, outlining the necessary parameters and operations, and discuss the theoretical security analysis. The ultimate goal is to provide a robust and practical DKG solution based on fundamental quantum mechanical phenomena.

title: Probabilistic Logic Programming
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to programming, termed Probabilistic Logic Programming, which aims to address the limitations of traditional logic programming in handling uncertainty and incomplete data. The core claim is that by integrating probabilistic reasoning within a logical framework, we can generate more robust and reliable decision-making systems. This is achieved through a new logic programming language that allows the explicit representation and manipulation of probability distributions alongside logical rules. The system utilizes Bayesian Networks or Markov Models for updating these probability distributions, guiding the iterative inference process. The innovation lies in the seamless fusion of logic and probability, offering a powerful tool for tackling complex, real-world problems characterized by inherent ambiguity. The paper details the core mechanisms, including the language design and the inference engine, and demonstrates the potential for improved decision-making under conditions of uncertainty. The ultimate goal is to create systems capable of not only deducing logical conclusions but also quantifying the confidence associated with those conclusions. ---

title: Dynamic Topology and Quantum Computing: A Fusion Paradigm
abstract: This paper explores the integration of dynamic topology and quantum computing, investigating the potential for leveraging quantum computation to accelerate and enhance the computation of complex topological structures. We propose a novel framework for quantum state-based topology, aiming to provide precise modeling and prediction of topological evolution. The core claim is that quantum computations, particularly those utilizing quantum entanglement and the precise manipulation of quantum states, can fundamentally change the landscape of topological field theory, offering a pathway to new computational models and potentially unlocking advanced quantum computation capabilities. The study will detail the design of a quantum computation framework centered around quantum entangled states, focusing on the precise modeling of topological changes and the prediction of future states.

title: Multi-Scale Quantum Topology Mapping
abstract: This paper introduces a novel quantum topology mapping algorithm designed to dynamically adapt to varying input data scales. Traditional approaches often rely on fixed parameters, limiting their ability to effectively handle data of differing dimensions. Our algorithm leverages multi-scale feature extraction to automatically adjust model parameters and structural topology, resulting in improved generalization capabilities. The core mechanism centers around a feedback loop that continuously refines the model based on the input's characteristics. We present a theoretical framework for this approach, detailing the algorithm's operational steps and demonstrating its effectiveness through illustrative examples. The potential implications of this work lie in the development of robust quantum systems capable of adapting to complex and evolving environments.

title: Symbiotic Algorithm for Data Synthesis (SADS)
abstract: This paper introduces the Symbiotic Algorithm for Data Synthesis (SADS), a novel approach to data synthesis that leverages a network of interconnected agents to dynamically generate complex datasets. Traditional data synthesis methods often rely on handcrafted rules or limited automation, struggling with the inherent complexity and emergent nature of data generation. SADS, however, employs a swarm intelligence paradigm, wherein agents specialize in specific data synthesis tasks and collaborate to produce intricate datasets. This algorithm aims to overcome these limitations by fostering a self-organizing synthesis process, resulting in more robust and adaptable data generation capabilities. The core of the algorithm involves a distributed agent network, dynamic feedback mechanisms, and a specialized synthesis framework, enabling the creation of diverse and high-fidelity synthetic datasets. We present a detailed description of the algorithm's components, including agent roles, communication protocols, and the underlying synthesis process. The research explores the potential of SADS for various applications, highlighting its advantages in terms of adaptability and complexity.

title: ## Giant Squid Inspired Metaheuristic Optimization Algorithm (GSIMO)
abstract: This paper introduces the Giant Squid Inspired Metaheuristic Optimization Algorithm (GSIMO), a novel optimization technique motivated by the remarkable adaptability and survival strategies of giant squids. Inspired by the squid's ability to dynamically adjust its buoyancy, camouflage, and movement patterns in response to environmental changes, GSIMO utilizes a multi-faceted approach incorporating elements of buoyancy control, adaptive camouflage, and exploratory movement. The algorithm employs a population of 'squid agents', each possessing parameters mimicking these biological features. These agents iteratively adjust their parameters based on a fitness landscape, guided by both local and global search strategies. A core innovation is the 'Buoyancy Regulation Mechanism' which dynamically adjusts agent movement speed and direction, and the 'Adaptive Camouflage' mechanism which alters the agent's search strategy based on its surroundings and the perceived fitness gradient. This paper outlines the theoretical framework of GSIMO, detailing its key components, operational rules, and potential applications. The algorithm's design seeks to provide a robust and efficient solution for complex optimization problems, particularly those exhibiting dynamic or evolving landscapes.

title: Ashy-headed Flying-fox: A Novel Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by Foraging Behavior
abstract: This paper introduces Ashy-headed Flying-fox (AHF), a novel metaheuristic algorithm inspired by the foraging strategies of Ashy-headed Flying-foxes (Pteraops brevirostris), a frugivorous bat species known for its efficient and adaptive foraging behavior. AHF combines elements of Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) and Artificial Bee Colony (ABC) algorithms, incorporating a unique "memory-based adaptation" mechanism mimicking the bats' ability to remember optimal foraging locations and adjust search directions accordingly. The algorithm aims to improve upon the convergence speed and exploration capabilities of existing metaheuristics. The core of AHF revolves around three key components: a population of candidate solutions (particles), a fitness function evaluating solution quality, and a memory matrix to store previously successful foraging locations. The algorithm employs a dynamic weight adjustment strategy based on the fitness of the particles and the age of the memory locations, ensuring effective exploration and exploitation of the search space. This paper presents the algorithm's theoretical foundations, design rationale, and demonstrates its effectiveness through simulations on benchmark optimization problems. The results indicate that AHF exhibits competitive performance compared to established metaheuristic algorithms, particularly in challenging landscapes with multiple local optima.

title: Program Optimization via Topological Sorting
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to program optimization leveraging topological sorting. The core idea centers on recognizing and eliminating dependencies within a program's code structure through the application of topological sorting algorithms. By translating program code into a topological graph and subsequently applying topological sorting, we identify and address cyclical dependencies and inefficient workflows. This process ultimately leads to optimized program execution and improved runtime efficiency. The methodology presented offers a fundamentally new perspective on program optimization, moving beyond traditional static analysis techniques. This work details the conversion process, the topological sorting implementation, and the resultant optimization strategies. The potential impact of this approach on various programming paradigms is discussed, highlighting opportunities for significant efficiency gains.

title: ## Stone Crab Inspired Metaheuristic Optimization Algorithm (SCIMO)
abstract: This paper introduces the Stone Crab Inspired Metaheuristic Optimization Algorithm (SCIMO), a novel metaheuristic algorithm inspired by the foraging behavior of stone crabs. Stone crabs, renowned for their ability to repeatedly dig and excavate in a limited area to find food, exhibit a strategy of alternating between exploration and exploitation. SCIMO mimics this behavior through a dynamic adjustment of exploration and exploitation parameters, coupled with a novel "digging" mechanism for solution refinement. The algorithm utilizes a population-based approach, employing a virtual "crab" that navigates a solution space, iteratively refining its position through a process of digging and moving. The core innovation lies in the adaptive regulation of the balance between exploration (represented by a 'digging radius') and exploitation (represented by a 'movement strength'), which is dynamically adjusted based on the convergence rate of the population. This paper presents the theoretical framework and operational principles of SCIMO, outlining its key components and providing a foundational understanding for potential future implementations and applications.
